# Gaudi Design System (@gaudi/design-system)

> A curated React design system for blogs and applications, with shared foundations, rich components, and reusable interface patterns. React 19 source components with Tailwind CSS v4, semantic tokens, accessibility, RTL-aware layout and copy-in blocks. Version 0.1.7.

Install from GitHub: `pnpm add github:g-udi/design-system`. Import from `@gaudi/design-system` (root), category entries (`/core`, `/chat`, `/charts`, `/animations`, `/blocks`, `/hooks`, `/mdx`, `/post`, `/layout`) or owner leaf entries such as `@gaudi/design-system/core/Button`. Load `@gaudi/design-system/global.css` once (or `styles.css` when the app owns its Tailwind entry). In Next.js add `transpilePackages: ['@gaudi/design-system']`. Peers: react, react-dom, next, next-themes, tailwindcss; optional recharts (charts) and @xyflow/react (Flow). A JS Tailwind preset is available at `@gaudi/design-system/tailwind-preset`.

Generated by `pnpm ai:build` from component docs, READMEs, stories and the catalogue. Links are relative to the repository root.

# Accordion

> Core/Accordion · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Accordion`

Rich disclosure for FAQs, settings, member directories, nested help, and guided setup. Eleven patterns use Gaudi tokens, icons, avatars, cards, and pills.

## Import

```js
import Accordion from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Accordion';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Accordion`, `AccordionContent`, `AccordionGroup`, `AccordionItem`, `AccordionRoot`, `AccordionTrigger`, `Collapsible`, `CollapsibleContent`, `CollapsibleTrigger`, `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Array<{ value, title, content, disabled?, leading?, description?, badge?, indicator?, indicatorPosition?, headingLevel?, forceMount?, className?, triggerClassName?, contentClassName? }>` | `[]` | no | Convenience group items. Rich slots accept React nodes. |
| `type` | `single \| multiple` | `single` | no | Allow one or several expanded panels. |
| `variant` | `outline \| flush \| separated \| solid \| framed` | `outline` | no | Shared border, quiet dividers, individual borders, muted items, or an inset frame. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| string[] \| null` | `first enabled item (group)` | no | Initial uncontrolled state. Use null or [] to start collapsed. |
| `value` | `string \| string[] \| undefined` | — | no | Controlled state. Single close emits undefined; multiple close emits an array. |
| `onValueChange` | `function` | — | no | Controlled state. Single close emits undefined; multiple close emits an array. |
| `collapsible` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Allow the current single item to close. Set false to keep the active item expanded. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Disable all root items or one AccordionItem. |
| `indicator` | `chevron \| plus-minus \| arrow \| ReactNode \| ({isOpen}) => ReactNode \| null` | `chevron` | no | Root default with per-trigger or per-item overrides. |
| `indicatorPosition` | `start \| end` | `end` | no | Logical indicator position, including RTL. |
| `highlight` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Use the accent surface on expanded headers. |
| `headingLevel` | `2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `3` | no | Heading level; override per item or trigger. |
| `leading / description / badge` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Noninteractive slots on AccordionTrigger or group items. |
| `forceMount` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Retain closed panel children, hidden and inert, to preserve form drafts. |
| `children` | `ReactNode \| render function` | — | no | AccordionRoot compound children or the legacy state render function. |
| `className / ref / DOM attributes` | `native props` | — | no | Root, item, and trigger forward native props; content className styles its padded inner body. |

## Variants

- `type`: `single`, `multiple`
- `variant`: `outline`, `flush`, `separated`, `solid`, `framed`
- `indicatorPosition`: `start`, `end`
- `headingLevel`: `2`, `3`, `4`, `5`, `6`

## Usage

```jsx
import { AccordionGroup } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<AccordionGroup
  items={[
    { value: 'usage', title: 'When should I use it?', content: 'Use accordions for compact progressive disclosure.' },
  ]}
/>
```

## Accessibility

Radix-backed native buttons expose expanded state and labelled panels. Arrow Up/Down and Home/End navigate enabled headers within the current accordion; Enter/Space toggle. Disabled items are skipped. Headings default to h3 and can follow the document hierarchy. Closed panels are inert during animation and unmounted afterward; forceMount retains hidden, inert content. Reduced motion is respected.

## Notes

- `Accordion` and `AccordionGroup` from the package root are the items-based convenience API. Use `AccordionRoot` for compound composition. The named `Accordion` from the `core/Accordion` subpath remains the compound root for compatibility.
- Give every item a stable, unique, non-empty string value. Single mode uses a string; multiple mode uses an array. An explicit undefined controlled value collapses every panel.
- The group opens the first enabled item by default. Use `defaultValue={null}` for a collapsed single group or `defaultValue={[]}` in multiple mode. AccordionRoot starts closed unless a default is supplied.
- Existing render-function children and explicit `isOpen` / `onClick` composition remain supported. New compound usage manages state and ARIA associations automatically.
- Leading content and badges must be noninteractive. Put links, inputs, and action buttons inside AccordionContent. Provide an appropriate headingLevel for nested sections.
- forceMount preserves form state but does not omit closed inputs from native form submission. Consumers own persistence, validation, and submission scope.

- Collapsible: Show more details — registry item `@gaudi/collapsible-show-more` (uses `Badge`, `Button`, `Collapsible`, `CollapsibleContent`, `CollapsibleTrigger`, `RegistryIcon`)

## README

Stacked sections whose headers expand and collapse their content. Use it for FAQs, settings groups, and long reference content that readers scan before opening one part. For a single show-more toggle, use `Collapsible`.

```jsx
import { AccordionGroup, Icon, Pill } from '@gaudi/design-system';
import '@gaudi/design-system/global.css';

<AccordionGroup
  variant='separated'
  indicator='plus-minus'
  items={[
    {
      value: 'account',
      title: 'Account settings',
      description: 'Manage your profile and preferences.',
      leading: <Icon name='Settings' decorative />,
      badge: <Pill size='xs' variant='soft'>New</Pill>,
      content: <p>Account settings content.</p>
    }
  ]}
/>
```

### State and variants

- `type`: `single` (default) or `multiple`.
- `value` / `onValueChange`: controlled state. Single close emits `undefined`; multiple changes emit an array. Explicit `value={undefined}` keeps a controlled single root collapsed.
- `defaultValue`: initial uncontrolled state. A group opens the first enabled item by default, including as an array in multiple mode. Pass `null` (single) or `[]` (multiple) to start closed. `AccordionRoot` starts closed by default.
- `collapsible={false}`: keep the current single panel open until another is selected.
- `disabled`: disable all root items; item `disabled` disables a single trigger.
- `variant`: `outline` (default), `flush`, `separated`, `solid`, or `framed`.
- `indicator`: `chevron` (default), `plus-minus`, `arrow`, a React node, `({ isOpen }) => ReactNode`, or `null`. Override on an individual item/trigger.
- `indicatorPosition`: logical `start` or `end` (default). `dir='rtl'` sets both layout and navigation direction.
- `highlight`: accent background for an expanded header.
- `headingLevel`: 2–6; defaults to 3. Override at root, item, or trigger.

Give each item a unique, nonempty string `value`. An item's `title` and `content` accept React nodes. `leading`, `description`, and `badge` enrich the trigger. `className`, `triggerClassName`, and `contentClassName` customize each group item; native props and refs pass through the compound primitives. `AccordionContent` applies `className` to its padded inner body and its remaining native props/ref to the animated region.

### Composition

```jsx
import {
  AccordionRoot, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, AccordionContent, Input
} from '@gaudi/design-system';

<AccordionRoot type='multiple' defaultValue={['profile']}>
  <AccordionItem value='profile'>
    <AccordionTrigger description='Drafts are kept when you close this section.'>
      Profile
    </AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent forceMount>
      <label htmlFor='profile-name'>Display name</label>
      <Input id='profile-name' defaultValue='Amira' />
    </AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</AccordionRoot>
```

The package-root `Accordion` remains an alias for `AccordionGroup`. Use `AccordionRoot` for unambiguous compound composition. The existing named `Accordion` export from `@gaudi/design-system/core/Accordion` remains the compound root. Legacy render-function children receive `{ currentValue, setValue, type }`; explicit `isOpen`, `onClick`, `contentId`, `id`, and `labelledBy` wiring remains supported.

### Accessibility and content lifecycle

Each header is a native button inside a heading, with unique IDs associating the trigger and content. Header descriptions are separate accessible descriptions; decorative icons/avatars do not duplicate names. Choose heading levels to fit the page. Keep header slots noninteractive and place links, buttons, and form controls inside content.

Tab follows the normal document order. Enter/Space toggles a header. Arrow Up/Down navigates enabled headers with wrapping; Home/End moves to the first/last. Nested groups maintain separate navigation. Disabled items are skipped. Open/close height and indicator motion respects reduced-motion preferences.

Closed content is inert during its exit animation, then unmounted. `forceMount` retains content while hiding it visually and from keyboard/screen-reader navigation, preserving form drafts. Hidden retained inputs still participate in native form submission: applications own validation and submission scope. Avoid unnecessary region proliferation in very large multiple-open groups; set `role={undefined}` on compound content when appropriate.

# AspectRatio

> Core/AspectRatio · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/AspectRatio`

Keep media at a stable aspect ratio as its container resizes.

## Import

```js
import { AspectRatio } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/AspectRatio';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `AspectRatio`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ratio` | `number` | `1` | no | Width divided by height; use 16 / 9 for landscape media. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Content composed from the exported parts. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { AspectRatio } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/AspectRatio';

<AspectRatio ratio={16 / 9}>
  <img src={cover.src} alt={cover.alt} className='h-full w-full object-cover' />
</AspectRatio>
```

## Accessibility

Supply alternative text for images and accessible names for embedded media.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-aspectratio--playground`)

Curated patterns:

- Common ratios — registry item `@gaudi/aspect-ratio-common-ratios` (uses `AspectRatio`)

## README

Keeps media at a fixed width-to-height ratio as its container resizes, so images and video do not shift the layout while they load.

```jsx
import { AspectRatio } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<AspectRatio ratio={16 / 9} className='overflow-hidden rounded-lg border'>
  <img src='/images/art/0.svg' alt='' className='size-full object-cover' />
</AspectRatio>
```

`ratio` is width divided by height (default `1`). Give related media, such as thumbnails in one row, the same ratio.

# Attachment

> Core/Attachment · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Attachment`

File attachments with metadata, previews, actions and upload states.

## Import

```js
import { Attachment } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Attachment';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Attachment`, `AttachmentAction`, `AttachmentActions`, `AttachmentContent`, `AttachmentDescription`, `AttachmentGroup`, `AttachmentMedia`, `AttachmentTitle`, `AttachmentTrigger`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | `idle \| uploading \| processing \| done \| error` | `done` | no | State exposed to the attachment styling. |
| `size` | `default \| sm \| xs` | `default` | no | Density of the attachment row. |
| `orientation` | `horizontal \| vertical` | `horizontal` | no | Arrangement of media, details and actions. |
| `AttachmentMedia.variant` | `icon \| image` | `automatic with file, otherwise icon` | no | Presentation of the media slot; icon suppresses a supplied thumbnail. |
| `AttachmentMedia.file` | `{ name, type?, mediaType?, fileType?, kind?, previewUrl? }` | — | no | Shared file-type icons for image, audio, video, document, code, spreadsheet, archive and link. A host-provided thumbnail falls back to its type icon if loading fails; explicit children take precedence. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Content composed from the exported parts. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `state`: `idle`, `uploading`, `processing`, `done`, `error`
- `size`: `default`, `sm`, `xs`
- `orientation`: `horizontal`, `vertical`

## Usage

```jsx
import { Attachment, AttachmentMedia, AttachmentContent, AttachmentTitle, AttachmentDescription } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Attachment';

const file = { name: 'report.pdf', type: 'application/pdf', description: 'PDF · ready to send' };

<Attachment>
  <AttachmentMedia file={file} />
  <AttachmentContent>
    <AttachmentTitle>{file.name}</AttachmentTitle>
    <AttachmentDescription>{file.description}</AttachmentDescription>
  </AttachmentContent>
</Attachment>
```

## Accessibility

Use descriptive filenames and name every icon action. Keep retry and remove actions available when an upload fails.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-attachment--playground`)
- Mixed media · detailed rows (Storybook `core-attachment--mixed-media`)
- Mixed media · wrapping pills (Storybook `core-attachment--compact-pills`)
- Images · thumbnail grid (Storybook `core-attachment--image-grid`)

Curated patterns:

- Files in an assistant reply — registry item `@gaudi/attachment-assistant-reply` (uses `Attachment`, `AttachmentAction`, `AttachmentActions`, `AttachmentContent`, `AttachmentDescription`, `AttachmentGroup`, `AttachmentMedia`, `AttachmentTitle`, `RegistryIcon`)
- Composer tray with removable files — registry item `@gaudi/attachment-composer-tray` (uses `Attachment`, `AttachmentAction`, `AttachmentActions`, `AttachmentContent`, `AttachmentGroup`, `AttachmentMedia`, `AttachmentTitle`, `FieldLabelPrimitive`, `FieldRoot`, `InputGroup`, `InputGroupAddon`, `InputGroupButton`, `InputGroupText`, `InputGroupTextarea`, `RegistryIcon`)
- File picker that fills a tray — registry item `@gaudi/attachment-file-picker` (uses `Attachment`, `AttachmentAction`, `AttachmentActions`, `AttachmentContent`, `AttachmentDescription`, `AttachmentMedia`, `AttachmentTitle`, `AttachmentTrigger`, `RegistryIcon`, `formatBytes`, `useFileUpload`)
- Image thumbnail strip — registry item `@gaudi/attachment-thumbnail-strip` (uses `Attachment`, `AttachmentContent`, `AttachmentGroup`, `AttachmentMedia`, `AttachmentTitle`, `AttachmentTrigger`)

## README

A file row, compact pill or image tile with media, a name, a status line and actions. Use the same parts for images, documents, audio, video, links, source files and spreadsheets in composer trays, upload queues and messages. `state` drives the idle, uploading, processing, done and error styling.

### Usage

```jsx
import { Attachment, AttachmentAction, AttachmentActions, AttachmentContent, AttachmentDescription, AttachmentMedia, AttachmentTitle, AttachmentTrigger } from '@gaudi/design-system';
import { RegistryIcon } from '@gaudi/design-system/icons';

const file = { id: 'cover', name: 'campaign-cover.jpg', type: 'image/jpeg', previewUrl: '/uploads/campaign-cover.jpg' };

<Attachment>
  <AttachmentMedia file={file} />
  <AttachmentContent>
    <AttachmentTitle title={file.name}>{file.name}</AttachmentTitle>
    <AttachmentDescription>Image · ready to send</AttachmentDescription>
  </AttachmentContent>
  <AttachmentTrigger aria-label={`Preview ${file.name}`} onClick={() => openPreview(file)} />
  <AttachmentActions>
    <AttachmentAction aria-label={`Remove ${file.name}`} onClick={() => remove(file.id)}><RegistryIcon lucide='X' /></AttachmentAction>
  </AttachmentActions>
</Attachment>
```

The host supplies `previewUrl` for a thumbnail or video poster. It is an image source, not a playable media URL. Without it, `AttachmentMedia` chooses an icon from the MIME type or filename extension; `kind: 'link'` chooses a globe. A failed thumbnail falls back to the file icon. File content, image previews, audio/video playback and download destinations stay with the host.

Explicit children still support custom artwork, progress or state feedback:

```jsx
<AttachmentMedia><RegistryIcon lucide='TriangleAlert' /></AttachmentMedia>
<AttachmentMedia file={file} variant='icon' />
```

The second form deliberately shows the file icon even when a preview URL exists.

### Parts

| Part | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `Attachment` | `state`, `size` (default, sm, xs) and `orientation` (horizontal, vertical). |
| `AttachmentMedia` | Optional `file={{ name, type?, mediaType?, kind?, previewUrl? }}` provides a file icon or supplied thumbnail. MIME type takes precedence over the filename extension; `kind='link'` identifies links. Explicit children take precedence over automatic media. `variant='icon'` suppresses the thumbnail; `variant='image'` supports composed image children. |
| `AttachmentTitle`, `AttachmentDescription` | File name and status line; both truncate. |
| `AttachmentActions`, `AttachmentAction` | Icon buttons built on Button (`size='icon-xs'`, ghost by default). |
| `AttachmentTrigger` | A full-card button or link, for selectable tiles. |
| `AttachmentGroup` | A horizontally scrolling strip. |

### Layouts and examples

- [Mixed media · detailed rows](?path=/story/core-attachment--mixed-media) places full-width Attachment rows in a labelled list. It includes a local image, PDF, audio, video, a supplied poster, a link, code and a spreadsheet, with selection, removal, reset and failed-thumbnail recovery.
- [Mixed media · wrapping pills](?path=/story/core-attachment--compact-pills) uses `size='xs'` inside a `flex flex-wrap` list for compact inline attachments. Each pill stays within its parent width and retains its own remove action.
- [Images · thumbnail grid](?path=/story/core-attachment--image-grid) uses `orientation='vertical'` inside a two-column grid that expands to three columns at `sm`. Selecting a tile displays its local image preview.

Use a labelled `ul` with one `li` per attachment for wrapping pills, grids or detailed lists. `AttachmentGroup` remains useful when horizontal scrolling is intentional. The examples reuse local artwork; audio, video, document and link entries are explicitly sample metadata with no fake player or download destination.

### Accessibility

Name every icon-only action after its file ("Remove report.pdf") so a list of buttons stays distinguishable. Keep `AttachmentTrigger` and `AttachmentActions` as siblings so the full-card action never nests a remove button. The filename names the automatic decorative media; a full preview needs descriptive alternative text. Keep focus on an available control after removal, and announce selection or attachment-count changes with a concise status.

# Avatar

> Core/Avatar · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Avatar`

Profile images, resilient initials, presence, verification, account menus and collaborator groups. The existing Avatar API and curated patterns share the same image and fallback primitives.

## Import

```js
import Avatar from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Avatar';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Avatar`, `AvatarBadge`, `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarGroup`, `AvatarGroupCount`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarRoot`, `avatarVariants`, `default`, `getAvatarInitials`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | — | no | Remote, local or data image source; failed and pending images show the fallback. |
| `name / label` | `string` | — | no | Name generates Unicode initials; label preserves explicit legacy initials. |
| `alt` | `string` | — | no | Accessible identity override; an empty string is decorative. |
| `fallback` | `ReactNode \| boolean` | `initials` | no | Custom artwork or text; true shows the guest silhouette. |
| `size` | `2xs \| xs \| sm \| md \| lg \| xl` | `md` | no | Six sizes; existing xs through lg dimensions are preserved. |
| `shape` | `circle \| square \| tile` | `square` | no | Identity crop and background treatment. |
| `surface` | `solid \| tinted \| plain \| bare` | `solid` | no | Identity crop and background treatment. |
| `indicator` | `{ label, tone?, icon?, position? }` | — | no | Host-provided presence or verification; positions follow reading direction. |
| `imageProps` | `object` | — | no | Image attributes and per-layer appearance. |
| `imageClassName` | `string` | — | no | Image attributes and per-layer appearance. |
| `fallbackClassName` | `string` | — | no | Image attributes and per-layer appearance. |
| `tone` | `gray \| neutral \| blue \| teal \| green \| amber \| yellow \| red \| rose \| indigo` | `gray` | no | Fallback colour family. |
| `grayscale` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Desaturates the image. |
| `onLoadingStatusChange` | `(status) => void` | — | no | Receives loading, loaded or error; source changes recover automatically. |
| `AvatarGroup` | `avatars, max, size, shape, label, renderAvatar, renderOverflow` | — | no | Accepts data-driven identities or existing compound children. |

## Variants

- `size`: `2xs`, `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`
- `shape`: `circle`, `square`, `tile`
- `surface`: `solid`, `tinted`, `plain`, `bare`
- `tone`: `gray`, `neutral`, `blue`, `teal`, `green`, `amber`, `yellow`, `red`, `rose`, `indigo`

## Usage

```jsx
import { Avatar } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Avatar name='Mei Castellanos' src='/avatars/person-20.svg' shape='circle' indicator={{ label: 'Online', tone: 'success' }} />
```

## Accessibility

A named Avatar exposes one image label, including host-provided presence. Use alt="" beside visible identity text. Wrap interactive avatars in Button, Tooltip or DropdownMenu; status badges never infer presence from image loading.

## Related

`blocks-profile`, `core-button`, `core-tooltip`, `core-dropdownmenu`, `mdx-image`

## README

A person, workspace or source shown as a photo, initials or an icon, with an optional presence badge. `Avatar` and `AvatarGroup` are built on the `AvatarRoot`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarFallback` and `AvatarBadge` parts.

Image examples use Gaudi's own illustrated avatars bundled with Storybook (`/avatars/person-20.svg`, generated deterministically from a seed) with fictional demo identities, so examples never load images from the network. The same avatars appear in sizes, account menus, presence badges, reviewer rosters and other component examples. Initials, color surfaces, workspace marks and broken-image states remain explicit fallback demonstrations. These URLs are fixture data; applications supply their own `src`. See the [portrait reference](../../../../.storybook/public/avatars/README.md).

```jsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Avatar
  name='Mei Castellanos'
  src={person.photoUrl}
  shape='circle'
  indicator={{ label: 'Online', tone: 'success' }}
/>

<AvatarGroup avatars={people} max={3} size='md' label='Review team' />
```

| Prop | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `src` | Remote, local or data image URL. Pending, missing and failed images show fallback content; changing the source resets loading. |
| `name` / `label` | Name generates Unicode-aware initials from the first and last words; a single word uses up to two characters. The 16px `2xs` size shows only the first initial so it stays legible at the `text-xs` step. Label preserves explicitly supplied initials. |
| `alt` | Overrides the accessible identity; `alt=''` makes the avatar decorative beside visible text. |
| `fallback` | Custom text or noninteractive artwork; `true` renders the guest silhouette. Empty names show `?`. |
| `size` | `2xs`, `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`: 16, 20, 32, 40, 56 and 80px. Existing sizes retain their dimensions. |
| `shape` | `square` (default), `circle`, `tile`. Image and fallback inherit the same shape. |
| `surface` | `solid` (default, selected tone), `tinted`, `plain` or `bare`. Plain/bare default to `contain`; solid/tinted use `cover`. |
| `tone` | Existing gray, neutral, blue, teal, green, amber, yellow, red, rose and indigo colors. |
| `fit` / `grayscale` | Image crop (`cover` or `contain`) and optional grayscale treatment. |
| `indicator` | `{ label, tone?, icon?, position?, className? }`. Label is required; status is always supplied by the application. |
| `children` | Additional noninteractive `AvatarBadge` content. Provide its meaning in the root `aria-label`. |
| `onLoadingStatusChange` | Receives `loading`, `loaded` or `error` for host-owned feedback. |
| `imageProps`, `imageClassName`, `fallbackClassName` | Native image attributes and per-layer appearance. Identity alt text is owned by the root. |
| `ref`, native attributes | Forwarded to the root span. Wrap Avatar in Button, Tooltip or DropdownMenu for interaction. |

Indicators support `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `neutral` and `primary`, and `top-start`, `top-end`, `bottom-start`, `bottom-end` positions. Logical positions follow reading direction. Presence remains separate from loading or failure. The face retains its rounded crop while badges remain outside its bounds.

### Groups

`AvatarGroup` continues to accept compound children. Pass `avatars` for data-driven composition: each entry contains a unique stable `id` plus Avatar props. `max` defaults to four; positive fractions round down to at least one, and zero/negative/non-finite values show all. Empty lists have no overflow count. Supply surrounding empty-state copy where appropriate.

`size`, `shape` and `label` apply to the group. `renderAvatar(avatar, person)` and `renderOverflow(count, overflow)` wrap the supplied elements with existing buttons, tooltips or dialogs. `formatOverflow(count)` supplies translated overflow text. Large groups scroll within their own bounds. Compound APIs remain available as `AvatarRoot`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarBadge` and `AvatarGroupCount` from this owner and the package root.

# Banner

> Core/Banner · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Banner`

Banner renders a compact announcement strip.

## Import

```js
import Banner from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Banner';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Alert`, `AlertAction`, `AlertActionPrimitive`, `AlertDescription`, `AlertDescriptionPrimitive`, `AlertRoot`, `AlertTitle`, `AlertTitlePrimitive`, `bannerTones`, `bannerVariants`, `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Optional bold leading text. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Announcement body copy. |
| `href` | `string` | — | no | Turns the banner copy into a navigation link. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `Rendered content` | no | Optional accessible-name override for linked banners. |
| `size` | `xs \| sm \| md \| lg` | `md` | no | Controls vertical and horizontal padding. |
| `tone` | `neutral \| accent \| info \| success \| warning \| danger \| attention \| discovery` | `neutral` | no | Semantic tone. Hue names (blue, green, amber…) still resolve to these. |
| `variant` | `solid \| soft \| outline` | `soft` | no | Visual treatment. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Root class override. |
| `classNames` | `{ root, body, action }` | — | no | Slot-level class overrides. |

## Variants

- `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`
- `tone`: `neutral`, `accent`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `attention`, `discovery`
- `variant`: `solid`, `soft`, `outline`

## Usage

```jsx
import { Banner } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Banner title='Now published' href='/blog'>
  New essays and project notes are available.
</Banner>
```

## Accessibility

Static banners use status semantics. Linked banners derive their accessible name from the rendered title and body, including rich content; ariaLabel provides an explicit override.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-banner--playground`)
- Tones and variants (Storybook `core-banner--tones-and-variants`)

Curated patterns:

- Alert: Dismissible notices — registry item `@gaudi/alert-dismissible` (uses `Alert`, `AlertAction`, `AlertDescription`, `AlertTitle`, `Button`, `Frame`, `FramePanel`, `RegistryIcon`)
- Alert: Message notification — registry item `@gaudi/alert-message-notice` (uses `Alert`, `AlertAction`, `AlertDescription`, `AlertTitle`, `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarRoot`, `Button`, `Frame`, `FramePanel`)
- Alert: Actions and rich content — registry item `@gaudi/alert-rich-actions` (uses `Alert`, `AlertAction`, `AlertDescription`, `AlertTitle`, `Button`, `RegistryIcon`)
- Alert: Service status summary — registry item `@gaudi/alert-service-status` (uses `Alert`, `AlertAction`, `AlertDescription`, `AlertTitle`, `Button`, `Frame`, `FramePanel`, `RegistryIcon`)
- Alert: Variants — registry item `@gaudi/alert-variants` (uses `Alert`, `AlertDescription`, `AlertTitle`, `RegistryIcon`)

## README

A banner is a full-width strip for a site-wide message: a release, maintenance, or a billing problem. For a message inside the page, next to the content it is about, compose `Alert`.

```jsx
import { Banner } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Banner title='Gaudi 2.0 is out' href='/changelog' tone='accent' variant='solid'>
  New tokens and a faster docs site.
</Banner>
```

- `tone` carries meaning (`neutral`, `accent`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `attention`, `discovery`); older hue names still work.
- `variant`: `solid` for the one announcement that matters most, `soft` or `outline` for routine notices. `size` sets the padding.
- With `href` the whole message is one link; without it the banner is announced as a status.

### Alert

`Alert`, `AlertTitle`, `AlertDescription` and `AlertAction` build an inline message with an icon, text and actions. `variant` is `default`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive` or `invert`. `AlertRoot` and the `*Primitive` names are aliases of the same parts.

# Breadcrumb

> Core/Breadcrumb · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Breadcrumb`

Breadcrumb renders hierarchical page trails for navigation context.

## Import

```js
import Breadcrumb from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Breadcrumb';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Breadcrumb`, `BreadcrumbEllipsis`, `BreadcrumbEllipsisPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbItem`, `BreadcrumbItemPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbLink`, `BreadcrumbLinkPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbList`, `BreadcrumbListPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbPage`, `BreadcrumbPagePrimitive`, `BreadcrumbRoot`, `BreadcrumbSeparator`, `BreadcrumbSeparatorPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbTrail`, `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Array<{ href, label, current }>` | `[]` | no | Convenience API for a complete breadcrumb trail. |
| `label` | `string` | `Breadcrumb` | no | Accessible name for the nav landmark. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Root or slot class override depending on the exported primitive. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Composition API for custom Breadcrumb/List/Item/Link/Page layouts. |
| `href` | `string` | — | no | Link target for ancestor pages. |
| `current` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Marks the active page with aria-current. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { BreadcrumbTrail } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<BreadcrumbTrail
  items={[
    { href: '/', label: 'Home' },
    { href: '/blog', label: 'Blog' },
    { current: true, label: 'Design Systems' },
  ]}
/>
```

## Accessibility

Breadcrumb renders a nav landmark, ordered list, real links for ancestors, and aria-current on the current page.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-breadcrumb--playground`)

Curated patterns:

- Collapsed path with menu — registry item `@gaudi/breadcrumb-collapsed-path` (uses `BreadcrumbEllipsisPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbItemPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbLinkPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbListPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbPagePrimitive`, `BreadcrumbRoot`, `BreadcrumbSeparatorPrimitive`, `Button`, `DropdownMenuContent`, `DropdownMenuItemPrimitive`, `DropdownMenuRoot`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`)
- Contained and button styles — registry item `@gaudi/breadcrumb-contained-buttons` (uses `BreadcrumbItemPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbLinkPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbListPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbPagePrimitive`, `BreadcrumbRoot`, `BreadcrumbSeparatorPrimitive`, `Button`, `CardContent`, `CardRoot`, `Frame`, `FramePanel`, `RegistryIcon`)
- Icons, badges and avatars — registry item `@gaudi/breadcrumb-icons-avatars` (uses `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarRoot`, `Badge`, `BreadcrumbItemPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbLinkPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbListPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbPagePrimitive`, `BreadcrumbRoot`, `BreadcrumbSeparatorPrimitive`, `Button`, `RegistryIcon`)
- Separators — registry item `@gaudi/breadcrumb-separators` (uses `BreadcrumbItemPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbLinkPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbListPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbPagePrimitive`, `BreadcrumbRoot`, `BreadcrumbSeparatorPrimitive`, `RegistryIcon`)
- Workspace, user and document — registry item `@gaudi/breadcrumb-workspace-path` (uses `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarRoot`, `BreadcrumbItemPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbLinkPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbListPrimitive`, `BreadcrumbPagePrimitive`, `BreadcrumbRoot`, `BreadcrumbSeparatorPrimitive`, `Frame`, `FramePanel`, `RegistryIcon`)

## Related

`core-item`, `core-link`

## README

A trail of links from the site root to the current page. Use it on nested pages (docs, categories, settings) so readers can see where they are and step back up a level.

```jsx
import { BreadcrumbTrail } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<BreadcrumbTrail
  items={[
    { href: '/', label: 'Home' },
    { href: '/blog', label: 'Blog' },
    { label: 'Design systems' }
  ]}
/>
```

`BreadcrumbTrail` (the default export) renders a labelled `nav`, an ordered list, router-aware links for ancestors and `aria-current="page"` on the last item (or the item marked `current`). `label` names the landmark.

For icons, collapsed paths or menus in the trail, compose the parts: `Breadcrumb`, `BreadcrumbList`, `BreadcrumbItem`, `BreadcrumbLink`, `BreadcrumbPage`, `BreadcrumbSeparator` and `BreadcrumbEllipsis`. The convenience names are the same parts with a labelled landmark and Gaudi `Link` for internal routes; `BreadcrumbLinkPrimitive` and friends are the raw parts (`asChild` on the link accepts a router link).

# Button

> Core/Button · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Button`

Button renders the Gaudi action and link-button variants.

## Import

```js
import Button from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Button';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `buttonSizes`, `buttonToneAliases`, `buttonTones`, `buttonVariants`, `default`, `variants`

## When to use

- Use `solid` with `accent` for the one primary action in a local group.
- Use `outline` or `soft` with `neutral` for secondary actions that still need a visible target.
- Use `ghost`, `subtle`, or inline Link for quiet navigation and toolbar actions.
- Choose semantic tones by meaning: `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `attention`, `discovery`, or `info`.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Visible button label or content. |
| `variant` | `solid \| soft \| outline \| ghost \| subtle` | `solid` | no | Reusable visual treatment. |
| `size` | `xs \| sm \| md \| lg \| icon \| icon-xs \| icon-sm \| icon-lg` | `md` | no | Compact heights: xs 24px, sm 28px, md/default 32px, lg 36px. Icon sizes match their text-button counterparts. Use matching sizes for controls in the same row. |
| `tone` | `accent \| neutral \| success \| warning \| danger \| attention \| discovery \| info` | `accent (solid, subtle); neutral (soft, outline, ghost)` | no | Semantic meaning for the action. Quiet variants default to neutral so screens do not turn blue. Legacy hue names remain supported as compatibility aliases. |
| `radius` | `sm \| md \| lg \| full` | `md` | no | Legacy aliases use the global --ds-radius setting (4px by default); none stays square where supported. |
| `href` | `string` | — | no | Renders an internal Next link or safe external anchor. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Disables native buttons and removes disabled links from the tab order. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Root class override. |

## Variants

- `variant`: `solid`, `soft`, `outline`, `ghost`, `subtle`
- `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `icon`, `icon-xs`, `icon-sm`, `icon-lg`
- `tone`: `accent`, `neutral`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `attention`, `discovery`, `info`
- `radius`: `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `full`

## Usage

```jsx
import { Button } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Button variant='solid' tone='accent' size='md'>Read article</Button>
```

## Accessibility

Button renders native buttons for actions and links for navigation. Disabled link variants are removed from tab order.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-button--playground`)
- Variants, tones and sizes (Storybook `core-button--variants`)
- Links and disabled (Storybook `core-button--states`)

Curated patterns:

- Async loading and success — registry item `@gaudi/button-async-success` (uses `Button`, `LoaderRoot`, `RegistryIcon`)
- Avatar and two-line content — registry item `@gaudi/button-avatar-two-line` (uses `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarRoot`, `Button`, `RegistryIcon`)
- Copy with feedback — registry item `@gaudi/button-copy-feedback` (uses `Button`, `RegistryIcon`, `TooltipContent`, `TooltipProvider`, `TooltipRoot`, `TooltipTrigger`, `useCopyToClipboard`)
- Counts, badges and shortcuts — registry item `@gaudi/button-counts-shortcuts` (uses `Badge`, `Button`, `KbdGroup`, `KbdRoot`, `RegistryIcon`, `TooltipContent`, `TooltipProvider`, `TooltipRoot`, `TooltipTrigger`)
- Icons, loading and links — registry item `@gaudi/button-icons-loading` (uses `Button`, `LoaderRoot`, `RegistryIcon`)
- Social sign-in — registry item `@gaudi/button-social-sign-in` (uses `Button`, `RegistryIcon`)
- Toggling icon and label — registry item `@gaudi/button-toggling-label` (uses `Button`, `RegistryIcon`, `cn`)

## Related

`core-link`, `core-icon`

## README

A button starts an action: submit a form, save a draft, open a dialog. Pass `href` to get a link that looks like a button.

```jsx
import { Button } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Button variant='outline' tone='neutral'>Cancel</Button>
<Button>Publish article</Button>
```

- `variant` sets the hierarchy: `solid` for the one primary action, `outline` or `soft` for supporting actions, `ghost` and `subtle` for low-emphasis ones.
- `tone` carries meaning (`accent`, `neutral`, `danger`, `success`, `warning`, `info`, `attention`, `discovery`). Pick it by intent, not colour.
- Sizes share heights with inputs and selects: `xs` 24px, `sm` 28px, `md` 32px, `lg` 36px. Icon-only buttons use `icon-xs`, `icon-sm`, `icon`, `icon-lg` and need an `aria-label`.
- `href` renders an internal link, or a new-tab anchor for external URLs. `disabled` works on both buttons and links.
- `asChild` passes the button styles to your own element, such as a router link.

## Related

`core-togglegroup`, `core-direction`

## README

A button group joins related buttons into one control: a toolbar, a split button, a pager, or an input with its action.

```jsx
import { Button, ButtonGroup, ButtonGroupSeparator } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<ButtonGroup aria-label='Reply'>
  <Button>Reply all</Button>
  <ButtonGroupSeparator />
  <Button size='icon' aria-label='More reply options'>…</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

- Give each group an `aria-label` so assistive tech announces what the buttons do together.
- `orientation='vertical'` stacks the buttons; turn any `ButtonGroupSeparator` to `horizontal` with it.
- `ButtonGroupText` holds a label or value (such as "Page 2 of 26") inside the group.
- Groups can hold inputs and selects, and can nest to keep a small gap between sets.

- Date selector: Translated, in a dialog — registry item `@gaudi/date-selector-translated-dialog` (uses `Button`, `DEFAULT_DATE_SELECTOR_I18N`, `DateSelector`, `DialogClosePrimitive`, `DialogContent`, `DialogFooter`, `DialogHeader`, `DialogRoot`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogTrigger`, `DropdownMenuContent`, `DropdownMenuItemPrimitive`, `DropdownMenuRoot`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`, `RegistryIcon`, `formatDateValue`)

## README

A month grid for picking one date, several dates or a range. Use it inline or inside a Popover for a date field; use `DateSelector` when people filter by day, month, quarter, half-year or year.

```jsx
import { Calendar } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Calendar mode='range' selected={range} onSelect={setRange} numberOfMonths={2} disabled={{ before: new Date() }} />
```

- `mode` is `single`, `multiple` or `range`. `disabled` takes dates, ranges or matchers, and `footer` shows a summary under the grid.
- `captionLayout` switches the header between a label and month or year dropdowns; `showOutsideDays`, `showWeekNumber` and `numberOfMonths` shape the grid.
- Day cells are squares of `--cell-size` (32px, 40px on touch screens). Set the variable on the calendar to fit custom day content; the month never stretches to fill its container.
- `CalendarDayButton` is the default day cell, for custom `components.DayButton` renderers.

### DateSelector

`DateSelector` combines an is/before/after/between filter, period tabs and a calendar or period grid, with optional typed input. Pass `value` / `onChange` and translate every string with `i18n`.

The period grid shows `yearRange` years (10 by default) around `baseYear`, or the current year when omitted. Pass both `minYear` and `maxYear` to supply an explicit inclusive year window.

An empty `value` clears a previous selection, including a cancelled draft in an overlay that is still closing. Hosts keep committed and draft values separate when using Apply and Cancel.

### Accessibility

Days are buttons in a grid with the full date as their name. Arrow keys move by day and week, Page Up and Page Down by month, and disabled days cannot be picked.

### Implementation ownership

`Calendar` owns the DayPicker bridge. DateSelector formatting, labels, state and context are separate from its private day/period views and controls. All supported exports remain available from the Calendar entry.

# Card

> Core/Card · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Card`

Card frames reusable content with title, subtitle, and optional children.

## Import

```js
import Card from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Card';
```

## When to use

- Use Card to frame one reusable content unit, not as page scaffolding.
- Put real links and buttons inside the card instead of turning the whole surface into a fake control.
- Avoid nested cards; separate sections with spacing or a table/list pattern instead.

| `radius` | `none \| sm \| md \| lg` | `md` | no | Legacy aliases use the global --ds-radius setting (4px by default); none stays square where supported. |
| `interactive` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Adds hover elevation for cards containing a real link or button. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Root class override. |

## Variants

- `variant`: `elevated`, `outline`, `soft`, `flat`
- `padding`: `none`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`

## Usage

```jsx
import { Card } from '@gaudi/design-system';
```

## Accessibility

Card is a structural container. Put links or buttons inside it rather than making the whole card a fake control.

## README

A bordered surface that frames one unit of content: an article teaser, a metric, a settings group. Use it when content needs a visible boundary; use spacing or a list instead for page structure.

```jsx
import { Card } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Card title='Weekly readers' subtitle='Last 7 days' variant='outline' padding='sm'>
  <p>12.4k</p>
</Card>
```

- `variant`: `elevated` (default), `outline`, `soft`, or `flat`. `padding`: `none`, `sm`, `md` (default), `lg`. `radius`: `none`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`.
- `title`, `subtitle`, and `titleLevel` (2-6, default 3) render the heading and description with the `CardTitle` and `CardDescription` parts.
- `interactive` adds hover elevation. Keep real links and buttons inside the card rather than making the whole surface clickable.

### Parts

For headers with actions or a footer, compose `CardRoot`, `CardHeader`, `CardTitle`, `CardDescription`, `CardAction`, `CardContent`, and `CardFooter`. `CardTitle` and `CardDescription` accept `as` to render a heading or paragraph.

`Frame`, `FramePanel`, `FrameHeader`, `FrameTitle`, `FrameDescription`, and `FrameFooter` build a tinted tray that holds one or more panels, such as stacked settings sections.

`Card` and `CardRoot` use the same surface and variant implementation. `Card` supplies a padded title/body composition; `CardRoot` defaults to section spacing for `CardHeader`, `CardContent`, and `CardFooter`. Zero-valued titles and descriptions are preserved.

# Carousel

> Core/Carousel · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Carousel`

Carousel renders standard feature slides and editorial card rails.

## Import

```js
import Carousel from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Carousel';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `CarouselContent`, `CarouselItem`, `CarouselNext`, `CarouselPrevious`, `CarouselRoot`, `carouselCardVariants`, `carouselSlideVariants`, `carouselVariants`, `default`, `useCarousel`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Array<{ id, title, description, eyebrow, image, alt, href, action, content }>` | `[]` | no | Slide data. Standard uses the active item; apple renders the horizontal rail. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `Carousel` | no | Accessible name for the carousel region. |
| `variant` | `standard \| rail \| apple` | `standard` | no | Slide format. Use rail for editorial card rails; apple remains a legacy alias. |
| `size` | `sm \| md \| lg` | `md` | no | Controls max width and slide/card height. |
| `radius` | `none \| sm \| md \| lg` | `lg` | no | Legacy aliases use the global --ds-radius setting; none keeps square corners. |
| `controls` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Shows previous and next buttons. |
| `loop` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Wraps previous/next navigation. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Root class override. |
| `classNames` | `{ root, header, viewport, track, slide, card, image, content, eyebrow, title, description, action, controls, control, indicators, indicator, dialog, overlay }` | — | no | Slot-level overrides for visual composition. |

## Variants

- `variant`: `standard`, `rail`, `apple`
- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg`
- `radius`: `none`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`

## Usage

```jsx
import { Carousel } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Carousel
  ariaLabel='Featured articles'
  items={[
    { title: 'Design systems keep editorial rhythm predictable', eyebrow: 'Design Systems', description: 'A focused carousel item.', href: '/blog' },
  ]}
/>
```

## Accessibility

Carousel exposes a labelled carousel region, native previous/next buttons, aria-live status updates, keyboard arrow support, and named indicators.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-carousel--playground`)
- Editorial Rail (Storybook `core-carousel--editorial-rail`)

Curated patterns:

- Autoplay — registry item `@gaudi/carousel-autoplay` (uses `Button`, `CardRoot`, `CarouselContent`, `CarouselItem`, `CarouselNext`, `CarouselPrevious`, `CarouselRoot`, `usePrefersReducedMotion`)
- Content overlays with dots — registry item `@gaudi/carousel-content-overlays` (uses `CardRoot`, `CarouselContent`, `CarouselItem`, `CarouselNext`, `CarouselPrevious`, `CarouselRoot`, `cn`)
- Layout options — registry item `@gaudi/carousel-layouts` (uses `CardRoot`, `CarouselContent`, `CarouselItem`, `CarouselNext`, `CarouselPrevious`, `CarouselRoot`, `Label`, `SwitchRoot`, `cn`)
- Thumbnail navigation — registry item `@gaudi/carousel-thumbnails` (uses `CarouselContent`, `CarouselItem`, `CarouselRoot`, `Label`, `SwitchRoot`, `cn`)

## README

Shows one item at a time, or a scrolling rail of cards, with previous and next buttons, dot indicators, and arrow-key navigation. Use it for featured content that readers browse in order; use a grid when every item should be visible at once.

```jsx
import { Carousel } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Carousel
  ariaLabel='Featured articles'
  loop
  items={[
    { id: 'graphs', title: 'An Introduction to Knowledge Graphs', eyebrow: 'Knowledge Graphs', image: '/images/art/2.svg', href: '/blog', action: 'Read article' }
  ]}
/>
```

- `variant='standard'` shows one slide with its call to action. `variant='rail'` shows snapping cards; selecting a card opens its `content` in a dialog.
- `loop` wraps navigation at the ends. `controls={false}` hides the previous and next buttons; the indicators stay.
- `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) sets the maximum width and slide height; `radius` sets the corners.

### Parts

`Carousel` is built on the `CarouselRoot`, `CarouselContent`, `CarouselItem`, `CarouselPrevious`, and `CarouselNext` parts. Compose them directly for custom layouts such as thumbnails, multiple slides per view, vertical carousels, or autoplay (pass Embla `opts` and `plugins` to `CarouselRoot`). `useCarousel` exposes the Embla API inside the root.

## Related

`core-select`

## README

Pick a value from a nested tree: a help topic, a folder, a region and its markets. Use it when options only make sense within their parent; use a Select for a flat list.

```jsx
import { Cascader, CascaderTrigger, CascaderValue, CascaderContent, CascaderPanel, CascaderList, CascaderItems } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Cascader items={topics} onValueChange={setTopic}>
  <CascaderTrigger aria-label='Topic'><CascaderValue /></CascaderTrigger>
  <CascaderContent>
    <CascaderPanel>
      <CascaderList><CascaderItems /></CascaderList>
    </CascaderPanel>
  </CascaderContent>
</Cascader>
```

- `items` are `{ value, label, children?, description?, icon?, disabled? }`. `mode` shows the tree as a drill-down list, Miller columns (`CascaderColumns`) or an expanding tree.
- `selectable='any'` lets branches be picked, not only leaves; `multiple` adds checkboxes and chips.
- `inline` renders the panel in the page instead of a popup. `CascaderInput`, `CascaderBreadcrumb`, `CascaderEmpty`, `CascaderStatus` and `CascaderFooter` add search, a path, empty and async states, and footer actions.
- `useCascaderLoader` fetches children on demand; `CascaderVirtualItems` windows long levels.
- `readOnly` preserves selection across active and background columns; `disabled` also disables navigation and dims every row. Both constraints follow prop changes.

### Accessibility

The trigger is a combobox. Up and Down move through a level, the inline-end and inline-start arrow keys open and leave a branch, and Enter picks. A live region announces changes, and every visible or announced string comes from `labels`.

### Implementation ownership

`Cascader` coordinates the controlled state and contexts. Owner-local hooks manage prepared rows, announcements, navigation and the Combobox callback contract. Trigger/chip and panel rendering live in private `components/` modules; the loader remains responsible for asynchronous children.

## README

A box people tick to turn one option on or off, or to pick several options from a list. Use a Switch instead when the change applies straight away.

### Usage

```jsx
import { Checkbox } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Checkbox label='Email me when someone replies' defaultChecked onCheckedChange={setReplies} />;
```

`Checkbox` pairs the box with a clickable label. For descriptions, cards, nested groups or the indeterminate state, compose `CheckboxRoot` with the Field parts (`Field`, `FieldLabel`, `FieldContent`, `FieldDescription`).

### Accessibility

The box is a `checkbox` with `aria-checked` (`mixed` when indeterminate), toggled by Space or a click on its label. A disabled checkbox dims its label too.

# CodeBlock

> Core/CodeBlock · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/CodeBlock`

CodeBlock renders syntax-highlighted source with an optional header, copy button, line numbers, highlighted and focused lines, diffs, folding and line selection.

## Related

`core-tabs`

## README

Render source code, streaming code, diffs or prepared highlighted lines with optional line numbers, wrapping, selection and folding. Compose a header and actions through the same CodeBlock context.

```jsx
import {
  CodeBlock,
  CodeBlockContent,
  CodeBlockCopyButton,
  CodeBlockHeader,
  CodeBlockTitle
} from '@gaudi/design-system/core/CodeBlock';

<CodeBlock code={source} language='javascript' showLineNumbers>
  <CodeBlockHeader>
    <CodeBlockTitle>example.js</CodeBlockTitle>
    <CodeBlockCopyButton />
  </CodeBlockHeader>
  <CodeBlockContent />
</CodeBlock>
```

`highlight={false}` renders plain source immediately. `wrap` / `onWrapChange`, `expanded` / `onExpandedChange`, `selectedLines` / `onSelectedLinesChange`, and `folded` / `onFoldedChange` support host-controlled state. Folding uses source line numbers; supplied `foldRegions` can replace indentation-based discovery. Copy and download actions use the current source.

### Implementation ownership

The root owns document state and highlighting. `CodeBlockContext.jsx` shares that state with private line, surface, header and control modules under `components/`. `codeBlockFolding.js` contains the independent fold model; `CodeBlockHighlight.jsx` owns highlighting and source parsing. Consumers use the public owner entry.

Selectable code uses a single focusable grid of source-line rows. Arrow keys, Home and End move the active line; Space or Enter toggles selection, and Shift extends it. Line actions remain real buttons inside a grid cell so their own Enter/Space behavior is preserved.

`CodeBlockCopyButton` announces copy success and failures in a polite live region. A failed attempt stays available as **Retry copy** until the next successful attempt. Override `labels.copy`, `labels.copied`, `labels.retry`, and `labels.error` for translated feedback; `onCopyError` lets the host react to a blocked clipboard.

# ColorPicker

> Core/ColorPicker · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/ColorPicker`

An inline color canvas with hue, opacity, an eyedropper, and HEX/RGB/HSL/CSS editors.

## Import

```js
import { ColorPicker } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ColorPicker';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `ColorPicker`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value / defaultValue` | `string` | `#2563eb (defaultValue)` | no | Controlled or initial color: hex, rgb(), rgba(), hsl(), or hsla(). |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — | no | Receives lowercase #rrggbb, or #rrggbbaa for a translucent color. |
| `defaultFormat` | `hex \| rgb \| hsl \| css` | `hex` | no | Initial editor format. The selector changes presentation without changing the color. |
| `showAlpha` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Show the opacity slider and percentage editor. Hiding them preserves existing alpha. |
| `showEyeDropper` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Show screen sampling, enabled when the browser supports the EyeDropper API in a secure context. |
| `label` | `string` | `Color` | no | Visible label and accessible name for every control. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Help text associated with the canvas keyboard controls and text editor. |
| `swatches` | `string[]` | `[]` | no | Optional color presets. Duplicate and invalid entries are omitted. |
| `disabled / readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Prevent editing. Read-only values allow format inspection; disabled values are omitted from forms. |
| `name / id` | `string` | — | no | Form field name and hex/CSS input ID. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `defaultFormat`: `hex`, `rgb`, `hsl`, `css`

## Usage

```jsx
import { ColorPicker } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ColorPicker';

<ColorPicker label='Accent color' value={color} onValueChange={setColor} swatches={['#2563eb', '#16a34a', '#e11d48']} />
```

## Accessibility

The canvas supports mouse, pen, and touch. Its two keyboard stops adjust saturation and brightness with visible thumb focus; hue and opacity also support arrows and Home/End. Presets expose selection with a checkmark and pressed state. Invalid drafts have associated errors.

## Notes

- Hex/CSS text commits on Enter or blur; Escape restores the current color. Invalid drafts never change the selection. RGB and HSL use Gaudi NumberField.
- With opacity controls shown, three- or six-digit hex preserves opacity; four- or eight-digit hex sets alpha explicitly. Screen sampling always preserves opacity. CSS names and other color spaces are unsupported.
- Sampling requires browser support and a secure context. Cancellation is silent. Changing the color, disabling the picker, making it read-only, or hiding/unmounting the eyedropper aborts pending sampling.
- Form reset clears drafts and restores the initial uncontrolled color, notifying only when it changes. Controlled values remain authoritative.
- Layout and interactions are inspired by the shadcn.io Color Picker; all controls use Gaudi styling and primitives.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-colorpicker--playground`)
- Controlled (Storybook `core-colorpicker--controlled`)
- Form and states (Storybook `core-colorpicker--form-and-states`)

## Related

`core-numberfield`

## README

An inline color editor with a saturation/brightness canvas, hue and opacity sliders, HEX/RGB/HSL/CSS entry, screen eyedropper, and optional preset swatches. Its layout follows the [shadcn.io Color Picker](https://www.shadcn.io/components/color-picker), composed with Gaudi's Slider, Input, NumberField, NativeSelect, and Button primitives.

```jsx
import { ColorPicker } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ColorPicker';

<ColorPicker
  label='Accent color'
  name='accent'
  value={color}
  onValueChange={setColor}
  swatches={['#2563eb', '#16a34a', '#f59e0b', '#e11d48']}
  description='Used for links and primary actions.'
/>
```

Use `defaultValue` (default `#2563eb`) for uncontrolled state. Values accept three-, four-, six-, or eight-digit hex with an optional `#`, plus numeric `rgb()`, `rgba()`, `hsl()`, and `hsla()` values. RGB percentages, percentage alpha, and space/slash forms are supported; CSS names, variables, and other color spaces are not. Callbacks and form values use lowercase six-digit hex when opaque, or eight digits when translucent. Alpha is quantized to an 8-bit channel. Invalid supplied values fall back to `#2563eb`; invalid and duplicate swatches are omitted.

`defaultFormat` selects the initial editor (`hex`, `rgb`, `hsl`, or `css`). Changing format does not change the selected color. RGB and HSL offer labelled numeric channels; CSS accepts a color expression and displays `rgba()`. Hex and CSS edits commit on Enter or blur. Invalid drafts show an associated error without changing the selection; Escape cancels the draft. A host color change discards pending text permanently. Controlled values remain authoritative, even when the host refuses a change.

`showAlpha` (default `true`) shows the opacity slider and percentage field. Hiding these controls preserves existing alpha; the hex field then includes alpha when present. With opacity controls visible, three- or six-digit hex edits preserve current opacity. Four- or eight-digit hex explicitly replaces alpha. The eyedropper always preserves current opacity; selecting a preset adopts that preset's alpha. `showEyeDropper` (default `true`) shows the sampling button; it is disabled when the browser lacks the EyeDropper API or a secure context. Sampling starts only on a click. Cancellation is silent, failures can be retried, and changing the color, disabling the picker, making it read-only, or hiding/unmounting the eyedropper aborts pending sampling.

`name` submits the current valid color. Form reset clears drafts, restores the initial uncontrolled color, and calls `onValueChange` if it changes. Controlled resets leave the host value intact. `disabled` prevents interaction and form submission. `readOnly` keeps values selectable and submitted; format switching remains available for inspection.

The visible `label` names the group and every control. The canvas uses pointer capture for mouse, pen, and touch; its two keyboard stops reuse Gaudi Slider for saturation and brightness. Arrow keys adjust values, Home/End jump to bounds, and the visible canvas thumb shows keyboard focus. Hue is retained when selecting black or gray. Presets expose selection with a checkmark and `aria-pressed`. Text and numeric editors inherit InputConfigProvider. `description` explains the picker and is associated with its canvas keyboard controls and text editor. `id` targets the hex/CSS input; remaining DOM props and `className` apply to the root group.

The canvas fills its container. At a container width of 20rem (320px at the default root font size) or narrower, the value editor moves below the toolbar; RGB, HSL, and CSS always use a full-width second row. Swatches wrap within the component. No native color popup or additional runtime dependency is required.

# Commander

> Core/Commander · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Commander`

Commander provides the site command palette with host-supplied destinations for navigation, content search, and theme actions.

Use Commander with a visible trigger such as MenuSearch. MenuSearch already includes the keyboard hint.

## Import

```js
import Commander from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Commander';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Command`, `CommandDialog`, `CommandEmpty`, `CommandFooter`, `CommandGroup`, `CommandInput`, `CommandItem`, `CommandList`, `CommandSeparator`, `CommandShortcut`, `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` | — | no | Controlled palette state. |
| `setOpen` | `(open: boolean) => void` | — | no | State setter used by the trigger, shortcut, keyboard handler, and close behavior. |
| `navigation` | `Array` | `[]` | no | Prepared destinations with id, title, href or onClick, and optional disabled. No built-in routes. |
| `posts` | `Array` | `[]` | no | Searchable post records with prepared id/slug, title and href or onClick. |
| `projects` | `Array` | `[]` | no | Searchable project records. |
| `publications` | `Array` | `[]` | no | Searchable publication records. |
| `tags` | `Array` | `[]` | no | Searchable tag records. |
| `thoughts` | `Array` | `[]` | no | Searchable thought records. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Button, Commander } from '@gaudi/design-system';

export function ContentSearch({ posts = [], projects = [], publications = [], tags = [], thoughts = [] }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Search content</Button>
      <Commander
        open={open}
        setOpen={setOpen}
        posts={posts}
        projects={projects}
        publications={publications}
        tags={tags}
        thoughts={thoughts}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

Commander is a keyboard-first overlay. Keep focus visible, support Escape close/back behavior, expose readable result labels, and make Cmd/Ctrl + K available without hiding the visible trigger.

## States and recovery

- Keep the query and current page intact when a search returns no results; offer a clear route back to all destinations.
- Escape closes the current level first, then the launcher, so keyboard users can recover without losing context.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-commander--playground`)
- Collection Pages (Storybook `core-commander--collection-pages`)

Curated patterns:

- Command dialog with groups and shortcuts — registry item `@gaudi/command-dialog-shortcuts` (uses `Button`, `Command`, `CommandDialog`, `CommandEmpty`, `CommandGroup`, `CommandInput`, `CommandItem`, `CommandList`, `CommandSeparator`, `CommandShortcut`, `RegistryIcon`)
- Inline palette — registry item `@gaudi/command-inline-palette` (uses `CardContent`, `CardRoot`, `Command`, `CommandEmpty`, `CommandGroup`, `CommandInput`, `CommandItem`, `CommandList`, `CommandSeparator`, `CommandShortcut`, `RegistryIcon`)
- Search everything — registry item `@gaudi/command-search-everything` (uses `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarRoot`, `Badge`, `Button`, `Command`, `CommandDialog`, `CommandEmpty`, `CommandGroup`, `CommandInput`, `CommandItem`, `CommandList`, `CommandSeparator`, `KbdRoot`, `RegistryIcon`)

## README

The site-wide command launcher: navigation, full-text search across posts, projects, thoughts, publications and tags, contact links and a theme switch. Open it from a visible trigger such as `MenuSearch`, or with ⌘K / Ctrl+K.

### Usage

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Commander, MenuSearch } from '@gaudi/design-system';

const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
const navigation = [{ id: 'library', title: 'Library', href: '/library' }];
const posts = [{ id: 'release', title: 'Release notes', href: '/articles/release-notes' }];

<MenuSearch setOpen={setOpen} />
<Commander open={open} setOpen={setOpen} navigation={navigation} posts={posts} />
```

### API

| Prop                                            | Type                     | Contract                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open / setOpen`                                | boolean / function       | Controlled visibility; ⌘K / Ctrl+K toggles it through `setOpen`.      |
| `navigation`                                   | Array                    | Prepared destinations; defaults to an empty list.                    |
| `posts / projects / thoughts / publications / tags` | Array                | Each non-empty collection adds a page and full-text results.          |
| `social`                                        | Array                    | Contact entries; defaults to the links in the site metadata.          |
| `restoreFocusRef`                               | Ref                      | Where focus returns when the element that opened the launcher is gone. |

Each destination or collection entry supplies a stable `id` (`slug` is a fallback), a `title`, and an explicit `href` or `onClick`. `disabled` prevents selection and `closeOnSelect={false}` keeps the launcher open for an action. Prepared titles, categories, subtitles, IDs and destinations are preserved, including empty and zero values. Collection names group entries; they do not construct routes. Home, Blog and About links must be supplied through `navigation` when the application uses those destinations.

### Composition

Commander is built on the Command parts it exports: `Command`, `CommandInput`, `CommandList`, `CommandGroup`, `CommandItem`, `CommandEmpty`, `CommandSeparator`, `CommandShortcut`, `CommandFooter` and `CommandDialog`. Use them for inline palettes or your own command dialog; `CommandInput` renders its children at the end of the search row. Pass a button as `CommandDialog`'s `trigger` to connect opening, expanded state, and focus restoration to the same control, including when the dialog opens through a keyboard shortcut.

### Accessibility

The search field is a combobox that controls a listbox. Arrow keys, Home and End move the selection, Enter runs it, and Escape leaves a sub-page before it closes the launcher. Focus returns to the trigger on close.

Inline and popover `Command` compositions use the semantic surface, text, border, and selected-item colors. A surrounding Popover or Dialog owns its outer frame. `CommandDialog` and `Commander` retain the dedicated launcher palette.

# DataTable

`useDataGridRowOrder`, `useDataGridSection`, `useDataGridStructureLabels`, `validateDataGridCellValue`

## When to use

- Use DataTable for actual tabular comparison, not card grids or definition lists.
- Keep filtering predicates in the host: pass FilterBar state through your own match function and give DataTable the visible rows.
- Right-align numeric columns with align: right so figures line up in tabular numerals.
- Pin at most the identifying column and one summary column; pinning releases on narrow screens so every column stays reachable.
- Pin rows for references readers compare against, such as a goal or the current item; pinned bands stop sticking when they would crowd out the scrolling rows.
- Give long lists a maxHeight (or let virtualize="auto" pick one) so the header and pinned rows stay in view; use stickyHeader="page" when the table should scroll with the page under app chrome.
- Prefer pagination or load-more for remote collections; client virtualization suits a few thousand rows that are already loaded.
- For workspaces people shape themselves, compose the DataGrid view controls: DataGridViewOptions, DataGridLayouts with useDataGridLayouts, DataGridCardView, DataGridStatusTabs, header column stats and DataGridColumnPicker (see the CRM workspace and Shipment exceptions examples).

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | `Array<{ key, header, render?, align?, width?, sticky?, footer?, sortable?, searchable?, hideable? }>` | `[]` | no | Column definitions. align: right sets tabular numerals; sticky: start \| end pins to the inline start or end (left \| right are read as start \| end, so pins mirror in RTL); className styles the column header and cells; footer(rows) renders a total. |
| `rows` | `Array<Record<string, unknown>>` | `[]` | no | Rows keyed by column key. row.id is used as the stable key when present. |
| `searchable / sortable / selectable` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Search with a live count, header sorting, and page-scoped row selection. |
| `columnVisibility / pagination` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Column controls and paged rows with first, previous, next and last. |
| `pageSize` | `number` | `10` | no | Rows per page when pagination is enabled. |
| `density` | `compact \| normal \| comfortable` | `normal` | no | Cell padding and header height. |
| `headerVariant` | `muted \| plain` | `muted` | no | Shared header fill; casing and typography stay consistent across table APIs. |
| `striped / footer` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Alternate row wash; a footer row with the record count and column totals. |
| `renderExpanded` | `function(row)` | — | no | Detail rows under an expand toggle. |
| `canExpand` | `function(row)` | — | no | Detail rows under an expand toggle. |
| `expandMode` | `single \| multiple` | `single` | no | Detail rows under an expand toggle. |
| `getRowActions` | `function(row) => Array<{ label, onSelect, icon?, tone?, disabled? }>` | — | no | An overflow menu at the end of each row; it also opens with a right-click, Shift+F10 or the Menu key. |
| `onRowClick` | `function(row)` | — | no | Makes rows focusable and activatable, ignoring clicks on inner controls; canActivateRow leaves rows that return false inert. |
| `canActivateRow` | `function(row) => boolean` | — | no | Makes rows focusable and activatable, ignoring clicks on inner controls; canActivateRow leaves rows that return false inert. |
| `sorting` | `Array<{ id, desc }>` | — | no | Controlled or initial sort state. The host can refuse or replace a change by not applying it. |
| `defaultSorting` | `Array` | `[]` | no | Controlled or initial sort state. The host can refuse or replace a change by not applying it. |
| `onSortingChange` | `function` | — | no | Controlled or initial sort state. The host can refuse or replace a change by not applying it. |
| `multiSort` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Shift-click a header to sort by more than one column; headers show their sort order. |
| `expanded` | `string[]` | — | no | Controlled or initial open detail rows by row ID. |
| `defaultExpanded` | `string[]` | `[]` | no | Controlled or initial open detail rows by row ID. |
| `onExpandedChange` | `function` | — | no | Controlled or initial open detail rows by row ID. |
| `pinnableRows` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Adds Pin to top, Pin to bottom and Unpin to each row menu. |
| `rowPinning` | `{ top: string[], bottom: string[] }` | — | no | Pinned rows stay above or below the others across sorting, search and pages, and stick under the header while the rest scroll. |
| `defaultRowPinning` | `object` | `{ top: [], bottom: [] }` | no | Pinned rows stay above or below the others across sorting, search and pages, and stick under the header while the rest scroll. |
| `onRowPinningChange` | `function` | — | no | Pinned rows stay above or below the others across sorting, search and pages, and stick under the header while the rest scroll. |
| `stickyHeader` | `false \| container \| page` | `container with maxHeight, otherwise false` | no | Keep the header in view inside the table region, or under page chrome while the page scrolls. Page mode lets the table fit its container rather than scroll sideways. |
| `stickyOffset` | `CSS length` | `0px` | no | Keep the header in view inside the table region, or under page chrome while the page scrolls. Page mode lets the table fit its container rather than scroll sideways. |
| `maxHeight` | `CSS length` | — | no | Scroll rows inside the table region so the header and pinned rows stay in view. |
| `virtualize` | `auto \| true \| false` | `auto` | no | Render only the rows in view for long flat lists; auto switches on above the threshold and gives the region a 32rem height unless maxHeight is set. |
| `virtualThreshold` | `number` | `100` | no | Render only the rows in view for long flat lists; auto switches on above the threshold and gives the region a 32rem height unless maxHeight is set. |
| `onLoadMore` | `function` | — | no | A Load more action for incremental collections; loadMoreOnScroll requests the next batch as the last row comes into view. |
| `hasMore` | `boolean` | `false` | no | A Load more action for incremental collections; loadMoreOnScroll requests the next batch as the last row comes into view. |
| `loadingMore` | `boolean` | `false` | no | A Load more action for incremental collections; loadMoreOnScroll requests the next batch as the last row comes into view. |
| `loadMoreOnScroll` | `boolean` | `false` | no | A Load more action for incremental collections; loadMoreOnScroll requests the next batch as the last row comes into view. |
| `exportable` | `boolean \| { filename, scope, label, delimiter, onExport }` | `false` | no | An Export CSV action: visible columns, current search and sort, and only the selected rows when there is a selection. Columns format values with exportValue(value, row) and opt out with export: false. |
| `groupBy` | `function(row) => { key, label }` | — | no | Collapsible group bands with counts. |
| `toolbar` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Extra controls beside the search, such as a FilterBar facet trigger. |

## Variants

- `density`: `compact`, `normal`, `comfortable`
- `headerVariant`: `muted`, `plain`
- `expandMode`: `single`, `multiple`

## Usage

```jsx
import { DataTable } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<DataTable
  columns={[{ key: 'component', header: 'Component' }]}
  rows={[{ component: 'Button' }]}
/>
```

## Accessibility

DataTable renders a real table: a visually hidden caption, scoped column headers with aria-sort, named selection checkboxes, and a labelled, keyboard-focusable scroll region that pans with the arrow keys. Expand, row-action and group toggles are named buttons with aria-expanded; clickable rows take focus and activate with Enter or Space. The row menu also opens with a right-click, Shift+F10 or the Menu key and returns focus to where it was. Virtualized tables keep aria-rowcount and aria-rowindex so assistive technology knows the full size, and export, load-more and pinning changes are announced through a status region.
