# ImageGallery

> Core/ImageGallery · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/ImageGallery`

A responsive masonry or grid collection with an accessible image viewer. A one-item collection is a full-width, click-to-expand image.

## Import

```js
import { ImageGallery } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ImageGallery';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `ImageGallery`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `images` | `Array<{ id, src, alt, caption?, thumbnailSrc?, width?, height? }>` | `[]` | no | Prepared images with unique, stable string IDs. src is the full image; thumbnailSrc optionally supplies a smaller preview. width and height reserve the thumbnail aspect ratio; a different ratio crops the preview. The viewer always contains the full image. |
| `label` | `string` | `Image gallery` | no | Accessible name of the gallery region. |
| `layout` | `masonry \| grid` | `masonry` | no | Masonry keeps each thumbnail ratio and reads down each column. Grid reads across rows and crops thumbnails to 4:3. |
| `columns` | `{ mobile?, tablet?, desktop? }` | `{ mobile: 1, tablet: 2, desktop: 3 }` | no | Positive integer column counts at gallery widths below 640px, from 640px, and from 1024px. A single image always occupies one full-width column. |
| `showCaptions` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Shows captions below thumbnails. The viewer always shows the active caption or alternative text. |
| `selectedId` | `string \| null` | `uncontrolled` | no | Controls or initializes the viewer selection. null closes it; selecting a thumbnail, navigating, swiping, and closing request a change. Controlled hosts remain authoritative. An ID absent from images closes the viewer. |
| `defaultSelectedId` | `string \| null` | `null` | no | Controls or initializes the viewer selection. null closes it; selecting a thumbnail, navigating, swiping, and closing request a change. Controlled hosts remain authoritative. An ID absent from images closes the viewer. |
| `onSelectedIdChange` | `(id) => void` | — | no | Controls or initializes the viewer selection. null closes it; selecting a thumbnail, navigating, swiping, and closing request a change. Controlled hosts remain authoritative. An ID absent from images closes the viewer. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Disables thumbnail activation and hides the viewer while true, retaining the selection. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `layout`: `masonry`, `grid`

## Usage

```jsx
import { ImageGallery } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ImageGallery';

<ImageGallery images={[{ id: 'lavender', src: '/static/images/art/0.svg', alt: 'Lavender gradient artwork', caption: 'A study in lavender and light', width: 1200, height: 675 }]} />
```

## Accessibility

Thumbnails are named buttons. Enter or Space opens the viewer. Arrow keys move between images (respecting direction), Home and End select the first and last images, and Escape closes. Touch supports swiping and browser pinch zoom. Dialog contains focus and restores the opener, or the gallery region if that opener was removed or disabled. Reduced motion removes animated slide movement.

## Notes

- Provide useful alt text; captions add visible context. Offscreen slides are hidden from assistive technology. Navigation stops at either end and disappears for a single image.
- Images load lazily, with the selected full image loaded eagerly. Failed sources show an accessible placeholder; replace thumbnailSrc (or src when no thumbnail is supplied) to recover a preview, and src to recover the full image. Empty collections show an explicit empty state.
- Use one image in images for an expandable article figure. No separate single-image wrapper is needed. Existing MDX/Image and MDX/ImageModal share the same viewer while preserving their APIs.
- The Shadix UI gallery informed the masonry and expansion behavior. The implementation uses Gaudi Dialog, Carousel, Button and Icon; it does not load remote demo resources.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-imagegallery--playground`)
- Single expandable image (Storybook `core-imagegallery--single`)
- Controlled grid (Storybook `core-imagegallery--controlled`)
- Empty & unavailable images (Storybook `core-imagegallery--recovery`)

## Related

`blocks-navigation`, `mdx-image`, `mdx-imagemodal`, `core-dialog`, `core-carousel`, `core-button`, `core-icon`

## README

A masonry or grid collection whose images open in a shared viewer. Pass one item for a full-width, click-to-expand image; the same component handles both uses.

```jsx
import { ImageGallery } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ImageGallery';

<ImageGallery
  label='Coastal photographs'
  images={[
    {
      id: 'north-coast',
      src: '/images/north-coast.jpg',
      thumbnailSrc: '/images/north-coast-small.jpg',
      alt: 'Waves breaking against a rocky coastline',
      caption: 'The north coast',
      width: 1200,
      height: 800
    }
  ]}
/>
```

Use local, host-supplied assets. Gaudi's examples use local files and do not fetch third-party demo resources.

### API

| Prop | Default | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `images` | `[]` | Array of `{ id, src, alt, caption?, thumbnailSrc?, width?, height? }`. Supply unique, stable string IDs and meaningful alternative text. |
| `label` | `'Image gallery'` | Accessible name of the gallery region; distinguish multiple galleries on a page. |
| `layout` | `'masonry'` | `'masonry'` preserves thumbnail ratios; `'grid'` crops thumbnails to 4:3. |
| `columns` | `{ mobile: 1, tablet: 2, desktop: 3 }` | Positive integer column counts. Each omitted field keeps its default. One image always uses one full-width column. |
| `showCaptions` | `true` | Shows captions below thumbnails. The viewer always shows the active caption, alternative text, or `'Image preview'`. |
| `selectedId` | `undefined` | Controlled selection. A matching ID opens the viewer; `null` closes it. |
| `defaultSelectedId` | `null` | Initial selection when uncontrolled. |
| `onSelectedIdChange` | — | Receives the requested ID, or `null` when closing. |
| `disabled` | `false` | Disables thumbnail activation and hides the viewer while preserving selection. |
| `className`, `style` | — | Applied to the gallery region. Other DOM props also pass to this outer element. |

`src` supplies the full image. `thumbnailSrc`, when present, supplies only the preview. Provide both `width` and `height` to reserve the thumbnail's aspect ratio; a source with a different ratio is cropped to fit. Without dimensions, masonry uses the loaded image's natural ratio. The viewer contains the full image without cropping.

Columns respond to the **gallery container width**: `mobile` below 640px, `tablet` from 640px, and `desktop` from 1024px. Masonry reads down each column before moving to the next; grid reads across rows. Keyboard and viewer navigation follow the supplied `images` order.

### Controlled selection

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { ImageGallery } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ImageGallery';

function Gallery({ images, disabled = false }) {
  const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState(null);

  return (
    <ImageGallery
      images={images}
      selectedId={selectedId}
      onSelectedIdChange={setSelectedId}
      disabled={disabled}
    />
  );
}
```

Thumbnail activation, navigation buttons, keyboard navigation, swiping, and closing request selection changes. The controlled host must accept a request by updating `selectedId`; it can also refuse or replace it. An ID absent from `images` hides the viewer without clearing the stored selection. Disabling behaves the same way: re-enabling reopens the retained image if it still exists. Set `selectedId` to `null` when the host wants to clear it permanently.

### Interaction and recovery

- Thumbnails are named buttons. Enter or Space opens the viewer and focuses Close. Left/Right arrows navigate with the current text direction; Home/End select the first/last image. Navigation stops at either end, and previous/next controls are omitted for a single image.
- Escape, Close, or the backdrop requests dismissal. Dialog contains focus and restores the opener when it remains connected and enabled; otherwise, it falls back to the gallery region. Offscreen slides are hidden from assistive technology, and the active caption is announced politely.
- Carousel owns touch swiping. Browser pinch zoom remains available; there are no separate zoom controls. Reduced motion removes animated slide movement and the expansion hint's transition.
- Thumbnails and inactive full images use lazy loading; the selected full image loads eagerly. Failed sources show an accessible `Image unavailable` placeholder. Replace the effective preview source (`thumbnailSrc || src`) to recover a thumbnail, or `src` to recover a full image. An empty collection displays `No images to display.`

### Shared ownership

ImageGallery composes Gaudi's Dialog, Carousel, Button, and Icon, using the existing neutral themes, radius tokens (4px by default), and density scale. The masonry and expansion behavior was informed by Shadix UI.

The existing MDX `Image` and `ImageModal` APIs share this viewer through the MDX adapter. The Core entry exports only `ImageGallery`; use a one-item collection for a standalone expandable image. The shared lightbox is private.

# Input

> Core/Input · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Input`

Text, search, numeric and date inputs with prefix and suffix slots.

## Import

```js
import Input from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Input';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `EmailInput`, `InputGroup`, `InputGroupAddon`, `InputGroupButton`, `InputGroupInput`, `InputGroupText`, `InputGroupTextarea`, `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `caretMode` | `native \| smooth` | `provider / smooth` | no | Overrides InputConfigProvider for this field. Smooth mode animates the collapsed caret while supported native text controls retain their editing behavior. |
| `type` | `text \| email \| search \| url \| tel \| password \| number \| date` | `text` | no | Native input type. Use EmailInput for addresses and NumberField for numeric values to retain the default smooth caret. |
| `prefix / suffix` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Content before or after the native control. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | — | no | Example value; never a replacement for a label. |
| `required / disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Native form constraint and availability. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | — | no | Marks the underlying FieldInput as invalid. |
| `inputClassName` | `string` | — | no | Classes on the input itself. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |
| `Native input props / ref` | `InputHTMLAttributes<HTMLInputElement>` | — | no | Forwards value, defaultValue, onChange, disabled, required, name, autocomplete and ARIA attributes to the input. |

## Variants

- `caretMode`: `native`, `smooth`

## Usage

```jsx
import Input, { EmailInput } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Input';

<>
  <Input aria-label='Project name' value={name} onChange={event => setName(event.target.value)} />
  <EmailInput aria-label='Email address' name='email' required />
</>
```

## Accessibility

Compose Field, FieldLabel, FieldDescription and FieldError. Keep labels visible and connect errors to their control.

## Notes

- EmailInput is a named export from the Input entry. It composes Input with a text editor, an email keyboard hint, email autocomplete and single-address pattern validation, so it supports smooth caret mode.
- EmailInput fixes type=text and inputMode=email; multiple addresses are unsupported. An additional pattern narrows the allowed addresses. Invalid author patterns are ignored while email validation remains active.
- EmailInput keeps raw text (spaces are invalid), reports patternMismatch instead of typeMismatch, and leaves custom error copy to FieldError/onInvalid. required, minLength/maxLength, name, form, value/defaultValue, refs and event handlers reach the native editor.
- Smooth caret is enabled by default. Use EmailInput for addresses and NumberField for numeric values throughout forms and examples; reserve native email/number types for documented semantic exceptions. Provider and per-field caretMode=native overrides remain available.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-input--playground`)
- Smooth Caret Mode (Storybook `core-input--smooth-caret-mode`)
- Email Address (Storybook `core-input--email-address`)

## Related

`core-numberfield`, `core-field`

## README

A single-line text field for names, emails, URLs, numbers and dates. `prefix` and `suffix` add text or icons inside the border (they render as InputGroup addons); every native attribute and the ref reach the input itself. Wrap it in a Field for its label, help and error.

For buttons, menus or several addons inside the border, compose `InputGroup`, `InputGroupAddon`, `InputGroupButton`, `InputGroupText` and `InputGroupInput` directly.

### Usage

```jsx
import { EmailInput } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Input';
import { Field, FieldLabel, FieldDescription } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Field';

<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Email address</FieldLabel>
  <EmailInput
    name='email'
    autoComplete='email'
    placeholder='you@example.com'
  />
  <FieldDescription>Used for your reading digest.</FieldDescription>
</Field>;
```

### Accessibility

Visible labels are connected through Field. Inputs retain native validation, autocomplete and form submission.

### Examples

The Playground uses EmailInput for its email field and NumberField for its monthly budget; both inherit the global Caret toolbar. Other type choices use Input. Its preview controls include a per-field caret override, adornments, invalid and disabled states. The catalogue adds native types, password strength, and every addon placement. The chat composer built on InputGroup is `ChatInput` in the Chat area.

The same `InputGroup` and native control remain mounted when `prefix` or `suffix` appears or disappears. Conditional clear buttons and validation adornments preserve typed values, focus, selection, and the input ref.

### EmailInput

`EmailInput` is the single-address email editor exported from this owner. It uses a text input with `inputMode='email'`, `autoComplete='email'`, no capitalization and no spellcheck. Its caret supports the same provider and field override as Input.

```jsx
import { EmailInput } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Input';
import { Field, FieldLabel, FieldDescription } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Field';

<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Email address</FieldLabel>
  <EmailInput name='email' required placeholder='you@example.com' />
  <FieldDescription>Enter one email address, without spaces.</FieldDescription>
</Field>
```

The browser validates the [HTML email-address grammar](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#email-state-(type=email)) through `pattern`. Invalid addresses block normal form submission and report `validity.patternMismatch`; empty required fields report `validity.valueMissing`. Optional empty fields are valid. This works from server-rendered HTML, without a validation effect or hidden input. `onInvalid`, `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`, `setCustomValidity()`, form reset, native validation styles and FormData continue to work.

`value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, refs, `name`, `form`, `required`, length constraints, disabled/read-only states, adornments and ARIA attributes follow Input. `autoComplete` can be overridden. An additional `pattern` further restricts valid email addresses; invalid author patterns are ignored without disabling email validation. Use `FieldError` and `onInvalid` for specific, localized feedback, as shown in the Email Address story.

This is a text editor with email validation, not a native `type='email'` input: it preserves typed whitespace (which is invalid), reports `patternMismatch` rather than `typeMismatch`, and accepts one address only. `type`, `inputMode` and `multiple` are fixed by the component. Internationalized domain names must be provided in ASCII/Punycode form; it does not convert them. Keep `Input type='email'` when native email sanitization or multiple-address entry is required.

For numeric values with smooth movement, compose [NumberField](../NumberField/README.md). Put `caretMode` on `NumberFieldInput` for a per-field override; the root manages numeric values, bounds, stepping and formatting.

### Smooth caret mode

Smooth movement is the default, including without a provider. Use `InputConfigProvider` around the application or a form to change that default. `caretMode='smooth'` adds a short glide while typing or moving within a line; `caretMode='native'` keeps the browser caret. The Storybook **Caret** toolbar switches the default across examples. Individual controls override the inherited value without remounting or changing their value.

```jsx
import { InputConfigProvider } from '@gaudi/design-system/context';
import Input from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Input';

<InputConfigProvider caretMode='smooth'>
  <Input aria-label='Project name' />
  <Input caretMode='native' aria-label='Reference code' />
</InputConfigProvider>
```

The setting reaches FieldInput, Input, EmailInput, Textarea, InputGroup controls, phone inputs, chat composers, autocomplete/combobox search fields, command search, Cascader, Questionnaire and NumberField text controls. Native text editor overlays in DataGrid inherit the setting. Set `caretMode` on the actual input part for a local override.

Editing, validation, form data, undo, autofill, selection and refs remain native. The decoration is hidden from assistive technology, stays inside the field, and uses the field's caret color and typography. Only a focused field is measured, with updates batched to animation frames; no motion dependency is required. Wrapped-line changes snap vertically.

Reduced motion, forced colors, touch selection, IME composition, selected text, read-only fields, password masking, bidirectional text and input types without browser selection APIs retain the native caret. Supported types are text, search, URL, telephone and textarea. These fallbacks preserve the browser's specialized editing UI.

Inspired by [Skiper UI's smooth caret input](https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper106); Gaudi's implementation uses DOM text layout and its existing motion tokens.

# InputOtp

> Core/InputOtp · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/InputOtp`

One-time code entry with grouped slots, paste support and completion feedback.

## Import

```js
import { InputOTP } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/InputOtp';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `InputOTP`, `InputOTPGroup`, `InputOTPSeparator`, `InputOTPSlot`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maxLength` | `number` | `Required` | no | Number of characters accepted. |
| `value` | `string` | — | no | Controlled code entry. |
| `onChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — | no | Controlled code entry. |
| `onComplete` | `(value: string) => void` | — | no | Called when every slot is filled. |
| `pattern` | `string` | — | no | Allowed character pattern. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Dims every slot and blocks code entry. |
| `containerClassName` | `string` | — | no | Classes on the slot container. |
| `InputOTPSlot.index` | `number` | `Required` | no | Zero-based character index. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Content composed from the exported parts. |
| `Native input props / ref` | `InputHTMLAttributes<HTMLInputElement>` | — | no | Forwards value, defaultValue, onChange, disabled, required, name, autocomplete and ARIA attributes to the input. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { InputOTP, InputOTPGroup, InputOTPSlot } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/InputOtp';

<InputOTP maxLength={6} aria-label='Verification code' value={code} onChange={setCode}>
  <InputOTPGroup>{Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, index) => <InputOTPSlot key={index} index={index} />)}</InputOTPGroup>
</InputOTP>
```

## Accessibility

The underlying input supports keyboard entry and paste. Label the complete code field and announce validation beside it.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-inputotp--playground`)

Curated patterns:

- Code formats — registry item `@gaudi/input-otp-code-formats` (uses `FieldDescriptionPrimitive`, `FieldLabelPrimitive`, `FieldRoot`, `InputOTP`, `InputOTPGroup`, `InputOTPSeparator`, `InputOTPSlot`)

## README

Separate boxes for a one-time code, such as a sign-in or verification code sent by email or text.

### Usage

```jsx
import { InputOTP, InputOTPGroup, InputOTPSeparator, InputOTPSlot } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<InputOTP maxLength={6} aria-label='Verification code' value={code} onChange={setCode}>
  <InputOTPGroup>
    <InputOTPSlot index={0} />
    <InputOTPSlot index={1} />
    <InputOTPSlot index={2} />
  </InputOTPGroup>
  <InputOTPSeparator />
  <InputOTPGroup>
    <InputOTPSlot index={3} />
    <InputOTPSlot index={4} />
    <InputOTPSlot index={5} />
  </InputOTPGroup>
</InputOTP>;
```

`pattern` limits which characters are accepted, and `onComplete` fires once every slot is filled.

### Accessibility

One real input sits behind the slots, so pasting, autofill and screen readers treat the code as a single field. Give it an `aria-label` or a visible label.

# Item

> Core/Item · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Item`

Flexible rows for people, settings, integrations, navigation and activity lists, composed from media, text, actions and optional header and footer rows.

## Import

```js
import { Item } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Item';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Item`, `ItemActions`, `ItemContent`, `ItemDescription`, `ItemFooter`, `ItemGroup`, `ItemHeader`, `ItemMedia`, `ItemSeparator`, `ItemTitle`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `default \| outline \| muted` | `default` | no | Row surface: plain, bordered or tinted. |
| `size` | `default \| sm \| xs` | `default` | no | Row density. |
| `as` | `ElementType` | `div` | no | Render the row as another element, or merge it into a link or button child. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Render the row as another element, or merge it into a link or button child. |
| `ItemMedia.variant` | `default \| icon \| image` | `default` | no | Presentation of the leading media slot. |
| `ItemGroup` | `HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>` | — | no | A role="group" wrapper that stacks rows; pair with ItemSeparator. |
| `ItemTitle / ItemDescription` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Row title (one line) and supporting text (two lines). |
| `ItemActions / ItemHeader / ItemFooter` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Trailing controls and full-width rows above or below the content. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Content composed from the exported parts. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `variant`: `default`, `outline`, `muted`
- `size`: `default`, `sm`, `xs`

## Usage

```jsx
import { Button, Item, ItemActions, ItemContent, ItemDescription, ItemGroup, ItemMedia, ItemTitle } from '@gaudi/design-system';
import { RegistryIcon } from '@gaudi/design-system/icons';

<ItemGroup>
  <Item variant='outline'>
    <ItemMedia variant='icon'><RegistryIcon lucide='GithubIcon' aria-hidden='true' /></ItemMedia>
    <ItemContent>
      <ItemTitle>GitHub</ItemTitle>
      <ItemDescription>Sync pull requests and issues.</ItemDescription>
    </ItemContent>
    <ItemActions><Button href='/settings/integrations/github' size='sm' variant='outline'>Connect</Button></ItemActions>
  </Item>
</ItemGroup>
```

## Accessibility

Use asChild with a link when the whole row navigates and keep independent actions outside that link. Name icon-only actions after their row, and label a group when the surrounding heading does not describe it.

## README

A flexible row for lists of people, settings, integrations, navigation links, activity and run logs. Compose media, a title and description, trailing actions, and an optional header or footer; group rows with `ItemGroup` and divide them with `ItemSeparator`.

### Usage

```jsx
import { Button, Item, ItemActions, ItemContent, ItemDescription, ItemGroup, ItemMedia, ItemTitle, RegistryIcon } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<ItemGroup>
  <Item variant='outline'>
    <ItemMedia variant='icon'><RegistryIcon lucide='GithubIcon' aria-hidden='true' /></ItemMedia>
    <ItemContent>
      <ItemTitle>GitHub</ItemTitle>
      <ItemDescription>Sync pull requests and issues.</ItemDescription>
    </ItemContent>
    <ItemActions><Button href='/settings/integrations/github' size='sm' variant='outline'>Connect</Button></ItemActions>
  </Item>
</ItemGroup>
```

The parts are also available from `@gaudi/design-system/core/Item`.

### Parts

| Part | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `Item` | `variant` (default, outline, muted), `size` (default, sm, xs), `as` for the element and `asChild` to render a link or button. |
| `ItemMedia` | `variant` default, icon or image. |
| `ItemContent`, `ItemTitle`, `ItemDescription` | Main text column; the description clamps to two lines. |
| `ItemActions` | Trailing badges, buttons or menus. |
| `ItemHeader`, `ItemFooter` | Full-width rows above and below the content. |
| `ItemGroup`, `ItemSeparator` | A `role='group'` list wrapper and a horizontal divider. |

### Accessibility

Use `asChild` with a link when the whole row navigates, and keep independent actions outside that link. Name icon-only actions after their row ("Remove Odile Marchetti"). Give a group of rows an accessible name with `aria-label` when the surrounding heading does not describe it.

### Log examples

The Item docs include a live run status, phases separated by labelled rules, changed files with badges, and log links with a reversible action. These compose Item, Separator, Badge, Loader, Link and Button without a separate marker wrapper.

# Kanban

> Core/Kanban · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/KanbanBoard`

Move work items between columns while retaining an accessible move action.

## Import

```js
import Kanban from '@gaudi/design-system/core/KanbanBoard';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Kanban`, `KanbanBoardPrimitive`, `KanbanColumn`, `KanbanColumnContent`, `KanbanColumnCount`, `KanbanColumnHandle`, `KanbanColumnRail`, `KanbanItem`, `KanbanItemHandle`, `KanbanOverlay`, `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | `Array<{ id, label, limit? }>` | `[]` | no | Board columns with stable IDs; limit adds a work-in-progress count that warns when exceeded. |
| `items` | `Array<{ id, columnId }>` | `[]` | no | Host-owned work items. |
| `renderItem` | `(item) => ReactNode` | — | no | Item card content. |
| `onMove` | `(itemId, columnId) => void` | — | no | Request a move; the application updates items. |
| `label / moveLabel / emptyLabel` | `string` | `Board / Move / No items` | no | Accessible board and action labels. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Disable moving items. |

## Usage

```jsx
import KanbanBoard from '@gaudi/design-system/core/KanbanBoard';

<KanbanBoard columns={columns} items={tasks} onMove={moveTask} />
```

## Accessibility

Every item has a move control so dragging is optional. Keep columns inside the contained horizontal scrolling region (layout="scroll" on the composition board). Collapsed rails are buttons that name the column and its count; cards with their own controls use withHandle so the drag grip, not the card, is the sortable control.

## Related

`core-item`

## README

A controlled board for editorial workflows. Supply columns, items, renderItem and onMove. Moves are explicit menu actions accessible by keyboard and touch; this version does not implement drag-and-drop.

### Usage

```jsx
<KanbanBoard
  columns={columns}
  items={items}
  onMove={(id, columnId) =>
    setItems(
      items.map((item) => (item.id === id ? { ...item, columnId } : item))
    )
  }
/>
```

### API

| Prop / export                    | Type                             | Contract                                           |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `columns`                        | {id, label, limit?}[]            | Ordered workflow columns; `limit` shows a WIP count. |
| `items`                          | {id, title, columnId, ...data}[] | Host-owned records and placement.                  |
| `renderItem`                     | function(item)                   | Optional card body.                                |
| `onMove`                         | function(id, columnId)           | Receives a move request. Update items in the host. |
| `disabled`                       | boolean                          | Disable move actions while host work is pending.   |
| `label / moveLabel / emptyLabel` | string                           | Accessible and empty-state copy.                   |

### Drag-and-drop composition

`Kanban`, `KanbanBoardPrimitive`, `KanbanColumn`, `KanbanColumnContent`, `KanbanItem`, the two handles and `KanbanOverlay`
compose a drag-and-drop board with keyboard sorting. For richer boards:

| Part / prop                                   | Contract                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `KanbanBoardPrimitive layout='scroll'`        | Fixed-width columns in their own focusable, horizontally scrolling region. Name it with `aria-label`. |
| `KanbanColumn collapsed` + `KanbanColumnRail` | A collapsed column drawn as a vertical rail button that expands it; cards dropped on it still land in the column. |
| `KanbanColumnCount count limit`               | The column count, or `count/limit`; over the limit it turns to the warning tone and says so.  |
| `KanbanItem withHandle`                       | Moves the sortable role and focus to `KanbanItemHandle`, so a card can hold its own buttons.  |

```jsx
<Kanban value={columns} onValueChange={setColumns} getItemValue={(item) => item.id}>
  <KanbanBoardPrimitive layout='scroll' aria-label='Release board'>
    {Object.entries(columns).map(([id, items]) => (
      <KanbanColumn key={id} value={id} collapsed={hidden.includes(id)}>
        {hidden.includes(id) ? (
          <KanbanColumnRail label={titles[id]} count={items.length} onExpand={() => show(id)} />
        ) : (
          <>
            <h3>{titles[id]}</h3>
            <KanbanColumnCount count={items.length} limit={limits[id]} />
            <KanbanColumnContent value={id}>{items.map(renderCard)}</KanbanColumnContent>
          </>
        )}
      </KanbanColumn>
    ))}
  </KanbanBoardPrimitive>
</Kanban>
```

### Ownership and verification

The host supplies data, translations, network calls, permissions and persistence. Gaudi owns layout, semantics and local interaction. Examples document working behavior and states, with Storybook interaction/axe checks and a server-rendering contract test alongside the component.

# Link

> Core/Link · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Link`

Link centralizes navigation semantics for internal, anchor, and external links.

## Import

```js
import Link from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Link';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `default`, `linkTones`, `linkVariants`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Visible link label. |
| `href` | `internal \| anchor \| external URL` | — | no | Internal routes use Next Link; anchors and external URLs use native anchors. |
| `prefetch` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Next.js prefetch behavior for internal links. |
| `variant` | `inline \| muted \| nav \| bare` | `inline` | no | Text link style: inline takes tone, muted is secondary gray, nav is strong gray turning blue on hover, bare inherits the parent color. |
| `tone` | `accent \| attention \| danger \| discovery \| info \| neutral \| success \| warning` | `neutral` | no | Color family of the inline variant. Default is black/gray and turns blue on hover. muted, nav, and bare have fixed colors and ignore tone. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Root class override. |

## Variants

- `variant`: `inline`, `muted`, `nav`, `bare`
- `tone`: `accent`, `attention`, `danger`, `discovery`, `info`, `neutral`, `success`, `warning`

## Usage

```jsx
import { Link } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Link href='/blog' variant='inline' tone='blue'>Read the blog</Link>
```

## Accessibility

Link renders Next links for internal URLs, anchors for fragments, and safe external anchors with noopener noreferrer.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-link--playground`)
- Link Types (Storybook `core-link--link-types`)
- Variants and tones (Storybook `core-link--variants`)

## README

A link moves the reader to another page, a section of this page, or another site. Use `Button` with `href` when the link should look like an action.

```jsx
import { Link } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Link href='/blog/publications' tone='accent'>publications</Link>
```

- `variant`: `inline` for links in prose (default), `muted` for secondary links such as "Edit this page", `nav` for navigation, and `bare` to inherit the parent colour.
- `tone` colours `inline` links by meaning: `accent`, `neutral` (default), `danger`, `success`, `warning`, `info`, `attention`, `discovery`. Older hue names (`blue`, `gray`, `red`…) still work.
- Internal paths use client navigation, external URLs open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, and a missing `href` renders plain text.

# LinkPreview

> Core/LinkPreview · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/LinkPreview`

A link enriched with what the destination is. One normaliser, normalizeLinkPreview, turns the app's preview payload into a kind (repository, video, article, social post, docs, Wikipedia, package, image, file, internal post or website) and the rich fields that kind earns; three variants present it.

## Import

```js
import LinkPreview from '@gaudi/design-system/core/LinkPreview';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `LinkPreviewBody`, `LinkPreviewCard`, `LinkPreviewCompact`, `LinkPreviewFallback`, `LinkPreviewFavicon`, `LinkPreviewMedia`, `LinkPreviewMeta`, `LinkPreviewSkeleton`, `LinkPreviewTags`, `NPM_HOSTNAME`, `UNAVAILABLE_STATUSES`, `clearPreviewCache`, `default`, `detectLinkKind`, `formatLinkCount`, `formatLinkDuration`, `formatLinkTitle`, `getLinkHost`, `getPreviewImageUrl`, `getYouTubeVideoId`, `hasLinkPreviewDetails`, `linkPreviewKinds`, `normalizeFaviconURL`, `normalizeLinkPreview`, `parseLinkUrl`, `resolvePreviewRequest`, `toImageResolver`, `usePreviewData`, `usePreviewEndpoint`, `usePreviewImageResolver`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | `string` | — | no | Destination, absolute or an app path such as /blog/post. |
| `title` | `string` | `page title` | no | Visible link text; the card keeps the page's own title. |
| `variant` | `inline \| card \| compact` | `inline` | no | Link with a hover card, a standalone card, or a one-line row. |
| `orientation` | `vertical \| horizontal` | `vertical` | no | Card layout: image above or beside the text. |
| `previewData` | `object` | — | no | Static payload; skips fetching. Understands title, description, image, favicon, siteName, author, publishedTime, readingTime, duration, stars, forks, language, likes, replies, views, tags, category, excerpt. |
| `endpoint` | `string \| (url) => string \| null` | `SiteConfig preview.endpoint (none)` | no | App-owned preview endpoint. With none configured nothing is fetched and the link renders from previewData or as a plain link. |
| `showImage` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Inline: open the hover card. Card: show the image. |
| `resolveImage` | `(link) => string \| null \| template map` | `SiteConfig preview.resolveImage (none)` | no | Image for links whose payload has none, e.g. a video thumbnail or a screenshot. Gaudi ships no image services. |
| `internal` | `boolean` | `paths starting with /` | no | Treat the link as an app page. |
| `headingLevel` | `2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `3` | no | Heading level of the card title. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Start the inline hover card open. |
| `timeout` | `number` | `10000` | no | Request timeout in milliseconds. |
| `onLoad / onError` | `function` | — | no | Load callbacks. |
| `fallback` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Replaces the plain-link fallback when metadata fails. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `variant`: `inline`, `card`, `compact`
- `orientation`: `vertical`, `horizontal`
- `headingLevel`: `2`, `3`, `4`, `5`, `6`

## Usage

```jsx
import { LinkPreview, SiteConfigProvider } from '@gaudi/design-system';

// Inline: the link text reveals a rich card on hover or focus.
<>
<p>The source is in <LinkPreview url='https://github.com/g-udi/design-system' title='Gaudi on GitHub' />.</p>

{/* Card and compact row; previewData skips fetching (server-rendered or cached metadata). */}
<LinkPreview url='https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qh3NGpYRG3I' variant='card' previewData={{ title: 'Designing with tokens', image: '/og/tokens.jpg', author: 'Gaudi', duration: 'PT12M41S' }} />
<LinkPreview url='https://medium.com/@ahmadassaf/knowledge-graphs' variant='compact' />

{/* The app owns the endpoint that fetches metadata and any derived images; Gaudi loads nothing by default. */}
<SiteConfigProvider preview={{ endpoint: '/api/preview', resolveImage: { video: '/thumbs/{videoId}.jpg' } }}>{children}</SiteConfigProvider>
</>
```

## Accessibility

Every variant is a real link with a readable name; the hover card opens on focus too and only adds detail. Unavailable links (400, 404, 410) say so in their accessible name, and stats are read as "1.3K stars", not bare numbers.

## Notes

- The app owns fetching: Gaudi only calls an endpoint the app configures, never third-party pages, and derives no image URLs itself.
- usePreviewData caches responses (LRU, one hour; failures for a minute) and deduplicates concurrent requests.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-linkpreview--playground`)
- Link previews (Storybook `core-linkpreview--link-previews`)
- States (Storybook `core-linkpreview--states`)

## Related

`core-link`, `core-card`, `mdx-image`

## README

A link enriched with what the destination is. One pure normaliser, `normalizeLinkPreview`, turns the app's preview payload into a display model, and three variants present it:

- `inline` (default): the link text, with a rich card on hover or focus. This is what the blog's MDX `Preview` renders.
- `card`: a Card with the Open Graph image, `orientation` vertical or horizontal; the title links to the destination.
- `compact`: a one-line row with the favicon, title, host and leading metadata.

### Usage

```jsx
import { LinkPreview, SiteConfigProvider } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<p>The source is in <LinkPreview url='https://github.com/g-udi/design-system' title='Gaudi on GitHub' />.</p>

<LinkPreview url='https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qh3NGpYRG3I' variant='card' previewData={payload} />
<LinkPreview url='https://medium.com/@ahmadassaf/knowledge-graphs' variant='compact' />

// The app owns the endpoint and any derived images; Gaudi loads nothing by default.
<SiteConfigProvider preview={{ endpoint: '/api/preview', resolveImage }}>{children}</SiteConfigProvider>
```

### What each link shows

`normalizeLinkPreview(data, { url, title, resolveImage, locale })` returns `{ kind, status, unavailable, title, linkTitle, description, excerpt, image, favicon, icon, site, label, author, date, formattedDate, readingTime, duration, tags, stats, meta, videoId, embeddable }`. The payload `type` wins; otherwise the URL decides the kind:

| Kind | Detected from | Rich information |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `internal` | `type: 'internal'` or an app path (`/blog/…`) | Category badge, post title, summary, date, reading time, tags. No image. |
| `repository` | `github.com` | `owner/repo` title, image (payload or `resolveImage`), language, stars and forks when the endpoint supplies them. |
| `video` | YouTube, youtu.be, Vimeo | Thumbnail with a play badge and duration chip, channel, views. |
| `social` | x.com, twitter.com, bsky.app | Author handle (from the URL when missing), the post text, replies and likes. |
| `wikipedia` | `wikipedia.org` | Article name and excerpt instead of an image. |
| `package` | `npmjs.com` (synthesized, no fetch) | Package name, package icon, version. |
| `docs` | MDN, `docs.*`, readthedocs, `/docs` paths | Cleaned title (site suffixes removed), description. |
| `image` / `file` | Image or document extensions | The image itself / the file type badge (PDF, CSV…). |
| `article` | Medium, Substack, dev.to, or any payload with an author or published time | Author, date, reading time. |
| `website` | Everything else | Title, description, image, site name. |

Titles drop noisy suffixes (` - MDN Web Docs`, ` - YouTube`, ` · GitHub`…) and cap at 60 characters. Failures with status 400, 404 or 410 are `unavailable` and render a red link named "(link may be unavailable)"; other failures and missing endpoints render an ordinary link. Gaudi derives no images of its own; see [Images](#images).

### Data

`usePreviewData(url, title, { previewData, endpoint, timeout })` calls the endpoint (`endpoint` option, then `SiteConfigProvider preview.endpoint`) with an LRU + TTL cache, request deduplication and a stale-response guard. A string endpoint receives `?url=`; a function returns the full request URL. **There is no default endpoint**: with none configured nothing is fetched, and links render from `previewData` or as plain links. Stories and tests pass static `previewData`.

### Images

A card shows the payload's `image`, or the link itself when it points at an image. Gaudi ships no thumbnail, Open Graph or screenshot service URLs. For anything else, pass `resolveImage` (prop, or `SiteConfigProvider preview.resolveImage`); it is called for links whose payload has no image with `{ kind, url, host, data, videoId, repository }` (`videoId` for YouTube links, `repository: { owner, repo }` for GitHub links) and returns an image URL or `null`. Instead of a function, `resolveImage` can be a template map: link kinds (`video`, `repository`, `website`, `article`…, plus `default`) to URL templates with `{url}` (encoded), `{rawUrl}`, `{host}`, `{videoId}`, `{owner}` and `{repo}`. A kind mapped to `null` shows no image, and a template whose placeholder has no value yields none. Templates are plain data, so a server component can pass them. Without a resolver those links show no image.

### Migrating from the built-in defaults (2026-10-02)

Earlier versions called `/api/preview` without being asked, derived YouTube thumbnails and GitHub Open Graph cards from the URL, used a Microlink screenshot when the MDX `Preview` had no image, and gave npm links a favicon from npmjs.com. Those defaults are gone, along with the `MICROLINK_SCREENSHOT_API`, `YOUTUBE_THUMBNAIL_API`, `GITHUB_OPENGRAPH_API`, `NPM_FAVICON_URL` and `DEFAULT_PREVIEW_ENDPOINT` exports and the `screenshotFallback` option. An app that wants the old behaviour configures it once:

```jsx
// Plain data, so it can be passed from the server LayoutContainer.
const preview = {
  endpoint: '/api/preview',
  resolveImage: {
    video: 'https://img.youtube.com/vi/{videoId}/maxresdefault.jpg',
    repository: 'https://opengraph.githubassets.com/1/{owner}/{repo}',
    wikipedia: null, // Wikipedia shows its excerpt instead
    default: 'https://api.microlink.io/?url={url}&screenshot=true&meta=false&embed=screenshot.url'
  }
};

<LayoutContainer preview={preview} …>   // or <SiteConfigProvider preview={preview}>
```

The old screenshot applied only to the MDX `Preview`; with this setting it applies to every LinkPreview without an image. To keep it MDX-only, pass `resolveImage` to the MDX `Preview` map entry instead of the provider.

### Parts

`LinkPreviewBody`, `LinkPreviewCard`, `LinkPreviewCompact`, `LinkPreviewMedia`, `LinkPreviewMeta`, `LinkPreviewTags`, `LinkPreviewFavicon`, `LinkPreviewSkeleton` and `LinkPreviewFallback` take the normalised `preview` and can be composed into other surfaces (chat sources, link lists).

### Accessibility

Every variant is a real link with a readable name, so the destination never depends on the card. The hover card opens on focus as well as hover and only adds detail. Stats are read with their unit ("1.3K stars"), and images inside cards are decorative except for image links.

---

# Loader

> Core/Loader · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Loader`

An accessible loading indicator with arcs, dots, expanding rings, and an indeterminate bar. Loader replaces the former Spinner component and story.

## Import

```js
import Loader from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Loader';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Loader`, `LoaderRoot`, `default`, `loaderVariants`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `arc \| dual-arc \| bar \| beat \| bounce \| circle-dots \| clip \| puff \| three-dots \| triangle \| two-dots` | `arc` | no | Selects the motion and shape. Every variant represents an unknown wait; use Progress when completion can be measured. |
| `size` | `xs \| sm \| md \| lg` | `md` | no | 12, 16, 20, or 32px tall. The bar is three times as wide; other variants are square. Shapes keep these dimensions across spacing presets. |
| `label` | `string` | `Loading` | no | Accessible status label describing the operation. A visible label belongs beside the indicator. |
| `LoaderRoot` | `component` | `currentColor, sm` | no | Composition primitive with the same variants and sizing. Inherits text color and accepts aria-label rather than label. Loader adds the accent color and md default. |
| `loaderVariants` | `string[]` | — | no | Supported variant names for controls or a variant picker. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `variant`: `arc`, `dual-arc`, `bar`, `beat`, `bounce`, `circle-dots`, `clip`, `puff`, `three-dots`, `triangle`, `two-dots`
- `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`

## Usage

```jsx
import { Loader } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Loader';

<Loader variant='three-dots' size='md' label='Loading articles' />
```

## Accessibility

Each loader exposes role="status" and a readable label. Motion is decorative to that status. With reduced motion, rotation, travel, scaling and bouncing stop; the whole indicator breathes slowly in place. For an already-labelled button or busy region, use aria-hidden="true" to avoid duplicate announcements.

## Notes

- Use className="text-current" to inherit surrounding text, or a semantic tone such as text-text-muted. Explicit size utility classes can override the dimensions. Keep the bar at its natural 3:1 ratio.
- All animation is CSS and SVG; there are no timers or browser-only rendering dependencies. Unmount the loader when the operation finishes. Loading state, cancellation, progress and recovery belong to the host.
- Import Loader from the root, core, or core/Loader entry. Spinner, SpinnerRoot and core/Spinner have been renamed to Loader, LoaderRoot and core/Loader; update existing imports.
- The Shadix UI loader reference informed the variant family. Geometry and motion are implemented locally using Gaudi colors, density and motion conventions.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-loader--playground`)
- Animation variants (Storybook `core-loader--variants`)

Curated patterns:

- In buttons, badges and inputs — registry item `@gaudi/loader-inline-controls` (uses `Badge`, `Button`, `InputGroup`, `InputGroupAddon`, `InputGroupInput`, `LoaderRoot`)
- Inline status — registry item `@gaudi/loader-inline-status` (uses `ChatActivityIndicator`, `LoaderRoot`)
- Overlays and empty states — registry item `@gaudi/loader-overlays` (uses `Button`, `CardContent`, `CardDescription`, `CardHeader`, `CardRoot`, `CardTitle`, `Empty`, `EmptyContent`, `EmptyDescription`, `EmptyHeader`, `EmptyMedia`, `EmptyTitle`, `Label`, `LoaderRoot`, `SwitchRoot`)

## Related

`core-progress`

## README

A named loading status with eleven CSS animation variants. `Loader` replaces `Spinner`, and the Storybook owner is `Core/Loader`.

```jsx
import { Loader } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Loader';

<Loader variant='three-dots' size='md' label='Loading articles' />
```

- `variant`: `arc` (default), `dual-arc`, `bar`, `beat`, `bounce`, `circle-dots`, `clip`, `puff`, `three-dots`, `triangle`, or `two-dots`. These indicate an unknown wait; use `Progress` for measured completion.
- `size`: `xs` 12px, `sm` 16px, `md` 20px (default), or `lg` 32px. The bar is three times as wide as it is tall. Other variants are square. Intrinsic dimensions stay fixed across density presets.
- `label`: accessible status label, default `Loading`. Describe the active operation and provide visible status text where useful.
- `className`: use `text-current` to inherit surrounding color or a semantic tone such as `text-text-muted`. Explicit size utilities can override dimensions; preserve the bar's 3:1 ratio.
- SVG attributes and refs pass through. Set `aria-hidden='true'` when a button or containing region already announces the same state.

`LoaderRoot` is the composition primitive: the same variants, `sm` default, current text color, and `aria-label` instead of `label`. `loaderVariants` exports the supported names. All three are available from the root, `core`, and `core/Loader` entries; the leaf also has a default `Loader` export.

Reduced motion stops rotation, travel, scaling, and hopping. The indicator uses Gaudi's slow opacity breath while keeping its status label. The SVG/CSS implementation has no timers, and server rendering is deterministic. Unmount it when work finishes; the host owns loading state, cancellation, errors, and recovery.

Existing button, input, inline-status, overlay, and empty-state examples remain under Loader. Update `Spinner`, `SpinnerRoot`, and `core/Spinner` imports to `Loader`, `LoaderRoot`, and `core/Loader`. The Shadix UI reference informed the variant family; no remote animation code or assets are loaded.

# Map

> Core/Map · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Map`

An interactive geographic map with selectable markers, route lines, and camera controls. Powered by MapLibre; applications supply their own style, geography, and prepared data.

## Import

```js
import { Map } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Map';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Map`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mapStyle` | `MapLibre StyleSpecification \| string` | `required` | no | A stable style object or an application-configured style URL. Gaudi has no built-in map service, access token, geocoding, or routing endpoint. Memoize object styles. Changing the style preserves the camera. |
| `initialViewState` | `{ center: [longitude, latitude], zoom?, bearing?, pitch? }` | `{ center: [0, 0], zoom: 2 }` | no | Initial camera. Later changes use ref.flyTo, ref.fitBounds, or ref.reset. Coordinates always use longitude before latitude. |
| `markers` | `Array<{ id, coordinates, label, tone?, icon?, badge? }>` | `[]` | no | Stable unique IDs, [longitude, latitude] coordinates, and an accessible label. tone uses Button tones, icon is a React slot, and badge is optional visible metadata; include its meaning in label. |
| `selectedMarkerId` | `string \| number` | — | no | Controlled selection. Pointer and keyboard activation request a selection; the host chooses whether to accept it. Selection does not move the camera. |
| `onMarkerClick` | `(id) => void` | — | no | Controlled selection. Pointer and keyboard activation request a selection; the host chooses whether to accept it. Selection does not move the camera. |
| `routes` | `Array<{ id, coordinates, color?, width?, dashed? }>` | `[]` | no | Prepared line strings (at least two coordinates each). The app supplies color and status meaning. Defaults: blue, 3px, solid. Preserve attribution in your map style. |
| `label` | `string` | `Map` | no | Accessible name for the map region and keyboard canvas. |
| `controls` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Shows reset, zoom in, and zoom out controls when interactive. |
| `interactive` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Enables camera gestures and keyboard navigation. False disables those and hides camera controls; marker buttons remain selectable. |
| `scrollZoom` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Enables wheel zoom. Off by default so a map embedded in a page does not trap page scrolling. |
| `minZoom` | `number` | `0` | no | Camera zoom bounds. Changes clamp the current view without replacing the map. |
| `maxZoom` | `number` | `20` | no | Camera zoom bounds. Changes clamp the current view without replacing the map. |
| `onViewStateChange` | `(view) => void` | — | no | Camera movement completion, map readiness, and renderer/style/source errors. view includes center, zoom, bearing, and pitch. onViewStateChange reports state; it is not a controlled camera prop. |
| `onLoad` | `(view) => void` | — | no | Camera movement completion, map readiness, and renderer/style/source errors. view includes center, zoom, bearing, and pitch. onViewStateChange reports state; it is not a controlled camera prop. |
| `onError` | `(error) => void` | — | no | Camera movement completion, map readiness, and renderer/style/source errors. view includes center, zoom, bearing, and pitch. onViewStateChange reports state; it is not a controlled camera prop. |
| `ref` | `{ flyTo(view), fitBounds(bounds, options?), reset(), getViewState() }` | — | no | Imperative camera access after readiness. fitBounds accepts southwest/northeast coordinate pairs and optional MapLibre fit options. Camera motion honors reduced motion. getViewState returns null before mount. |
| `labels` | `{ loading?, unavailable?, retry?, zoomIn?, zoomOut?, reset? }` | `English labels` | no | Localized state and control text. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Bottom-left overlay content and custom unavailable-state content. Retry remains available. Keep overlay content concise and provide a textual alternative for important geographic information. |
| `fallback` | `ReactNode` | `location buttons` | no | Bottom-left overlay content and custom unavailable-state content. Retry remains available. Keep overlay content concise and provide a textual alternative for important geographic information. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` | — | no | Container styling, including height (default 32rem). The map follows its container size. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Usage

```jsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { Map } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Map';

const meeting = {
  id: 'meeting',
  coordinates: [-73.983, 40.7535],
  label: 'Bryant Park meeting point'
};

// Pass the host application's MapLibre style object or URL as mapStyle.
// Load @gaudi/design-system/styles.css once in the application's stylesheet entry.
export function MeetingMap({ mapStyle }) {
  const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState(null);

  return (
    <div>
      <Map
        label='Meeting location'
        mapStyle={mapStyle}
        initialViewState={{ center: meeting.coordinates, zoom: 15 }}
        markers={[meeting]}
        selectedMarkerId={selectedId}
        onMarkerClick={setSelectedId}
        style={{ height: '24rem' }}
      />
      <p>Bryant Park, 42nd Street and Sixth Avenue, New York.</p>
      {selectedId === meeting.id && (
        <p role='status'>Meet at the Sixth Avenue entrance.</p>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

The named region contains a focusable map canvas: arrows pan, plus/minus zoom. Marker buttons and controls work with Enter/Space and show focus. Selected markers expose aria-pressed. Browser touch gestures and reduced motion are supported. Geographic canvas content itself is not a screen-reader equivalent: provide a linked list or textual route summary, as the tracking example does.

## Notes

- Use an app-owned basemap and preserve the provider’s attribution. Style URLs, tiles, sprites, and glyphs are only requested when configured by the host. For local demos, the bundled NYC geometry and system fonts need no external services.
- The tracking story is a composition of Map, Button, Input, Select, Icon, and Pill. Vehicles and journeys are fictional, stored locally, and do not imply live tracking, traffic, or route calculation.
- Keep markers and route IDs stable. Updating coordinates moves the existing marker and preserves its button identity. Resource failures show a recoverable state with a list fallback; WebGL support is required to draw the map.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-map--playground`)
- Single location (Storybook `core-map--location`)
- Unavailable map & recovery (Storybook `core-map--recovery`)

## Related

`core-button`, `core-input`, `core-select`, `core-icon`, `core-pill`, `core-pointer`

## README

`Map` renders a host-supplied MapLibre style with selectable markers, route lines,
camera controls, and a recoverable unavailable state. Import it from the public
owner entry:

```jsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { Map } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Map';

const meeting = {
  id: 'meeting',
  coordinates: [-73.983, 40.7535],
  label: 'Bryant Park meeting point'
};

export function MeetingMap({ mapStyle }) {
  const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState(null);

  return (
    <div>
      <Map
        label='Meeting location'
        mapStyle={mapStyle}
        initialViewState={{ center: meeting.coordinates, zoom: 15 }}
        markers={[meeting]}
        selectedMarkerId={selectedId}
        onMarkerClick={setSelectedId}
        style={{ height: '24rem' }}
      />
      <p>Bryant Park, 42nd Street and Sixth Avenue, New York.</p>
      {selectedId === meeting.id && (
        <p role='status'>Meet at the Sixth Avenue entrance.</p>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

Pass your application's MapLibre style object or style URL as `mapStyle`. Keep
object styles stable, for example with a module constant or `useMemo`. Load
`@gaudi/design-system/styles.css` once in your application's stylesheet entry;
it already includes MapLibre's CSS.

### Data and application ownership

Coordinates always use `[longitude, latitude]`. Supply valid coordinates and
stable, unique string or number IDs. Keep each ID's type consistent across data,
selection, and callbacks. Updating a marker's coordinates moves its existing
button, preserving focus.

| Prop | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `mapStyle` | Required MapLibre style object or URL. Changing it preserves the current camera and reloads the style and overlays. |
| `markers` | Array of `{ id, coordinates, label, tone?, icon?, badge? }`; defaults to `[]`. `label` is the button's accessible name. `tone` uses Button tones and defaults to `accent`; `icon` accepts a React node and defaults to a map pin. |
| `selectedMarkerId` | Controlled selection. Match a marker ID exactly, or use `null` for no selection. |
| `onMarkerClick` | Receives the activated marker's ID, including activation from the fallback list. Update `selectedMarkerId` to accept the selection. |
| `routes` | Array of `{ id, coordinates, color?, width?, dashed? }`; defaults to `[]`. Each route needs at least two coordinate pairs. Defaults are `#2563eb`, `3` pixels, and a solid line. |

Selecting a marker does not change the camera. Focusing an offscreen marker brings
it into view. Routes are prepared line strings, without route calculation or
route selection. The host determines status labels, colors, filtering, selected
route emphasis, and any location details shown beside the map.

Gaudi supplies no basemap, provider endpoint, access token, geocoding, routing,
traffic, or tracking service. The application owns those integrations, data
updates, tiles, sprites, glyphs, and required attribution. Include attribution in
the supplied style's sources; the map shows MapLibre's compact attribution
control. Avoid the reserved source ID `gaudi-routes` and layer IDs
`gaudi-routes-solid` and `gaudi-routes-dashed` in your style.

Storybook's tracking, single-location, and recovery examples use local NYC
geography in `.storybook/public/static/maps` and fictional journey data. Those
assets are documentation fixtures and are not shipped in the npm package.

### Camera and events

| Prop | Default and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `initialViewState` | `{ center: [0, 0], zoom: 2 }`. Accepts `center`, `zoom`, `bearing`, and `pitch`. Applied on mount and retry; later prop changes do not move the camera. Reset uses the latest value. |
| `interactive` | `true`. Enables pan, zoom, and keyboard navigation. When false, camera gestures and controls are disabled; marker buttons remain selectable. |
| `controls` | `true`. Shows reset, zoom in, and zoom out while interactive. |
| `scrollZoom` | `false`. Opt in to wheel zoom when appropriate for the surrounding page. |
| `minZoom` / `maxZoom` | `0` / `20`. Updates clamp the current camera without replacing the map. |
| `onLoad` | Receives the view when the map is ready, and again after a replacement style becomes ready. |
| `onViewStateChange` | Receives the view after camera movement ends. This is a notification, not a controlled camera prop. |
| `onError` | Receives renderer, style, or source errors. The unavailable state handles recovery locally. |

Views have `{ center: [longitude, latitude], zoom, bearing, pitch }`. Attach a
React ref for explicit camera actions after `onLoad`:

| Ref method | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `flyTo(view)` | Moves to the supplied camera values. |
| `fitBounds(bounds, options?)` | Fits `[[west, south], [east, north]]`; accepts MapLibre fit options and defaults to `48` pixels of padding. |
| `reset()` | Returns to the latest `initialViewState`. |
| `getViewState()` | Returns the current view, or `null` before renderer initialization. |

Camera methods use a 600 ms transition, or no transition when reduced motion is
requested. Built-in zoom controls use 200 ms. Passing a duration does not override
these timings.

### Layout, accessibility, and recovery

The map fills its container width, defaults to `32rem` tall, and resizes with its
container. Use `style` or `className` to set the required height. `children` appear
in a bottom-left overlay while ready; keep legends and location cards concise so
they fit narrow containers and leave the attribution accessible.

Set `label` for the named map region and keyboard canvas; its default is `Map`.
Arrow keys pan, plus/minus zoom, and marker and control buttons support
Enter/Space. Selected markers expose `aria-pressed`. A marker's `badge` is visual
metadata hidden from assistive technology, so include its meaning in `label`
(for example, “TRK-208, 25 minutes delayed”).

Provide a visible list or textual summary for important locations and routes;
the geographic canvas is not a screen-reader equivalent. Use labels, icons, or
line patterns alongside status colors. Keep essential information outside
`children`, which is hidden during loading and failure.

While loading, the map announces its loading status. On error, it presents an
unavailable message, a selectable marker list, and a retry button. Supply
`fallback` to replace the list with application-specific content; retry remains
available. Retry rebuilds the renderer with the current style and initial view.
Replacing a failed style with a valid one also supports recovery. After recovery
from a focused fallback or retry button, focus moves to the map canvas.

Override state and control text with
`labels={{ loading, unavailable, retry, zoomIn, zoomOut, reset }}`. These keys
localize those messages and buttons; they do not replace the canvas keyboard
instructions or the controls group's accessible name.

The component imports MapLibre in a client effect, so server rendering does not
initialize WebGL. Drawing the map requires browser WebGL support. MapLibre is a
package dependency and uses its bundled worker; no custom worker setup or Vite
dependency exclusion is required. If the host enforces a Content Security Policy,
its worker policy must allow `blob:` workers and its resource policy must allow
the host's configured map resources.

## Accessibility

NavigationMenu renders a nav landmark, real links, native dropdown buttons, aria-expanded triggers, Escape-to-close behavior, outside-click dismissal, and aria-current for active links.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-navigationmenu--playground`)

Curated patterns:

- Blog menu with recent posts — registry item `@gaudi/navigation-menu-blog-recent-posts` (uses `NavigationMenu`, `NavigationMenuAside`, `NavigationMenuDropdown`, `NavigationMenuLink`, `NavigationMenuList`)
- Site header menu — registry item `@gaudi/navigation-menu-site-header` (uses `Button`, `NavigationMenuContent`, `NavigationMenuItemPrimitive`, `NavigationMenuLinkPrimitive`, `NavigationMenuListPrimitive`, `NavigationMenuRoot`, `NavigationMenuTrigger`, `RegistryIcon`, `navigationMenuTriggerStyle`)

## README

A site navigation bar with plain links and dropdown panels of related destinations. Use it for a header's primary navigation; use `DropdownMenu` for actions and `Tabs` for views within one page.

```jsx
import { NavigationMenu, NavigationMenuDropdown, NavigationMenuLink, NavigationMenuList, NavigationMenuPanel } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<NavigationMenu label='Main navigation'>
  <NavigationMenuList>
    <NavigationMenuLink href='/blog' active>Blog</NavigationMenuLink>
    <NavigationMenuDropdown label='Categories' align='start' width='lg'>
      <NavigationMenuPanel columns={2}>
        <NavigationMenuLink variant='panel' href='/blog/categories/data' description='Knowledge graphs and retrieval'>Data</NavigationMenuLink>
      </NavigationMenuPanel>
    </NavigationMenuDropdown>
  </NavigationMenuList>
</NavigationMenu>
```

Dropdowns open on click, close on Escape (focus returns to the trigger) or an outside click, and only one is open at a time. `align` and `width` place and size a panel, which is nudged back inside the viewport near an edge; `defaultOpen` starts one open. `active` marks the current page with `aria-current="page"`. Links close the open panel when followed.

The convenience components are built on the composition parts (`NavigationMenuRoot`, `NavigationMenuTrigger`, `NavigationMenuContent`, `NavigationMenuLinkPrimitive`, `NavigationMenuViewport`, `NavigationMenuIndicator`), which add hover-to-open and a shared animated viewport for custom menus.

For a two-block panel, pass `aside` to `NavigationMenuDropdown`: the children fill the first column and the aside the second (stacked below `sm`, `width='2xl'` gives both room). `NavigationMenuAside` is the usual second block, a muted column with a small title, an optional `action` (`{ href, label }` renders a "See all →" link) and its own links, labelled by its title for assistive technology.

```jsx
<NavigationMenuDropdown
  label='Blog'
  align='center'
  width='2xl'
  aside={
    <NavigationMenuAside title='Recent posts' action={{ href: '/blog', label: 'See all' }}>
      <ul>{posts.map((post) => <li key={post.slug}><NavigationMenuLink variant='panel' href={`/blog/${post.slug}`} description={post.date}>{post.title}</NavigationMenuLink></li>)}</ul>
    </NavigationMenuAside>
  }
>
  <ul>{categories.map((category) => <li key={category.id}><NavigationMenuLink variant='panel' href={category.href} description={category.description}>{category.title}</NavigationMenuLink></li>)}</ul>
</NavigationMenuDropdown>
```

## README

A numeric input with step buttons, for quantities, durations and prices within a known range. Use a Slider when an approximate value is enough.

### Usage

```jsx
import { NumberField, NumberFieldDecrement, NumberFieldGroup, NumberFieldIncrement, NumberFieldInput, NumberFieldScrubArea } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<NumberField defaultValue={5} min={0} max={10} step={1}>
  <NumberFieldScrubArea label='Articles per week' />
  <NumberFieldGroup>
    <NumberFieldDecrement aria-label='Decrease' />
    <NumberFieldInput />
    <NumberFieldIncrement aria-label='Increase' />
  </NumberFieldGroup>
</NumberField>;
```

`size` (`sm`, `default`, `lg`) sets the control height, and `format` takes `Intl.NumberFormat` options for units and currency.

Inside `Field`, the input automatically receives its label ID, description and error state. Use an explicit root `id` when composing primitive labels.

The editor is text-based, so it inherits `InputConfigProvider` smooth caret mode. Use `NumberFieldInput caretMode='native'` or `caretMode='smooth'` for an individual override. Prefer this component to `Input type='number'` when you need smooth caret movement with numeric bounds, stepping and formatting. The native number input does not expose its caret position.

### Accessibility

Arrow keys step the value, Home and End jump to `min` and `max`, and typed values clamp on blur. Give the step buttons an `aria-label`.

## Related

`core-item`, `core-link`

## README

Moves between pages of a long list. Use `PaginationBar` under a post archive or search results; compose the parts for numbered, compact or table-footer pagers.

```jsx
import { PaginationBar } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<PaginationBar currentPage={3} totalPages={8} getHref={(page) => `/blog/page/${page}`} />
```

`PaginationBar` shows Previous, an "n of total" status and Next. Previous and Next disable at either end; clicking the status or pressing Enter or Space opens page shortcuts, with ellipses past five pages. Pass `onPageChange` for client-side paging: page links become buttons and the host owns `currentPage`. `label` names the landmark; `previousLabel`, `nextLabel`, `ofLabel` and `shortcutsLabel` (also on `PaginationStatus`) translate the remaining copy, defaulting to Previous, Next, of and Page shortcuts.

The parts (`Pagination`, `PaginationContent`, `PaginationItem`, `PaginationLink`, `PaginationPrevious`, `PaginationNext`, `PaginationEllipsis`) are built on `Button`: `PaginationLink` is a router-aware link with `href`, a button with `onClick`, or a disabled button with `disabled`, and `isActive` marks the current page with `aria-current="page"`.

# Pill

> Core/Pill · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Pill`

Pill renders compact category and status labels.

## Import

```js
import Pill from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Pill';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Badge`, `BadgeRoot`, `badgeVariants`, `badgeVariantsPrimitive`, `default`, `pillSizes`, `pillTones`, `pillVariants`

## When to use

- Use Pill for compact metadata, tags, filters, and status labels.
- Keep the visible label as the source of meaning; color only supports scanning.
- Use the Badge `discovery` variants for suggested or machine-generated labels and `attention` for items that need a person to look, such as staged or unreviewed records; each has solid, `-light` and `-outline` treatments.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Visible category, status, or tag label. |
| `size` | `xs \| sm \| md \| lg` | `md` | no | Controls padding and text size. |
| `tone` | `gray \| neutral \| blue \| teal \| green \| amber \| yellow \| red \| rose \| indigo` | `blue` | no | Semantic tone alias mapped through Gaudi tokens rather than raw palette utilities. |
| `variant` | `solid \| soft \| outline \| ghost \| subtle` | `solid` | no | Visual treatment. |
| `radius` | `sm \| md \| full` | `sm` | no | Legacy aliases use the global --ds-radius setting (4px by default); none stays square where supported. |
| `href` | `string` | — | no | Renders the pill as a navigation link. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Decorative leading icon. |
| `pulse` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Adds a pulsing status dot. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Root class override. |

## Variants

- `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`
- `tone`: `gray`, `neutral`, `blue`, `teal`, `green`, `amber`, `yellow`, `red`, `rose`, `indigo`
- `variant`: `solid`, `soft`, `outline`, `ghost`, `subtle`
- `radius`: `sm`, `md`, `full`

## Usage

```jsx
import { Pill } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Pill tone='blue' variant='solid' size='sm'>Engineering</Pill>
```

## Accessibility

Pill includes visible text so status or category meaning is not color-only.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-pill--playground`)
- Tones (Storybook `core-pill--tones`)
- Semantic Badges (Storybook `core-pill--semantic-badges`)

Curated patterns:

- Icons, dots, avatars and images — registry item `@gaudi/badge-icons-avatars` (uses `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarRoot`, `Badge`, `RegistryIcon`)
- Removable filters and links — registry item `@gaudi/badge-removable-filters` (uses `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarRoot`, `Badge`, `Button`, `RegistryIcon`)
- Sizes, counts and labels — registry item `@gaudi/badge-sizes-counts` (uses `Badge`)
- Variants — registry item `@gaudi/badge-variants` (uses `Badge`)

## README

A small label for a status, category, tag or count. Use `Pill` when you want a named tone (`blue`, `green`, `amber`…) with a
`variant` for emphasis; use `Badge` when you compose with the semantic variants (`success-light`, `destructive-outline`…).
Both render the same Badge element, and Pill tones read from the shared Button tone scale, so they switch with the theme.

```jsx
import { Badge, Pill } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Pill tone='green' variant='soft' size='sm' pulse>Live</Pill>
<Pill href='/blog/tags/tokens' tone='gray' variant='soft'>#tokens</Pill>
<Badge variant='success-light'>Shipped</Badge>
<Badge variant='discovery-light'>Suggested</Badge>
<Badge variant='attention-light'>Needs review</Badge>
```

- `tone`: `blue` (default), `green`, `amber`, `red`, `indigo`, `teal`, `rose`, `neutral`, `gray`; `yellow` is an alias of `amber`.
- `variant`: `solid` (default), `soft`, `outline`, `ghost`, `subtle`. `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md` (default), `lg`. `radius`: `sm` (default), `md`, `full`.
- `href` renders a link with a comfortable hit target; `icon` adds a decorative leading icon; `pulse` adds a decorative live dot, so keep the meaning in the text.
- `Badge` variants: `default`, `secondary`, `outline`, and the semantic `info`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`,
  `discovery`, `attention`, `focus`, `invert`, each with `-light` and `-outline` treatments (`primary-light`/`primary-outline` too).
  Use `discovery` for suggested or generated labels (for example tags proposed by an assistant) and `attention` for records
  that need a person to look (staged, unreviewed). They read from the `--ds-color-discovery*` and `--ds-color-attention*` tokens.
- `BadgeRoot` and `badgeVariantsPrimitive` are kept as aliases of `Badge` and `badgeVariants`.
