# Pointer

> Core/Pointer · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Pointer`

A pointer effect scoped to its container, with direct, spring and lazy tracking, hover feedback, and native input fallbacks.

## Import

```js
import { Pointer } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Pointer';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Pointer`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `dot \| ring \| frame \| label` | `frame` | no | Follower appearance. Ring and frame keep a precise dot at the actual pointer; label places a hint beside it. |
| `tracking` | `direct \| spring \| lazy` | `lazy` | no | Immediate movement, a responsive spring, or a slower trailing frame. |
| `tone` | `neutral \| accent` | `neutral` | no | Theme-aware foreground or accent color. |
| `label` | `string` | `Explore` | no | Default label for the label variant. A descendant data-pointer-label overrides it while hovered. |
| `hideCursor` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Hides the native cursor only while the effect is active inside this container. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Turns off the decorative effect. Descendant controls stay usable. |
| `data-pointer-native` | `HTML attribute on descendants` | — | no | Opt any subtree into the native cursor, for example selectable article text. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Content composed from the exported parts. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `variant`: `dot`, `ring`, `frame`, `label`
- `tracking`: `direct`, `spring`, `lazy`
- `tone`: `neutral`, `accent`

## Usage

```jsx
import { Pointer, Button } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Pointer variant='frame' tracking='lazy' className='min-h-80 p-8'>
  <Button>Explore work</Button>
</Pointer>
```

## Accessibility

The overlay is aria-hidden and never captures pointer events. Touch, pen, reduced motion, editable fields, keyboard use, and disabled effects retain the native cursor. Give every action its normal visible label; pointer text is supplementary. No global cursor styles are changed.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-pointer--playground`)
- Direct, spring and lazy (Storybook `core-pointer--tracking`)
- Contextual labels (Storybook `core-pointer--labels`)
- Inputs and native fallbacks (Storybook `core-pointer--native-fallbacks`)

## README

A decorative pointer scoped to a container. It supplies direct, spring, and lazy tracking with dot, ring, corner-frame, and contextual-label variants.

```jsx
import { Pointer, Button } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Pointer variant='frame' tracking='lazy' className='min-h-80 p-8'>
  <Button>Explore work</Button>
</Pointer>
```

Also available from `@gaudi/design-system/core/Pointer`. Load Gaudi's stylesheet once. `tone` is `neutral` or `accent`; `hideCursor={false}` keeps the native cursor beside the effect. `disabled` turns off the decoration without disabling the content. The forwarded ref and DOM props belong to the container. A cancelled pointer enter/move handler prevents that event from moving the follower.

For `variant='label'`, supply a default `label` and optional `data-pointer-label='View project'` on individual targets. Keep a visible accessible label on each action; the pointer label is only a decoration. Set `data-pointer-native` on selectable text or any region that should retain its native cursor. Inputs, textareas, selects, and editable content do this automatically.

The follower appears only after a real mouse enters. Touch, pen, reduced motion, window blur, scrolling, and keyboard use hide it and restore the native cursor. The overlay is clipped to its container, is hidden from assistive technology, and never intercepts clicks. Springs settle when movement stops and are stopped on exit; listeners are cleaned up on unmount. Nested followers have independent scopes.

The lazy frame revisits the dot-and-corner-frame behavior of an earlier website cursor by the same author. The motion references are [Asterisk](https://www.withasterisk.com/) and [Skiper UI's mouse-follow examples](https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper61). Gaudi uses its existing Motion dependency, shared hooks, icons, and tokens; no Skiper or Asterisk source or remote assets are included.

---

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |

| `open` | `boolean` | — | no | Controlled or initial open state, and whether outside content is inert while open. |

## Usage

## Accessibility

The trigger is a DS button with aria-expanded; the panel is portalled, dismisses on Escape or an outside click, and returns focus to the trigger. Keep popover content short and non-modal.

- Settings form — registry item `@gaudi/popover-settings-form` (uses `Button`, `FieldGroup`, `FieldInput`, `FieldLabelPrimitive`, `FieldRoot`, `PopoverContentPrimitive`, `PopoverDescription`, `PopoverHeader`, `PopoverPrimitive`, `PopoverTitle`, `PopoverTriggerPrimitive`, `RegistryIcon`, `Slider`, `SwitchRoot`)

## README

A button that opens a small, non-modal panel for supporting content: share settings, quick filters, a short form. Use a hover card for read-only previews that open on hover, and a Dialog when the task needs the user's full attention.

### Usage

```jsx
import { Popover } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Popover trigger='Share' side='bottom' align='start'>
  <PopoverHeader>
    <PopoverTitle>Share this draft</PopoverTitle>
    <PopoverDescription>Anyone with the link can view.</PopoverDescription>
  </PopoverHeader>
</Popover>
```

### API

| Prop                                         | Type                            | Contract                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `trigger`                                    | ReactNode                       | Content of the outline button that opens the panel.       |
| `children`                                   | ReactNode                       | Panel content.                                            |
| `side / align`                               | top, right, bottom, left / start, center, end | Preferred placement; collisions may flip it. |
| `open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange / modal`  | boolean / boolean / function / boolean | Controlled or initial visibility.                  |
| `className / contentClassName`               | string                          | Classes for the trigger button and the panel.             |

### Composition

`@gaudi/design-system/core/Popover` exports the compound parts: `Popover`, `PopoverTrigger`, `PopoverContent`, `PopoverAnchor`, `PopoverHeader`, `PopoverTitle`, `PopoverDescription`, and `HoverCard`, `HoverCardTrigger`, `HoverCardContent`. From the package root the parts are `PopoverPrimitive`, `PopoverTriggerPrimitive` and `PopoverContentPrimitive`, because `Popover` there is the convenience component.

### Accessibility

The trigger is a native button with `aria-expanded`. Escape and a click outside close the panel and return focus to the trigger. Keep the content short; move long forms into a Dialog.

# Progress

> Core/Progress · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Progress`

Determinate and indeterminate progress with a readable task label.

## Import

```js
import Progress from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Progress';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `ProgressRing`, `ProgressRoot`, `default`, `normalizeProgress`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | — | no | Accessible name of the progress indicator. |
| `value` | `number` | — | no | Completed amount; omit for indeterminate progress. |
| `max` | `number` | `100` | no | Total amount. |
| `valueText` | `string` | — | no | Human-readable progress such as 3 of 8 files. |
| `tone` | `accent \| success \| warning \| danger` | `accent` | no | Status color. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `tone`: `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`

## Usage

```jsx
import Progress from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Progress';

<Progress value={completed} max={total} label='Upload progress' />
```

## Accessibility

Provide a task label and meaningful value text. Avoid announcing every small progress update.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-progress--playground`)
- Indeterminate (Storybook `core-progress--indeterminate`)
- Progress ring (Storybook `core-progress--ring`)

Curated patterns:

- Multi-step — registry item `@gaudi/progress-multi-step` (uses `ProgressRoot`, `RegistryIcon`)
- Sizes and colors — registry item `@gaudi/progress-sizes-colors` (uses `ProgressRoot`, `Slider`)
- Status messages — registry item `@gaudi/progress-status-messages` (uses `ProgressRoot`)
- File upload list — registry item `@gaudi/progress-upload-list` (uses `Item`, `ItemContent`, `ItemGroup`, `ItemMedia`, `ItemTitle`, `ProgressRoot`, `RegistryIcon`)

## README

A progress bar for one task. `Progress` adds a label and an optional value text to the `ProgressRoot` bar; use
`ProgressRoot` on its own when the label lives elsewhere (a stepper, a series box, a file row).

```jsx
import Progress, { ProgressRoot } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Progress';

<Progress label='Uploading references' value={31} max={50} valueText='31 of 50 files' tone='accent' />
<ProgressRoot value={62} aria-label='Series progress' />
```

- `value` is clamped between 0 and a finite positive `max` (default 100). Omit it when the amount of work is unknown: the bar
  stays indeterminate instead of inventing a percentage, and stays still for reduced motion.
- `valueText` is shown beside the label and announced as the value; `tone` is `accent`, `success`, `warning` or `danger`.
- The bar is a `progressbar` named by the label, with `aria-valuenow` and `aria-valuemax`.

### Progress ring

`ProgressRing` is the circular form for compact places such as board cards and table cells. It carries the same
`progressbar` semantics as the bar: pass `label` (or `aria-labelledby`), `value`, `max`, an optional `valueText`, a
`tone` (accent, info, success, warning, danger, discovery, attention, neutral) and a `size` (xs, sm, md, lg). `showValue`
prints the percentage in the centre at md and lg.

```jsx
import { ProgressRing } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<ProgressRing value={58} tone='success' label='BUG-452 completion' />
```

# Questionnaire

> Core/Questionnaire · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Questionnaire`

A sequence of form questions with selection, validation and progress.

## Import

```js
import { Questionnaire } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Questionnaire';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Questionnaire`, `QuestionnaireActions`, `QuestionnaireChoice`, `QuestionnaireChoiceDescription`, `QuestionnaireChoices`, `QuestionnaireDescription`, `QuestionnaireError`, `QuestionnaireInput`, `QuestionnaireItem`, `QuestionnaireNext`, `QuestionnairePrevious`, `QuestionnaireProgress`, `QuestionnaireSkip`, `QuestionnaireSubmit`, `QuestionnaireTitle`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `item / defaultItem / onItemChange` | `string / function` | — | no | Controlled or initial active question. |
| `onSubmit / onReset` | `FormEventHandler` | — | no | Native form submission and reset. |
| `shortcuts` | `QuestionnaireShortcutMode` | — | no | Keyboard shortcut mode. |
| `QuestionnaireItem.name` | `string` | `Required` | no | Question field name. |
| `QuestionnaireItem.multiple / required / invalid` | `boolean` | — | no | Selection and validation constraints. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Content composed from the exported parts. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { Questionnaire, QuestionnaireItem, QuestionnaireTitle, QuestionnaireInput, QuestionnaireActions, QuestionnaireSubmit } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Questionnaire';
```

## Accessibility

Question titles render as legends. Keep validation beside the question and ensure Previous, Next and Submit have clear names.

## Examples

Curated patterns:

- Answer types — registry item `@gaudi/questionnaire-answer-types` (uses `Badge`, `Button`, `CardContent`, `CardDescription`, `CardFooter`, `CardHeader`, `CardRoot`, `CardTitle`, `Label`, `Questionnaire`, `QuestionnaireActions`, `QuestionnaireChoice`, `QuestionnaireChoiceDescription`, `QuestionnaireChoices`, `QuestionnaireError`, `QuestionnaireInput`, `QuestionnaireItem`, `QuestionnaireNext`, `QuestionnairePrevious`, `QuestionnaireProgress`, `QuestionnaireSkip`, `QuestionnaireSubmit`, `QuestionnaireTitle`)
- Conditional branch — registry item `@gaudi/questionnaire-conditional-branch` (uses `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarRoot`, `Button`, `CardAction`, `CardContent`, `CardDescription`, `CardFooter`, `CardHeader`, `CardRoot`, `CardTitle`, `Questionnaire`, `QuestionnaireActions`, `QuestionnaireChoice`, `QuestionnaireChoiceDescription`, `QuestionnaireChoices`, `QuestionnaireDescription`, `QuestionnaireError`, `QuestionnaireItem`, `QuestionnaireNext`, `QuestionnairePrevious`, `QuestionnaireProgress`, `QuestionnaireSubmit`, `QuestionnaireTitle`, `RegistryIcon`, `cn`)
- Cross-question validation — registry item `@gaudi/questionnaire-cross-validation` (uses `Button`, `CardAction`, `CardContent`, `CardDescription`, `CardFooter`, `CardHeader`, `CardRoot`, `CardTitle`, `Questionnaire`, `QuestionnaireActions`, `QuestionnaireChoice`, `QuestionnaireChoices`, `QuestionnaireDescription`, `QuestionnaireError`, `QuestionnaireItem`, `QuestionnaireNext`, `QuestionnairePrevious`, `QuestionnaireProgress`, `QuestionnaireSubmit`, `QuestionnaireTitle`)
- Guided setup — registry item `@gaudi/questionnaire-guided-setup` (uses `Button`, `CardContent`, `CardDescription`, `CardFooter`, `CardHeader`, `CardRoot`, `CardTitle`, `Questionnaire`, `QuestionnaireActions`, `QuestionnaireChoice`, `QuestionnaireChoiceDescription`, `QuestionnaireChoices`, `QuestionnaireDescription`, `QuestionnaireError`, `QuestionnaireItem`, `QuestionnaireNext`, `QuestionnairePrevious`, `QuestionnaireProgress`, `QuestionnaireSubmit`, `QuestionnaireTitle`, `cn`)

## README

A form that shows one question at a time, with progress, keyboard shortcuts for choices, validation and Previous, Skip, Next and Submit actions. Use it for onboarding, surveys and guided setup; use a plain form when people need to see every field at once.

```jsx
import { Questionnaire, QuestionnaireProgress, QuestionnaireItem, QuestionnaireTitle, QuestionnaireChoices, QuestionnaireChoice, QuestionnaireError, QuestionnaireActions, QuestionnairePrevious, QuestionnaireNext, QuestionnaireSubmit } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Questionnaire items={items} onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
  <QuestionnaireProgress />
  <QuestionnaireItem name='goal' required>
    <QuestionnaireTitle>What brings you here?</QuestionnaireTitle>
    <QuestionnaireChoices>
      <QuestionnaireChoice value='system'>Build a design system</QuestionnaireChoice>
    </QuestionnaireChoices>
    <QuestionnaireError />
  </QuestionnaireItem>
  <QuestionnaireActions>
    <QuestionnairePrevious />
    <QuestionnaireNext />
    <QuestionnaireSubmit />
  </QuestionnaireActions>
</Questionnaire>
```

- `QuestionnaireItem multiple` turns choices into checkboxes; `QuestionnaireInput` takes a written answer; `QuestionnaireSkip` appears on optional questions.
- `shortcuts` labels choices with `letters` or `numbers`; `defaultItem` / `onItemChange` control the active question.
- The actions are Button-styled: Previous and Skip are neutral outlines, Next and Submit are filled. Pass `variant` or `size` to change them.

### Accessibility

Each question is a fieldset, choices are native radios or checkboxes, and the progress is a labelled progress bar. Hidden questions are inert, so focus and screen readers only reach the active one.

# RadioGroup

```jsx
import { RadioGroup } from '@gaudi/design-system';
```

- Review summary — registry item `@gaudi/rating-review-summary` (uses `ProgressRoot`, `Rating`, `Separator`)

## README

Shows a score as stars, or lets people choose one. Use it for reviews and feedback.

### Usage

```jsx
import { Rating } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Rating rating={4.5} showValue />
<Rating rating={score} editable onRatingChange={setScore} />;
```

`size` is `sm`, `default` or `lg`, `maxRating` sets the number of stars, and `starClassName` restyles the stars.

### Accessibility

A read-only rating is one image named "Rated 4.5 out of 5". An editable rating is a radio group: arrow keys move and select, Home and End jump to the ends.

# ReadingIndicator

> Core/ReadingIndicator · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/ReadingIndicator`

Reading progress as a classic top bar, a vertical ruler with a moving percentage, or a movable circular meter.

## Import

```js
import { ReadingIndicator } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ReadingIndicator';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `ReadingIndicator`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `bar \| ruler \| ring` | `bar` | no | A thin horizontal bar, a vertical tick scale, or a compact circular meter. |
| `position` | `fixed \| absolute \| inline` | `fixed` | no | Fixed to the viewport, anchored inside a positioned parent, or placed in normal layout. Bar sits at the top; ruler at the end edge; ring at the bottom end. |
| `targetRef` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` | `window` | no | Ref to a scrolling element or a Gaudi ScrollArea root. Omit to track the document. |
| `contentRef` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` | `whole scroll range` | no | Optional article inside the scroll target. Starts when its top reaches the viewport top; finishes when its bottom comes into view. |
| `value` | `number (0–100)` | `automatic` | no | Supply an external reading percentage to bypass scroll tracking. Clamped to 0–100; non-finite values become 0. |
| `tone` | `accent \| neutral` | `accent` | no | Accent or foreground marks, adapted to the current theme. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` | `false for bar; true otherwise` | no | Shows the percentage next to the indicator. |
| `label` | `string` | `Reading progress` | no | Accessible name for the progressbar. aria-labelledby can name it from an existing heading. |
| `draggable` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Adds a movement handle to a fixed or absolute ring. Arrow keys move it; Home or Escape resets it. |
| `dragBoundsRef` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` | `viewport` | no | Constrains the movable ring to this container. Set it for a ring positioned inside a panel. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `variant`: `bar`, `ruler`, `ring`
- `position`: `fixed`, `absolute`, `inline`
- `tone`: `accent`, `neutral`

## Usage

```jsx
import { ReadingIndicator } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ReadingIndicator';

// Render once near the page root.
<ReadingIndicator />
```

## Accessibility

Exposes a named progressbar without live announcements on every scroll. The indicator does not capture scrolling or text selection; only the optional ring handle receives input. Reduced motion removes the number transition. Progress measures scroll position, not comprehension.

## Notes

- Resizes and content growth are measured automatically. A non-scrollable document is complete (100%); an unresolved target starts at 0%.
- Reserve a side gutter for the ruler and room for the ring so they do not cover reading text. Set style.top to place a fixed bar below a site header. For a top bar with no extra configuration, render <ReadingIndicator /> once in the page.
- The ruler and ring are independently implemented interpretations of the Skiper UI scroll progress references; no remote assets or registry code are loaded.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-readingindicator--playground`)
- Bar, ruler and ring (Storybook `core-readingindicator--styles`)
- Article range (Storybook `core-readingindicator--article`)
- Top of page (Storybook `core-readingindicator--page`)

## Related

`core-progress`, `core-scrollarea`

## README

Track reading position with a top bar, vertical ruler, or circular meter.

```jsx
import { ReadingIndicator } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ReadingIndicator';

<ReadingIndicator />
```

The default bar is fixed to the top of the page. Set `style={{ top: 64 }}` to clear a fixed header. `variant='ruler'` sits at the end edge; `variant='ring'` sits at the bottom end. Both show a percentage by default. `tone` accepts `accent` or `neutral`.

Pass `targetRef` for a scrolling element or a Gaudi `ScrollArea` root. Inside a panel, use `position='absolute'` and a positioned parent; `position='inline'` leaves placement to the host. Reserve a gutter for the ruler and space for the ring so they do not obscure text.

`contentRef` restricts progress to an article inside the scroll target: 0% when its top reaches the top of the viewport, 100% when its bottom comes into view. Related content is excluded. A fully visible, non-scrollable range is complete. Missing refs remain at 0%. Resizes and dynamic content update the range.

For externally measured progress, set `value` (0–100). Values are clamped; non-finite values become 0. Automatic scroll tracking is suspended while `value` is supplied.

`draggable` gives the ring a handle. `dragBoundsRef` constrains it to a panel; otherwise it stays within the viewport. Arrow keys move by 10px, Shift by 40px; Home or Escape resets it. Inline meters are not draggable. The handle is the only pointer-interactive part.

Use `label` or `aria-labelledby` to name the progressbar. No live region announces every scroll. Reduced motion disables the number transition. Progress describes position, not reading comprehension. The ref and DOM props belong to the outer container.

Visual references: [Skiper UI scroll progress 003](https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper95) and [scroll progress 001](https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper89). This implementation composes Gaudi progress primitives and Motion; it does not copy registry source or load remote resources.

# SchemaDisplay

Read an API endpoint or a JSON Schema: method badge, path with highlighted parameters, and request and response schemas as an expandable property tree.

```js
import SchemaDisplay from '@gaudi/design-system/core/SchemaDisplay';
```

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | `string` | — | no | Endpoint verb and path; {id} and :id parameters are highlighted. |
| `path` | `string` | — | no | Endpoint verb and path; {id} and :id parameters are highlighted. |
| `title / description` | `ReactNode` | — | no | A name for a bare schema and a summary line. |
| `parameters` | `Array<{ name, in, type?, schema?, required?, description? }>` | `[]` | no | Path, query and header parameters; path parameters are always required. |
| `requestBody / responseBody / schema` | `JSONSchema` | — | no | Schemas read as trees: type, format, required, description, enum, items and oneOf. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { SchemaDisplay } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<SchemaDisplay
  method='GET'
  path='/posts/{slug}/comments'
  parameters={[{ name: 'slug', in: 'path', type: 'string' }, { name: 'limit', in: 'query', type: 'integer' }]}
  responseBody={commentsSchema}
/>
```

## Accessibility

Sections are real headings at headingLevel. Nested objects are disclosure buttons with aria-expanded; required is written out, never colour alone, and parameter highlights keep their braces.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-schemadisplay--playground`)

## Related

`core-codeblock`

## README

An API endpoint or a JSON Schema as a reference card: the method badge, the path with its parameters highlighted, and the parameters, request body and response as an expandable property tree with types, formats, enums, required markers and descriptions.

It lives in Core rather than Chat because API reference is as common in blog posts and app settings as it is in a tool result. In a chat, render it inside a reply or as `ChatMessageTool` output.

### Usage

```jsx
import { SchemaDisplay } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<SchemaDisplay
  method='GET'
  path='/posts/{slug}/comments'
  parameters={[
    { name: 'slug', in: 'path', type: 'string' },
    { name: 'limit', in: 'query', type: 'integer', description: 'At most 50.' }
  ]}
  responseBody={commentsSchema}
  showJson
/>

<SchemaDisplay title='Comment' schema={commentSchema} defaultExpandDepth={2} />
```

### API

| Prop / part | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `method` / `path` | Endpoint verb (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE colour-coded) and path; `{id}` and `:id` are highlighted. |
| `parameters` | `{ name, in, type?, schema?, required?, description? }`; path parameters are always required. |
| `requestBody` / `responseBody` / `schema` | Plain JSON Schema: `type`, `properties`, `required`, `items`, `enum`, `format`, `description`, `oneOf`/`anyOf`. |
| `defaultExpandDepth` | Levels of nested objects that start open (default 1). |
| `showJson` | Adds a Schema / JSON toggle with the raw definition in `CodeBlock`. |
| `headingLevel` | Heading level of the section titles (default 3). |
| `SchemaDisplayMethod`, `SchemaDisplayPath`, `SchemaDisplayProperties` | The badge, the path and the property tree on their own. |

It reads schemas only. Fetching, `$ref` resolution and validation stay in the app.

### Accessibility

Section titles are real headings. Nested objects open from disclosure buttons with `aria-expanded`. "required" is written out rather than shown by colour, and highlighted path parameters keep their braces.

# ScrollArea

> Core/ScrollArea · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/ScrollArea`

Contained scrolling with themed scrollbars and optional smooth wheel motion for article reading.

## Import

```js
import { ScrollArea } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ScrollArea';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `ScrollArea`, `ScrollBar`, `ScrollEdges`, `SmoothScroll`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `auto \| always \| scroll \| hover` | `hover` | no | Scrollbar visibility behavior. |
| `smooth` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Enhances vertical mouse-wheel scrolling with Lenis. Touch, keyboard, focus, links and reduced motion retain native behavior. The engine loads only when requested and pauses when the area or page is hidden. |
| `fadeEdges` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Blurs the top and bottom edges while more content continues past them. Decorative: hidden during keyboard focus, for reduced motion and in forced colours. |
| `ScrollEdges.targetRef` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` | `page` | no | The same edges for any scroll boundary: an element, or the page when targetRef is omitted. offsetTop keeps the page top edge below a sticky header; range is the distance in pixels at which an edge reaches full strength. |
| `offsetTop` | `number` | `0` | no | The same edges for any scroll boundary: an element, or the page when targetRef is omitted. offsetTop keeps the page top edge below a sticky header; range is the distance in pixels at which an edge reaches full strength. |
| `range` | `number` | `80` | no | The same edges for any scroll boundary: an element, or the page when targetRef is omitted. offsetTop keeps the page top edge below a sticky header; range is the distance in pixels at which an edge reaches full strength. |
| `edges` | `both \| top \| bottom` | `both` | no | The same edges for any scroll boundary: an element, or the page when targetRef is omitted. offsetTop keeps the page top edge below a sticky header; range is the distance in pixels at which an edge reaches full strength. |
| `SmoothScroll.targetRef` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` | `page` | no | Eased wheel scrolling for any scroll boundary; omit targetRef to smooth the page. ScrollArea smooth uses it for its own viewport. |
| `viewportRef` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` | — | no | Ref to the actual scrolling viewport. Share with ReadingIndicator.targetRef, a heading observer or native scrollTo calls. The ordinary ref still points to the outer root. |
| `scrollbarClassName` | `{ track?: string, thumb?: string }` | — | no | Classes for the built-in vertical scrollbar track and thumb, using Gaudi tokens. |
| `ScrollBar.orientation` | `horizontal \| vertical` | `vertical` | no | Axis of an additional scrollbar. Smooth wheel motion applies to the vertical viewport; horizontal regions remain native. |
| `ScrollBar.thumbClassName` | `string` | — | no | Classes for a separately composed scrollbar thumb. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Content composed from the exported parts. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `type`: `auto`, `always`, `scroll`, `hover`
- `edges`: `both`, `top`, `bottom`

## Usage

```jsx
import { ScrollArea } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ScrollArea';

<ScrollArea smooth className='h-[32rem]' aria-label='Blog post content'>{article}</ScrollArea>
```

## Accessibility

Give the viewport a useful accessible name using aria-label or aria-labelledby. Constrain the area dimensions and retain keyboard access. Reduced motion skips the smooth engine entirely; native scrolling remains available before hydration or if the enhancement cannot load. Nested scrollable content keeps its own wheel behavior.

## Notes

- A page that scrolls as a whole, such as a blog post between a site header and footer, keeps native page scrolling and uses ScrollEdges without targetRef for the same blurred edges. Use a bounded ScrollArea when the reading area is the only scroller, as in the Article examples.
- Smooth scrolling is an enhancement to the existing ScrollArea owner, not a second global page scroller. Bound the height, including min-h-0 when using a flex layout. Avoid stacking a second document-wide smoothing engine around it.
- Native fragment links, keyboard scrolling, focus, text selection and touch retain browser behavior. Pointer and keyboard intent interrupt any pending wheel inertia. Code, tables and other nested scroll regions scroll natively.
- Theme the track and thumb through scrollbarClassName. Keep enough contrast and an adequate hit area. Use ScrollBar with orientation="horizontal" for content that deliberately overflows horizontally.
- Inspired by Shadix UI Smooth Scroll Area. Gaudi composes its existing Radix viewport with the packaged Lenis engine; it does not load remote scripts or copy registry source.

## Examples

- Smooth blog reading (Storybook `core-scrollarea--smooth-reading`)
- Playground (Storybook `core-scrollarea--playground`)

Curated patterns:

- Horizontal gallery — registry item `@gaudi/scroll-area-horizontal-gallery` (uses `ScrollArea`, `ScrollBar`, `cn`)
- Wide table — registry item `@gaudi/scroll-area-wide-table` (uses `ScrollArea`, `ScrollBar`, `TableBodyPrimitive`, `TableCellPrimitive`, `TableHeadPrimitive`, `TableHeader`, `TableRoot`, `TableRowPrimitive`)

## Related

`blocks-blog-article`, `core-pointer`, `mdx-code`, `core-readingindicator`

## README

A keyboard-accessible Radix scroll viewport with themed scrollbars. Enable `smooth` for eased vertical mouse-wheel scrolling through the locally installed Lenis engine.

```jsx
'use client';

import { useRef } from 'react';
import { ScrollArea } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ScrollArea';
import { ReadingIndicator } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ReadingIndicator';

export function ArticleReader({ children }) {
  const viewport = useRef(null);
  return (
    <div className='relative min-h-0'>
      <ScrollArea smooth viewportRef={viewport} className='h-[calc(100dvh-4rem)]' aria-label='Blog post content'>
        <article className='mx-auto max-w-prose px-5 py-8'>{children}</article>
      </ScrollArea>
      <ReadingIndicator targetRef={viewport} position='absolute' />
    </div>
  );
}
```

- `smooth` defaults to `false`. `true` adds wheel interpolation, with native scrolling available before hydration and if the enhancement cannot load. It applies to vertical wheel movement, not CSS scroll snapping or a document-wide smooth-scroll engine.
- `viewportRef` receives the actual scrolling element; `ref` receives the outer root. Use native `scrollTo`, or share the viewport with reading progress and heading observers.
- `type` controls scrollbar visibility: `hover` (default), `auto`, `always`, or `scroll`.
- `scrollbarClassName={{ track, thumb }}` styles the built-in vertical scrollbar. For example, `{ thumb: 'bg-accent/60' }` uses the active accent. `ScrollBar` also accepts `thumbClassName` and `orientation='horizontal'`.
- Give the region an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Set a bounded height, and use `min-h-0` on flex parents so the content scrolls inside the area.

Touch, keyboard scrolling, native fragment links, focus, selection, and scrollbar dragging retain their browser behavior. Nested scroll regions keep their own wheel interaction. Pointer, keyboard and focus intent interrupt wheel inertia. Reduced motion skips Lenis entirely; changing the preference takes effect without a reload. The engine is destroyed while the area is offscreen or the page is hidden, and on unmount, releasing its listeners, observers and animation frame.

### Faded edges

`fadeEdges` blurs the top and bottom of the viewport while more content continues past them. `ScrollEdges` is the same effect for any scroll boundary: pass `targetRef`, or omit it for the page, with `offsetTop` to keep the top edge below a sticky header, and `edges='bottom'` (or `'top'`) to blur only one edge.

```jsx
import { ScrollArea, ScrollEdges } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ScrollArea';

<ScrollArea smooth fadeEdges className='h-[32rem]' aria-label='Blog post content'>{article}</ScrollArea>
<ScrollEdges offsetTop={64} />
```

`SmoothScroll` is the same eased wheel scrolling for the page: render `<SmoothScroll />` once on a reading page that scrolls as a whole. Pair it with `ScrollEdges` for the full reading feel; keyboard, focus, touch and links stay native, and reduced motion turns it off.

The edges are decorative: they never take pointer events, disappear while anything has keyboard focus, and are hidden for reduced motion and in forced colours. A page that scrolls as a whole, such as a blog post between a site header and footer, keeps native page scrolling and uses `ScrollEdges` without `targetRef`; use a bounded `ScrollArea` when the reading area is the only scroller.

The `Smooth blog reading` story demonstrates the intended composition, heading links, a contained reading list, custom thumb styling, and reading progress. [Shadix UI Smooth Scroll Area](https://shadix-ui.vercel.app/docs/components/smooth-scroll-area) informed the behavior; Gaudi uses its existing Radix primitive and [Lenis](https://github.com/darkroomengineering/lenis) rather than copied registry source.

# Scrollspy

> Core/Scrollspy · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Scrollspy`

Track the visible section and navigate a long document using anchor links.

## Import

```js
import { Scrollspy } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Scrollspy';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Scrollspy`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `targetRef` | `RefObject<HTMLElement>` | — | no | Scrollable region or ScrollArea viewport to observe. Omit to track the document. |
| `onUpdate` | `(activeId: string \| null) => void` | — | no | Respond to the active section changing. |
| `offset` | `number` | `0` | no | Compensate for sticky headers. |
| `smooth` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Smooth scrolling when an anchor is clicked. |
| `history` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Opt in to rewriting the page URL hash to the active section. |
| `dataAttribute` | `string` | `scrollspy` | no | Attribute identifying tracked content. |
| `fallbackToFirst` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Mark the first section before it reaches the offset. Disable for an index whose first target appears later in the article; onUpdate then receives null before that target. |

| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { Scrollspy } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Scrollspy';
import Button from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Button';

<>
<Scrollspy targetRef={articleRef}>
  <Button data-scrollspy-anchor='overview'>Overview</Button>
  <Button data-scrollspy-anchor='details'>Details</Button>
</Scrollspy>
<div ref={articleRef}>
  <section id='overview'><h2>Overview</h2>{overview}</section>
  <section id='details'><h2>Details</h2>{details}</section>
</div>
</>
```

## Accessibility

Use real links with valid targets. Preserve focus and allow navigation without motion.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-scrollspy--playground`)

Curated patterns:

- Top navigation — registry item `@gaudi/scrollspy-top-navigation` (uses `Button`, `ScrollArea`, `Scrollspy`)

## Related

`core-scrollarea`

## README

Highlights the link for the section currently in view and scrolls to a section when its link is clicked. Use it for a table of contents beside a long document or a scrollable panel.

```jsx
import { useRef } from 'react';
import { ScrollArea, Scrollspy } from '@gaudi/design-system';

const targetRef = useRef(null);

<Scrollspy targetRef={targetRef} offset={44}>
  <button data-scrollspy-anchor='overview'>Overview</button>
  <button data-scrollspy-anchor='usage'>Usage</button>
</Scrollspy>
<div ref={targetRef}>
  <ScrollArea className='h-72'>
    <section id='overview'>…</section>
    <section id='usage'>…</section>
  </ScrollArea>
</div>
```

Each anchor names the id of its section; the active anchor gets `data-active="true"` for styling and `onUpdate` receives its id. `offset` reserves room for a sticky header, `smooth` animates the jump, and `history` (off by default) writes the active section to the URL hash. Point `targetRef` at `document` to follow the page scroll.

## Props

| `searchable` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Shows a search field inside the popup and filters options. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `Select option` | no | Trigger placeholder when nothing is selected. |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` | `Search options...` | no | Search input placeholder. |
| `emptyText` | `string` | `No options found.` | no | Empty result text. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Initial open state for demos or controlled-looking examples. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Disables the trigger. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Applies aria-invalid and error styling. |
| `name` | `string` | — | no | Renders hidden form inputs for selected values. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | — | no | Accessible label for icon-only or unlabeled select controls. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Option children normalized when options is empty. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Root class override. |
| `classNames` | `{ root, trigger, value, placeholder, chevron, popup, search, option, check, empty }` | — | no | Slot-level class overrides. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { Select } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Select
  searchable
  multiple
  placeholder='Choose topics'
  options={[
    { label: 'Design systems', value: 'design-systems' },
    { label: 'Knowledge graphs', value: 'knowledge-graphs' },
  ]}
/>
```

## Accessibility

Select uses a native button trigger, listbox semantics, aria-expanded, aria-selected, aria-multiselectable for multi-select, and keyboard support for Arrow keys, Enter, Space, Home, End, and Escape.

## States and recovery

- Keep the existing selection when filtering returns no matches and expose `emptyText` as the recovery message.
- Invalid state must be paired with nearby text that explains the required correction; color and `aria-invalid` alone are insufficient.

- Select in a toolbar — registry item `@gaudi/select-toolbar` (uses `Button`, `FieldInput`, `SelectContent`, `SelectGroup`, `SelectItem`, `SelectRoot`, `SelectTrigger`, `SelectValue`)

## README

Pick one or several values from a list. Use it for form fields with a known set of options; use a combobox when people type to filter a long list, an autocomplete when free text is also allowed, and a native select for the plainest, platform-styled field.

```jsx
import { Select } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Select
  aria-label='Topics'
  options={[{ value: 'design-systems', label: 'Design systems', description: 'Tokens and components.' }]}
  multiple
  searchable
  onValueChange={setTopics}
/>
```

- `options` takes `{ value, label, description?, disabled? }`; native `<option>` children work when `options` is empty.
- `multiple` keeps the popup open and counts the selection in the trigger. `searchable` adds a filter field that matches labels and descriptions.
- `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange` control the selection; `name` submits it with a form. `invalid`, `disabled` and `loading` cover the field states.
- The options API composes the shared `Combobox` trigger, popup, search input and rows; keyboard navigation, focus and viewport collision handling belong to that primitive.

### Composition

`@gaudi/design-system/core/Select` also exports the compound families: `SelectRoot` with `SelectTrigger`, `SelectValue`, `SelectContent`, `SelectItem`, `SelectGroup`, `SelectLabel`, `SelectSeparator`; `Combobox*` (with chips for multiple values); `Autocomplete*`; and `NativeSelect`, `NativeSelectOption`, `NativeSelectOptGroup`.

### Accessibility

The trigger is a button with `aria-haspopup='listbox'`. Arrow keys, Home and End highlight options; disabled options remain discoverable but cannot be selected. Enter selects an enabled option, and Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger. Give every select a visible label or `aria-label`.

# SignaturePad

> Core/SignaturePad · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/SignaturePad`

A composable signature input with pressure-aware SVG ink, undo and redo, native forms, saved previews, and image or JSON export.

## Import

```js
import SignaturePad from '@gaudi/design-system/core/SignaturePad';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `SignaturePad`, `SignaturePadArea`, `SignaturePadClear`, `SignaturePadControls`, `SignaturePadGuide`, `SignaturePadPlaceholder`, `SignaturePadPreview`, `SignaturePadRedo`, `SignaturePadSave`, `SignaturePadUndo`, `default`, `getSignaturePadBounds`, `getSignaturePadStrokePath`, `serializeSignaturePad`, `signaturePadLabels`, `signaturePadToBlob`, `signaturePadToDataURL`, `signaturePadToSVG`, `useSignaturePad`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value / defaultValue / onValueChange` | `SignaturePadStroke[] / function` | `[]` | no | Controlled or initial strokes. A stroke is { points: [x, y, diameter][], color? }. Changes fire once per completed stroke or history action. |
| `disabled / readOnly / invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Disabled prevents interaction and form submission; readOnly allows saving existing ink. Invalid marks the drawing area. |
| `name` | `string` | — | no | Native form field name, external form association, validation, and submission format. Reset restores defaultValue and clears history. |
| `form` | `string` | — | no | Native form field name, external form association, validation, and submission format. Reset restores defaultValue and clears history. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Native form field name, external form association, validation, and submission format. Reset restores defaultValue and clears history. |
| `format` | `svg \| png \| jpeg \| json` | `svg` | no | Native form field name, external form association, validation, and submission format. Reset restores defaultValue and clears history. |
| `color` | `CSS color` | `currentColor` | no | Optional ink color recorded per stroke; unset ink follows the theme. Export defaults to black. |
| `minWidth / maxWidth` | `number` | `0.8 / 3.2` | no | Minimum and maximum ink diameter in CSS pixels. Equal values produce a constant line. |
| `smoothing` | `number` | `0.5` | no | 0–1 smoothing; higher values soften the curve. |
| `sizing` | `auto \| pressure \| velocity` | `auto` | no | Auto reads pen pressure and uses speed for mouse or touch. |
| `pointerTypes` | `(mouse \| touch \| pen)[]` | `all` | no | Filter input devices, such as ["pen"] to ignore touch. |
| `onStrokeStart / onStrokeEnd` | `function` | — | no | Receive { pointerType } when drawing starts and the completed stroke when it ends. Cancelled strokes are discarded. |
| `apiRef` | `ref` | — | no | Access strokes, isEmpty, isDrawing, canUndo, canRedo, clear, undo, redo, focus, toSVG, toDataURL, toBlob, and serialize. |
| `useSignaturePad()` | `hook` | — | no | Access strokes, isEmpty, isDrawing, canUndo, canRedo, clear, undo, redo, focus, toSVG, toDataURL, toBlob, and serialize. |
| `labels` | `object` | `English labels` | no | Override drawing instructions, placeholder, state announcements, and default button labels. Area and Preview accept their own ARIA names. |
| `SignaturePadArea.variant` | `default \| muted \| ghost` | `default` | no | Drawing surface appearance. Root sizing and state props are shared with every part. |
| `SignaturePadControls.position` | `top-start \| top-end \| bottom-start \| bottom-end` | `top-end` | no | Pins controls inside the drawing surface; a regular flex row can place them outside. |
| `SignaturePadSave.format` | `format` | `png` | no | Serialize to a data URL or JSON and pass it to the host. Saving performs no download or upload itself. |
| `options` | `export options` | — | no | Serialize to a data URL or JSON and pass it to the host. Saving performs no download or upload itself. |
| `onSave` | `(value, strokes) => void` | — | no | Serialize to a data URL or JSON and pass it to the host. Saving performs no download or upload itself. |
| `SignaturePadPreview.strokes` | `strokes` | — | no | A standalone SVG preview cropped to its ink; aria-label names its purpose. |
| `padding` | `number` | `4` | no | A standalone SVG preview cropped to its ink; aria-label names its purpose. |
| `color` | `CSS color` | `currentColor` | no | A standalone SVG preview cropped to its ink; aria-label names its purpose. |
| `export options` | `object` | `padding 8; raster scale 2` | no | width and height set a fixed frame. Otherwise crop includes ink thickness and padding. background, color, scale, type, and quality configure output. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Content composed from the exported parts. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `format`: `svg`, `png`, `jpeg`, `json`
- `sizing`: `auto`, `pressure`, `velocity`

## Usage

```jsx
import { SignaturePad, SignaturePadArea, SignaturePadGuide, SignaturePadPlaceholder, SignaturePadUndo, SignaturePadRedo, SignaturePadClear, SignaturePadSave } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/SignaturePad';

<SignaturePad name='signature' required onValueChange={setStrokes}>
  <SignaturePadArea aria-label='Recipient signature'>
    <SignaturePadGuide />
    <SignaturePadPlaceholder />
  </SignaturePadArea>
  <div className='flex flex-wrap gap-2'>
    <SignaturePadUndo />
    <SignaturePadRedo />
    <SignaturePadClear />
    <SignaturePadSave format='svg' onSave={handleSave} />
  </div>
</SignaturePad>
```

## Accessibility

Give the area a visible label and useful instructions. Drawing requires a pointer, so compose a typed-name alternative with Core Tabs and Input when the workflow needs keyboard-only entry. Undo/redo shortcuts apply only within the area, respect editable overlays and IME, and do not capture page shortcuts. Cancel a live stroke with Escape. Clear and exhausted history controls return focus to the area.

## Notes

- Compose SignaturePadArea inside SignaturePad; guide, placeholder, controls, and save actions are optional.
- Store the stroke array to reopen and edit a signature. A changed controlled value clears history; an equivalent deep copy preserves it.
- Applications own consent, document identity, validation policy, upload, persistence, and any signing audit trail.

- Draw Or Type (Storybook `core-signaturepad--draw-or-type`)
- Export Formats (Storybook `core-signaturepad--export-formats`)
- Controlled And Stylus (Storybook `core-signaturepad--controlled-and-stylus`)

## Related

`core-tabs`, `core-input`, `mdx-preview`

## README

Composable signature entry with SVG ink, mouse/touch/pen input, undo/redo, a native form value, saved previews, and PNG, JPEG, SVG, or JSON export. Adapted from [ReUI Signature Pad](https://reui.io/docs/components/base/signature-pad), under the MIT notice in the [root README](../../../../README.md#third-party-notices).

```jsx
import {
  SignaturePad, SignaturePadArea, SignaturePadGuide,
  SignaturePadPlaceholder, SignaturePadClear, SignaturePadSave
} from '@gaudi/design-system/core/SignaturePad';

<SignaturePad value={strokes} onValueChange={setStrokes} name='signature' required>
  <SignaturePadArea aria-label='Recipient signature'>
    <SignaturePadGuide />
    <SignaturePadPlaceholder />
  </SignaturePadArea>
  <div className='flex flex-wrap gap-2'>
    <SignaturePadClear />
    <SignaturePadSave format='svg' onSave={(dataUrl, strokes) => save(dataUrl, strokes)} />
  </div>
</SignaturePad>
```

### Value and editing

Each stroke is `{ points: [[x, y, diameter], ...], color? }`. Coordinates use the drawing area's CSS pixel space; the display scales existing ink uniformly when a container becomes smaller without mutating the stored data. `onValueChange` fires once when a stroke completes or history changes, never for each pointer move. Treat values as immutable.

`value` is controlled; `defaultValue` initializes local state. Equal deep copies preserve history. A different external value starts a new history. Refused controlled changes leave the accepted strokes and history authoritative. History retains up to 100 changes.

`color` is optional: unset ink follows the theme. `minWidth` / `maxWidth` set the ink diameter (0.8 / 3.2 by default); `smoothing` is 0–1. `sizing='auto'` uses pen pressure and mouse/touch velocity. Use `pointerTypes={['pen']}` to reject touch. Pointer cancellation, lost capture, Escape, a resize during drawing, or disabling/locking the pad discard unfinished ink. Overlay controls do not draw beneath themselves.

### Parts and API

- `SignaturePadArea`: labelled drawing area; `variant='default' | 'muted' | 'ghost'`. Fills its container width with a default height of `12rem`; override its height with a class.
- `SignaturePadGuide`, `SignaturePadPlaceholder`: optional non-interactive overlays.
- `SignaturePadControls`: pinned controls; `position='top-start' | 'top-end' | 'bottom-start' | 'bottom-end'`.
- `SignaturePadUndo`, `SignaturePadRedo`, `SignaturePadClear`, `SignaturePadSave`: Gaudi buttons, supporting button props and text children. Their click handlers compose with host handlers and honor `preventDefault()`.
- `SignaturePadPreview`: a server-renderable, standalone SVG from `strokes`, cropped with `padding` (default 4). Supply an `aria-label` for its purpose.
- `useSignaturePad()` or `apiRef`: `strokes`, `isEmpty`, `isDrawing`, `canUndo`, `canRedo`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `clear()`, `undo()`, `redo()`, `focus()`, `toSVG(options)`, `toDataURL(options)`, `toBlob(options)`, `serialize(format, options)`. Editing operations also respect disabled/read-only state.

### Styling

The pad follows Gaudi's compact neutral styling: shared rounded corners, input border, semantic background/foreground colors, and the accent token for visible focus. These tokens support light and dark themes. Component gaps and internal padding follow the `--ds-space-scale` multiplier. Pinned controls wrap within the drawing area; completed ink preserves its proportions as the container shrinks, as described above.

### Forms and exports

`name` creates a native field; `form` associates it with an external form. `required` rejects an empty value and focuses the drawing area. `format` defaults to SVG. PNG/JPEG form formats rasterize after each completed change; SVG/JSON avoid that work. A disabled pad is omitted from `FormData`. Native reset restores `defaultValue` and clears history; cancelling reset preserves the value. `invalid` and `aria-describedby` connect application validation feedback.

Save returns a data URL for PNG, JPEG, or SVG; JSON returns the stroke array as a string. It does not upload or download. Export helpers are `getSignaturePadBounds`, `getSignaturePadStrokePath`, `signaturePadToSVG`, `signaturePadToDataURL`, `signaturePadToBlob`, and `serializeSignaturePad`. Raster helpers require a browser and belong in handlers/effects; SVG/JSON helpers and previews work on the server. Empty serialization is an empty string.

Exports crop to the ink including stroke thickness and 8px padding. Both `width` and `height` fix a frame; `crop: false` keeps the origin. With the pad API, `crop: false` uses its displayed coordinate frame. `color` defaults to black; `background` is transparent except JPEG, which defaults to white. Raster `scale` defaults to 2; `type` and `quality` configure the image. Use `toBlob()` for uploads without base64 expansion.

### Accessibility and application boundaries

Give the area a visible label with `aria-labelledby` and instructions through `aria-describedby`. `labels` overrides default labels and instructions. Undo/redo supports Ctrl/Cmd+Z, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z, and Ctrl/Cmd+Y; editable overlays and IME keep their own keyboard handling. The surface shows focus, preserves ink across themes, and returns focus from actions that disable themselves.

Drawing has no keyboard equivalent. The Draw or Type example composes existing Tabs, Input, and Button and stores the typed name as a separate application value. Applications own consent, document identity, persistence, upload, and signing policy; this component collects input.

# Skeleton

> Core/Skeleton · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Skeleton`

Skeleton renders non-semantic loading placeholders on the theme border token, so blocks read clearly in light and dark themes. Shimmer is the text counterpart: a highlight that sweeps across a label such as Thinking… while work is in progress. SkeletonMorph grows placeholders into the loaded content block by block instead of swapping them.

## Import

```js
import Skeleton from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Skeleton';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Shimmer`, `SkeletonMorph`, `SkeletonMorphBlock`, `SkeletonRoot`, `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Defines shape, width, height, radius, and layout placement. |
| `as` | `ElementType` | `div` | no | Element to render; use 'span' inside text such as a paragraph or link. |
| `Shimmer.children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Text that shimmers while work is in progress, such as Thinking… or Searching the web…; it stays real, readable text. |
| `Shimmer.active` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Run or rest the sweep, seconds per sweep, and band width in pixels per character. |
| `duration` | `number` | `2` | no | Run or rest the sweep, seconds per sweep, and band width in pixels per character. |
| `spread` | `number` | `2` | no | Run or rest the sweep, seconds per sweep, and band width in pixels per character. |
| `Shimmer.as` | `ElementType` | `span` | no | Element to render, such as p or h3. |
| `SkeletonMorph.loading` | `boolean` | — | no | Shows placeholders while true; when it turns false each block resizes into its content in document order. |
| `SkeletonMorph.label` | `string` | — | no | Status message announced while loading, such as Loading profile. |
| `SkeletonMorph.as` | `ElementType` | `div` | no | Element or component for the region, such as CardContent. |
| `SkeletonMorphBlock.width / height` | `number \| string` | — | no | Placeholder size; numbers are pixels. Ignored once loaded, when the block takes its content size. |
| `SkeletonMorphBlock.lines` | `number` | — | no | Text placeholder: that many lines at the content line height, the last one shorter. |
| `lineHeight` | `number \| string` | `20` | no | Text placeholder: that many lines at the content line height, the last one shorter. |
| `SkeletonMorphBlock.shape` | `'circle'` | — | no | Round placeholder and clip for avatars. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { Shimmer, Skeleton, SkeletonMorph, SkeletonMorphBlock } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<>
<Skeleton className='h-4 w-40' />
<p role='status'><Shimmer>Searching the web…</Shimmer></p>
<SkeletonMorph loading={!user} label='Loading profile'>
  <SkeletonMorphBlock shape='circle' width={48} height={48}><Avatar /></SkeletonMorphBlock>
  <SkeletonMorphBlock lines={2}><p>{user?.bio}</p></SkeletonMorphBlock>
</SkeletonMorph>
</>
```

## Accessibility

Skeleton is aria-hidden and should be paired with loading text or a labelled busy region when content loading needs announcement. Shimmer keeps its words as real text; put it in a status region when the change should be announced. Both hold still for reduced motion. SkeletonMorph marks its region aria-busy and announces its label in a status message while loading; placeholders stay hidden, content renders only once loaded, and reduced motion swaps without animating.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-skeleton--playground`)
- Text shimmer (Storybook `core-skeleton--text-shimmer`)

Curated patterns:

- List with avatars and actions — registry item `@gaudi/skeleton-avatar-list` (uses `Separator`, `SkeletonRoot`)
- Chat messages — registry item `@gaudi/skeleton-chat` (uses `CardContent`, `CardRoot`, `SkeletonRoot`)
- Dashboard stats and table — registry item `@gaudi/skeleton-dashboard` (uses `CardContent`, `CardHeader`, `CardRoot`, `SkeletonRoot`)
- Form — registry item `@gaudi/skeleton-form` (uses `SkeletonRoot`)
- Media card — registry item `@gaudi/skeleton-media-card` (uses `CardContent`, `CardFooter`, `CardHeader`, `CardRoot`, `SkeletonRoot`)
- Skeleton morph — registry item `@gaudi/skeleton-morph` (uses `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarRoot`, `Badge`, `Button`, `CardAction`, `CardContent`, `CardHeader`, `CardRoot`, `CardTitle`, `RegistryIcon`, `SkeletonMorph`, `SkeletonMorphBlock`)
- Profile page — registry item `@gaudi/skeleton-profile` (uses `CardContent`, `CardHeader`, `CardRoot`, `Separator`, `SkeletonRoot`)

## README

A skeleton is a grey placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading, so the layout does not jump when it arrives.

```jsx
import { Skeleton } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<section aria-label='Latest article' aria-busy='true' className='grid gap-3'>
  <span role='status' className='sr-only'>Loading the latest article</span>
  <Skeleton className='aspect-video w-full' />
  <Skeleton className='h-4 w-2/3' />
</section>
```

- Shape each block with `className` (height, width, `rounded-full` for avatars) to match the content it stands in for.
- Inside text, such as a paragraph or a link, render it as a span: `<Skeleton as='span' className='inline-block h-4 w-24' />`.
- Skeletons are hidden from assistive tech. Mark the region `aria-busy` and add a status message that names what is loading.
- Use a skeleton when the layout is known; use `Loader` for short waits or when the shape is unknown.

### Shimmer

`Shimmer` is the text counterpart: a highlight sweeps across a label while work is in progress, such as "Thinking…" in a chat reply or "Searching the web…" in an agent step.

```jsx
import { Shimmer } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<p role='status'><Shimmer>Searching the web…</Shimmer></p>
<Shimmer as='h3' duration={3} spread={3}>Drafting the summary</Shimmer>
```

- `duration` is one sweep in seconds (default 2); `spread` is the band width in pixels per character (default 2); `active={false}` rests it as plain text.
- The words stay real text, so they are read, selectable and translated. Put the label in a status region when the change should be announced.
- The sweep is the `shimmer` utility on the text tokens; it holds still for reduced motion and in forced-colour modes.

### Skeleton morph

`SkeletonMorph` grows its placeholders into the loaded content instead of swapping them: when `loading` turns false, each `SkeletonMorphBlock` resizes from its placeholder to its content as the content fades in, one block after another in document order.

```jsx
import { SkeletonMorph, SkeletonMorphBlock } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<SkeletonMorph loading={!user} label='Loading profile' className='flex items-start gap-3'>
  <SkeletonMorphBlock shape='circle' width={48} height={48}>
    <Avatar>…</Avatar>
  </SkeletonMorphBlock>
  <SkeletonMorphBlock width={140} lines={1}><p className='leading-5'>{user?.name}</p></SkeletonMorphBlock>
  <SkeletonMorphBlock lines={3}><p className='leading-5'>{user?.bio}</p></SkeletonMorphBlock>
</SkeletonMorph>
```

- Size each placeholder like its content: `width`/`height` for a block (numbers are pixels), or `lines` with the content's `lineHeight` (default 20) for text. `shape='circle'` is for avatars.
- Block children render only once loaded, but the JSX is still evaluated while loading, so read optional data (`user?.name`).
- The region is `aria-busy` while loading and announces `label` in a status message; `as` renders it as another element or component, such as `CardContent`. Placeholders stay hidden from assistive tech, and focus is not moved.
- Reduced motion swaps without animating. Use it for cards, short lists and dashboards whose layout is known in advance; keep plain `Skeleton` rows for long tables, where animating layout is costly, and `Loader` for waits longer than a few seconds.

# Slider

> Core/Slider · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Slider`

Adjust one value or a range with pointer and keyboard input.

## Import

```js
import { Slider } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Slider';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Slider`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `getValueText` | `(value, index) => string` | — | no | Text a thumb announces instead of the number, such as a level name; use it with a controlled value. |
| `value / defaultValue` | `number[]` | — | no | Controlled or initial thumb positions. |
| `onValueChange / onValueCommit` | `(values: number[]) => void` | — | no | Continuous updates or the committed selection. |
| `min / max` | `number` | `0 / 100` | no | Allowed range. |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | no | Keyboard and pointer increment. |
| `orientation` | `horizontal \| vertical` | `horizontal` | no | Control orientation. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Prevent adjustment. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `orientation`: `horizontal`, `vertical`

## Usage

```jsx
import { Slider } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Slider';

<Slider aria-label='Volume' value={volume} onValueChange={setVolume} min={0} max={100} />
```

## Accessibility

Label every thumb and provide a readable value. Use range examples when the two endpoints have different meanings.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-slider--playground`)

Curated patterns:

- Paired with a number field — registry item `@gaudi/slider-number-sync` (uses `Label`, `NumberField`, `NumberFieldGroup`, `NumberFieldInput`, `Slider`)
- Custom readouts — registry item `@gaudi/slider-readouts` (uses `Label`, `Slider`)

- Thumbs and states — registry item `@gaudi/slider-thumbs-states` (uses `Slider`)

## README

Picks a value, or a range with two thumbs, by dragging along a track. Use it for approximate settings such as volume or a price range; use a NumberField when the exact number matters.

### Usage

```jsx
import { Slider } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Slider aria-label='Volume' defaultValue={[50]} min={0} max={100} step={5} onValueChange={setVolume} />;
```

Pass two values for a range. `orientation` is `horizontal` or `vertical`.

### Accessibility

Each thumb is a `slider` named from `aria-label` (numbered for ranges). Arrow keys step the value, Home and End jump to the ends. Show the current value as text next to the slider.

# Sortable

> Core/Sortable · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Sortable`

Reorder lists and grids with drag handles, keyboard controls and cancellation.

## Import

```js
import { Sortable } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Sortable';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Sortable`, `SortableItem`, `SortableItemHandle`, `SortableOverlay`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `Array` | — | no | Controlled item order. |
| `onValueChange` | `function` | — | no | Controlled item order. |
| `getItemValue` | `(item) => string` | — | no | Stable unique identity for each item. |
| `strategy` | `vertical \| horizontal \| grid` | `vertical` | no | Layout-specific sorting strategy. |
| `onMove / onValueCommit` | `function` | — | no | Move notification and committed order. |
| `onDragStart / onDragEnd / onDragCancel` | `function` | — | no | Drag lifecycle callbacks. |
| `accessibility / modifiers` | `DndContext props` | — | no | Announcements, instructions and movement constraints. |
| `SortableItem.disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Locks the item in place; its handle dims and shows a not-allowed cursor. |
| `SortableOverlay.children` | `ReactNode \| ({ value }) => ReactNode` | `Copy of the active item` | no | Custom content for the single drag overlay. Place it directly inside Sortable. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Content composed from the exported parts. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `strategy`: `vertical`, `horizontal`, `grid`

## Usage

```jsx
import { Sortable, SortableItem, SortableItemHandle } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Sortable';

<Sortable value={ids} onValueChange={setIds}>
  {ids.map(id => <SortableItem key={id} value={id}>
    <SortableItemHandle aria-label={`Reorder ${labels[id]}`} />
    {labels[id]}
  </SortableItem>)}
</Sortable>
```

## Accessibility

Keep a keyboard-operable handle and announce moves. The application owns saving and restoring the last committed order.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-sortable--playground`)

Curated patterns:

- Media grid — registry item `@gaudi/sortable-media-grid` (uses `Badge`, `Frame`, `FrameDescription`, `FrameHeader`, `FramePanel`, `FrameTitle`, `RegistryIcon`, `Sortable`, `SortableItem`, `SortableItemHandle`, `cn`)
- Nested lists — registry item `@gaudi/sortable-nested` (uses `CardContent`, `CardRoot`, `RegistryIcon`, `Sortable`, `SortableItem`, `SortableItemHandle`, `ToastProvider`, `toast`)
- Persisted order — registry item `@gaudi/sortable-persisted` (uses `Badge`, `Label`, `RegistryIcon`, `Sortable`, `SortableItem`, `SortableItemHandle`, `SwitchRoot`, `ToastProvider`, `toast`, `useTimeout`)
- List with row controls — registry item `@gaudi/sortable-row-controls` (uses `Badge`, `Frame`, `FrameDescription`, `FrameHeader`, `FramePanel`, `FrameTitle`, `RegistryIcon`, `Sortable`, `SortableItem`, `SortableItemHandle`, `SwitchRoot`, `ToastProvider`, `toast`)

## README

Drag-and-drop reordering for lists, lanes, and grids, with keyboard support. Use it when the order of items matters to the reader, such as a checklist or a gallery cover.

```jsx
import { Sortable, SortableItem, SortableItemHandle } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Sortable value={tasks} onValueChange={setTasks} getItemValue={(task) => task.id}>
  {tasks.map((task) => (
    <SortableItem key={task.id} value={task.id}>
      <SortableItemHandle aria-label={`Reorder ${task.title}`}>⋮⋮</SortableItemHandle>
      {task.title}
    </SortableItem>
  ))}
</Sortable>
```

- `strategy`: `vertical` (default), `horizontal`, or `grid`.
- `onValueCommit` fires once per completed move, which is where you persist the new order.
- `disabled` on an item pins it in place. `SortableOverlay` customises the lifted copy shown while dragging.
- Handles are buttons: Space picks up an item, arrow keys move it, Space drops it, and Escape cancels.

## Related

`blocks-wizard`

## README

Shows progress through an ordered set of steps. Use the `Stepper` default export to display where a reader is in a flow; use `Wizard` when the steps also need validation and Back/Next navigation.

```jsx
import Stepper from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Stepper';

<Stepper
  activeStep={1}
  label='Publishing progress'
  steps={[
    { id: 'details', label: 'Details', description: 'Title and cover' },
    { id: 'audience', label: 'Audience', description: 'Readers and tags' },
    { id: 'review', label: 'Review', description: 'Two editors' }
  ]}
/>
```

`activeStep` is zero-based; set it to `steps.length` when every step is done. The current step has `aria-current="step"` and completed steps show a check with a "Completed" text alternative. `label` names the group.

The display stepper is built on the composition parts (`StepperRoot`, `StepperNav`, `StepperItem`, `StepperTrigger`, `StepperIndicator`, `StepperSeparator`, `StepperTitle`, `StepperDescription`, `StepperPanel`, `StepperContent`). Compose them for clickable, controlled, loading or vertical steppers.

# Tabs

```jsx
  <TabsContent value='overview'>{overview}</TabsContent>
```

## Accessibility

Radix associates tabs and panels. Label the tab list; use manual activation when loading panels is expensive.

## Related

`core-switch`

## README

Switches between related panels on the same page. Use it for views of one thing (overview, history, settings); use `NavigationMenu` or links when each view has its own URL.

```jsx
<Tabs defaultValue='overview'>
  <TabsList aria-label='Article'>
    <TabsTrigger value='overview'>Overview</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value='history'>History</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsContent value='overview'>Article details</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value='history'>Revision history</TabsContent>
</Tabs>
```

| Prop / export | Type | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value / defaultValue / onValueChange` | string / string / function | Controlled or uncontrolled active panel. |
| `orientation` | horizontal or vertical | List direction and arrow keys. |
| `activationMode` | automatic or manual | Select on focus, or wait for Enter/Space. |
| `TabsList variant` | default or line | `line` drops the rule under the list. |
| `TabsTrigger / TabsContent` | components | Match their `value`; triggers accept `disabled`. |

Label each `TabsList`. Use manual activation when a panel is expensive to load.

Keyboard focus is drawn inside each trigger, so the scrolling list never clips it. In forced-colours mode (Windows High Contrast) idle tabs drop their border and the selected tab draws it, and its underline, in `Highlight`.

# Terminal

> Core/Terminal · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Terminal`

| `username` | `string` | `ahmad` | no | Prompt username segment. |

| `variant` | `dark \| light \| translucent` | `dark` | no | Terminal surface treatment. |
| `size` | `sm \| md \| lg` | `md` | no | Controls max width, body height, and text size. |
| `radius` | `none \| sm \| md \| lg` | `lg` | no | Legacy aliases use the global --ds-radius setting; none keeps square corners. |
| `showHeader` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Shows mac window controls and title. |
| `animate` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Types commands over time unless reduced motion is preferred. |
| `typingSpeed` | `number` | `35` | no | Milliseconds between typed characters. |
| `initialDelay` | `number` | `400` | no | Delay before the first command starts. |
| `delayBetweenCommands` | `number` | `700` | no | Delay after a command before the next command starts. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Root class override. |
| `classNames` | `{ root, header, controls, title, body, line, prompt, command, output }` | — | no | Slot-level class overrides. |

## Variants

- `variant`: `dark`, `light`, `translucent`
- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg`
- `radius`: `none`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`

## Usage

```jsx
import { Terminal } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Terminal
  title='blog — zsh'
  username='ahmad'
  commands={[
    { command: 'pnpm test:ds-contracts', output: [{ text: '85 component contracts passed.', tone: 'success' }] },
  ]}
/>
```

## Accessibility

Terminal renders readable command history inside a labelled region. Motion is disabled when users prefer reduced motion.

## Examples

- Legacy Outputs (Storybook `core-terminal--legacy-outputs`)

Curated patterns:

- Activity stream — registry item `@gaudi/timeline-activity-stream` (uses `Attachment`, `AttachmentAction`, `AttachmentActions`, `AttachmentContent`, `AttachmentDescription`, `AttachmentGroup`, `AttachmentMedia`, `AttachmentTitle`, `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarGroup`, `AvatarGroupCount`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarRoot`, `Badge`, `Button`, `DropdownMenuContent`, `DropdownMenuItemPrimitive`, `DropdownMenuRoot`, `DropdownMenuSeparatorPrimitive`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`, `ProgressRoot`, `Rating`, `RegistryIcon`, `TimelineContent`, `TimelineDate`, `TimelineHeader`, `TimelineIndicator`, `TimelineItem`, `TimelineRoot`, `TimelineSeparator`, `useCopyToClipboard`)
- Alternating milestones — registry item `@gaudi/timeline-alternating` (uses `TimelineDate`, `TimelineHeader`, `TimelineIndicator`, `TimelineItem`, `TimelineRoot`, `TimelineSeparator`, `TimelineTitle`, `cn`)
- Release changelog — registry item `@gaudi/timeline-changelog` (uses `Badge`, `TimelineContent`, `TimelineDate`, `TimelineHeader`, `TimelineIndicator`, `TimelineItem`, `TimelineRoot`, `TimelineSeparator`, `TimelineTitle`)
- Horizontal releases — registry item `@gaudi/timeline-horizontal-releases` (uses `Badge`, `Label`, `RegistryIcon`, `ScrollArea`, `ScrollBar`, `SwitchRoot`, `TimelineContent`, `TimelineDate`, `TimelineHeader`, `TimelineIndicator`, `TimelineItem`, `TimelineRoot`, `TimelineSeparator`, `TimelineTitle`, `cn`)
- Pipeline steps — registry item `@gaudi/timeline-pipeline-steps` (uses `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarRoot`, `Badge`, `Collapsible`, `CollapsibleContent`, `CollapsibleTrigger`, `Frame`, `FrameHeader`, `FramePanel`, `LoaderRoot`, `RegistryIcon`, `TimelineContent`, `TimelineHeader`, `TimelineIndicator`, `TimelineItem`, `TimelineRoot`, `TimelineSeparator`, `TimelineTitle`, `cn`)

## README

A dated activity feed or a set of milestones. `Timeline` takes an `items` array and renders an ordered list built from
the Timeline parts; compose `TimelineRoot`, `TimelineItem`, `TimelineIndicator`, `TimelineSeparator`, `TimelineHeader`,
`TimelineTitle`, `TimelineDate` and `TimelineContent` directly for steps, horizontal rails or avatars.

```jsx
import Timeline from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Timeline';

<Timeline
  label='Editorial activity'
  items={[{ id: 'published', title: 'Article published', time: '2 days ago', dateTime: '2026-09-27T09:00:00Z', icon: <Icon name='CircleCheck' decorative /> }]}
/>
```

- Each item needs a stable `id` and a `title`; `description`, `time` with a machine-readable `dateTime`, a decorative `icon`
  and `children` (actions, quotes, files) are optional.
- `label` names the list. Icons are decorative, so keep the meaning in the text.
- `TimelineRoot` tracks the active step (`value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `orientation`); `TimelineRoot`,
  `TimelineItem` and `TimelineTitle` accept `asChild` to render your own element, such as `<ol>`, `<li>` or a heading level.

# Toast

> Core/Toast · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Toast`

Transient feedback for completed actions, errors and recoverable background work.

## Import

```js
import Toast from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Toast';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `default`, `toast`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | `top-left \| top-center \| top-right \| bottom-left \| bottom-center \| bottom-right` | `bottom-right` | no | Toast stack position. |
| `closeButton` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Show an explicit dismiss action. |
| `expand` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Show every toast in the stack instead of collapsing them behind the front one. |
| `duration` | `number` | `Sonner default` | no | Default display duration in milliseconds. |
| `toastOptions` | `ExternalToast` | `Gaudi class names` | no | Default appearance and behavior for each toast. |
| `toast(message, options)` | `function` | — | no | Show a message; options include description, action and cancellation. |
| `toast.promise(promise, options)` | `function` | — | no | Show loading, success and error feedback for one operation. |

## Variants

- `position`: `top-left`, `top-center`, `top-right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-center`, `bottom-right`

## Usage

```jsx
import ToastProvider, { toast } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Toast';
import Button from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Button';

<><ToastProvider /><Button onClick={() => toast.success('Changes saved')}>Save</Button></>
```

## Accessibility

Use inline errors for fields and persistent failures. Keep toast actions keyboard accessible and allow enough time to act.

## Notes

- Mount one ToastProvider for a region. The toast API and additional provider props are forwarded from Sonner.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-toast--playground`)

Curated patterns:

- Actions — registry item `@gaudi/toast-actions` (uses `Button`, `ToastProvider`, `toast`)
- Progress and async work — registry item `@gaudi/toast-async-progress` (uses `Button`, `ProgressRoot`, `RegistryIcon`, `ToastProvider`, `toast`, `useInterval`, `useTimeout`)
- Custom content — registry item `@gaudi/toast-custom-content` (uses `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarGroup`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarRoot`, `Button`, `Label`, `RegistryIcon`, `Separator`, `SwitchRoot`, `ToastProvider`, `toast`)
- Types and options — registry item `@gaudi/toast-types-options` (uses `Button`, `Label`, `NativeSelect`, `NativeSelectOption`, `RegistryIcon`, `SwitchRoot`, `ToastProvider`, `ToggleGroupItem`, `ToggleGroupRoot`, `toast`)

## README

Short, non-blocking notifications for finished actions, errors and background work. Mount one `ToastProvider` per app and call `toast()` from anywhere. The toast surface uses Gaudi tokens and its action, cancel and close buttons use the Button variants.

### Usage

```jsx
<ToastProvider />
<Button onClick={() => toast.success('Draft saved')}>Save draft</Button>
```

### API

| Prop / export   | Type             | Contract                                                                          |
| --------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ToastProvider` | component        | Mount once; forwards Sonner configuration including position, duration and theme. `toastOptions.classNames` are merged with the Gaudi classes. |
| `toast`         | function         | Use toast(), toast.success(), toast.error(), toast.promise() and toast.dismiss(). |
| `action`        | {label, onClick} | Optional recovery or undo action on a notification.                               |

### Ownership and verification

The host supplies data, translations, network calls, permissions and persistence. Gaudi owns layout, semantics and local interaction. Examples document working behavior and states, with Storybook interaction/axe checks and a server-rendering contract test alongside the component.
