# ToggleGroup

> Core/ToggleGroup · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/ToggleGroup`

Single or multiple pressed choices for view modes and compact formatting controls.

## Import

```js
import ToggleGroup from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ToggleGroup';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Toggle`, `ToggleGroupItem`, `ToggleGroupRoot`, `default`, `toggleVariants`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | — | no | Accessible name of the group. |
| `options` | `Array<{ value, label, disabled? }>` | `[]` | no | Available choices. |
| `type` | `single \| multiple` | `single` | no | Selection model. |
| `variant` | `outline \| default` | `outline` | no | Attached outline items by default; spacing separates them. |
| `size` | `sm \| default \| lg` | `default` | no | Attached outline items by default; spacing separates them. |
| `spacing` | `number` | `0` | no | Attached outline items by default; spacing separates them. |
| `value / defaultValue / onValueChange` | `string \| string[] / function` | — | no | Controlled or initial selection matching type. |
| `disabled / loop` | `boolean` | `false / true` | no | Group availability and keyboard wrapping. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `type`: `single`, `multiple`
- `variant`: `outline`, `default`
- `size`: `sm`, `default`, `lg`

## Usage

```jsx
import ToggleGroup from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ToggleGroup';

<ToggleGroup type='single' label='Display' value={view} onValueChange={setView}
  options={[{ value: 'list', label: 'List' }, { value: 'grid', label: 'Grid' }]} />
```

## Accessibility

Each item communicates its pressed state. Choose radio controls when a form requires exactly one persistent choice.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-togglegroup--playground`)
- Disabled Options (Storybook `core-togglegroup--disabled-options`)

Curated patterns:

- Filters — registry item `@gaudi/toggle-group-filters` (uses `RegistryIcon`, `ToggleGroupItem`, `ToggleGroupRoot`)
- Icon and label switchers — registry item `@gaudi/toggle-group-switchers` (uses `RegistryIcon`, `ToggleGroupItem`, `ToggleGroupRoot`)
- Group variants, spacing, sizes and orientation — registry item `@gaudi/toggle-group-variants` (uses `Badge`, `RegistryIcon`, `ToggleGroupItem`, `ToggleGroupRoot`)
- Toggle that swaps icon and label — registry item `@gaudi/toggle-icon-label-swap` (uses `RegistryIcon`, `Toggle`, `TooltipContent`, `TooltipProvider`, `TooltipRoot`, `TooltipTrigger`)
- Reactions and counts — registry item `@gaudi/toggle-reactions` (uses `Badge`, `RegistryIcon`, `Toggle`)
- Toggle variants, sizes and states — registry item `@gaudi/toggle-variants` (uses `Button`, `RegistryIcon`, `Toggle`)

## README

A toggle group lets people pick one option (a view mode) or several (filters, formatting) from a short set of buttons.

```jsx
import { ToggleGroup } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<ToggleGroup
  label='Collection view'
  defaultValue='list'
  options={[
    { value: 'list', label: 'List' },
    { value: 'grid', label: 'Grid' },
    { value: 'board', label: 'Board', disabled: true }
  ]}
/>
```

- `type='single'` (default) keeps one value and allows clearing it; `type='multiple'` keeps an array.
- `variant` (`outline` or `default`), `size` (`sm`, `default`, `lg`) and `spacing` (0 attaches the items) change the look.
- Icon-only options need an `ariaLabel`.
- For custom item content, compose `ToggleGroupRoot` and `ToggleGroupItem`; use `Toggle` for a single on/off button.
- Arrow keys move between options and skip disabled ones.

# Tree

> Core/Tree · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/Tree`

Browse hierarchical content with expansion, selection, checkboxes and drag feedback.

## Import

```js
import { Tree } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Tree';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `Tree`, `TreeDragLine`, `TreeItem`, `TreeItemLabel`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tree` | `Headless Tree instance` | `Required` | no | State and feature configuration returned by useTree. |
| `indent` | `number` | `20` | no | Indentation per hierarchy level. |
| `toggleIconType` | `chevron \| plus-minus` | `chevron` | no | Expansion indicator style. |
| `TreeItem.item` | `Headless Tree item instance` | `Required` | no | Node state and event bindings. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Merge the root into a child element. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Content composed from the exported parts. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `toggleIconType`: `chevron`, `plus-minus`

## Usage

```jsx
import { Tree, TreeItem, TreeItemLabel } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Tree';

// tree is the host's @headless-tree/react useTree instance.
<Tree tree={tree} aria-label='Project files'>
  {tree.getItems().map(item => <TreeItem key={item.getId()} item={item}>
    <TreeItemLabel>{item.getItemName()}</TreeItemLabel>
  </TreeItem>)}
</Tree>
```

## Accessibility

Headless Tree supplies hierarchical keyboard navigation. Keep node names stable and announce loading or failed child fetches.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-tree--playground`)

Curated patterns:

- Display options — registry item `@gaudi/tree-display-options` (uses `Label`, `RegistryIcon`, `SwitchRoot`, `Tree`, `TreeItem`, `TreeItemLabel`)
- Organization chart — registry item `@gaudi/tree-org-chart` (uses `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarRoot`, `Tree`, `TreeItem`, `TreeItemLabel`)
- Permission checkboxes — registry item `@gaudi/tree-permissions` (uses `CheckboxRoot`, `Tree`, `TreeItem`, `TreeItemLabel`)

## README

An expandable hierarchy such as a file explorer, an org chart or nested permissions. Use it when readers need to open branches and pick items; use `Accordion` for a flat list of sections.

```jsx
import { useTree } from '@headless-tree/react';
import { selectionFeature, syncDataLoaderFeature } from '@headless-tree/core';
import { Tree, TreeItem, TreeItemLabel } from '@gaudi/design-system';

const tree = useTree({ rootItemId: 'root', dataLoader, getItemName, isItemFolder, features: [syncDataLoaderFeature, selectionFeature] });

<Tree tree={tree} indent={20}>
  {tree.getItems().map((item) => (
    <TreeItem key={item.getId()} item={item}>
      <TreeItemLabel />
    </TreeItem>
  ))}
</Tree>
```

Headless Tree owns state, selection and keyboard navigation (arrows, Home/End, type-ahead); Gaudi renders the rows. `indent` spaces each level, `toggleIconType` switches the folder chevron for plus and minus, and `TreeDragLine` shows the drop position while dragging. Keep item names stable and announce loading or failed child fetches.

# VideoPlayer

> Core/VideoPlayer · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/VideoPlayer`

A native video player with a complete toolbar, an elastic minimal timeline, and a poster that opens a focused viewing dialog.

## Import

```js
import { VideoPlayer } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/VideoPlayer';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `VideoPlayer`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | — | no | A browser-playable video URL. Changing it resets playback and pending requests. An empty source shows the empty state. |
| `poster` | `string` | — | no | Preview image while the video is idle, and the dialog trigger image. |
| `title` | `string` | `Video` | no | Names the video, player region, and dialog. |
| `variant` | `standard \| minimal \| dialog` | `standard` | no | Full toolbar, compact elastic scrubber, or pointer-enhanced poster opening a dialog. |
| `aspectRatio` | `string \| number` | `16 / 9` | no | CSS aspect ratio of the video stage and poster. |
| `fit` | `contain \| cover` | `contain` | no | Contain preserves the entire frame. Cover crops to fill the stage. |
| `tracks` | `Array<{ src, srcLang, label, kind?, default? }>` | `[]` | no | Native WebVTT tracks; kind defaults to captions. Only captions and subtitles appear in the language selector. Selecting or disabling captions leaves metadata and chapter track modes untouched. Serve track files from the same origin. |
| `autoPlay` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Attempts playback when this source mounts or its dialog opens. Browser rejection leaves a usable Play control and a status message. |
| `defaultMuted` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Initial muted preference for each source. Native volume events own later changes. |
| `defaultVolume` | `number (0–1)` | `1` | no | Initial volume, clamped to the supported range. Applied when the source mounts. |
| `loop` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Restarts the native video at the end. |
| `preload` | `none \| metadata \| auto` | `metadata` | no | Native browser preload hint. Metadata enables the duration and seek controls. |
| `nativeControls` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Uses the browser’s controls in place of the custom toolbar. The source must still be browser-playable; this adds no streaming adapters or codec support. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `uncontrolled` | no | Controlled or uncontrolled dialog visibility. Only used by the dialog variant. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Controlled or uncontrolled dialog visibility. Only used by the dialog variant. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open) => void` | — | no | Controlled or uncontrolled dialog visibility. Only used by the dialog variant. |
| `onPlay / onPause / onEnded / onTimeUpdate / onError` | `(event) => void` | — | no | Native media event callbacks. Time updates are not live announcements. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLVideoElement>` | — | no | Access to the active native video for programmatic playback changes. Null while a dialog is closed. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `variant`: `standard`, `minimal`, `dialog`
- `fit`: `contain`, `cover`
- `preload`: `none`, `metadata`, `auto`

## Usage

```jsx
import { VideoPlayer } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/VideoPlayer';

<VideoPlayer src='/media/film.webm' poster='/media/film.webp' title='A short film'
  tracks={[{ src: '/media/film.en.vtt', srcLang: 'en', label: 'English', default: true }]} />
```

## Accessibility

All controls have accessible names. Space or Enter activates focused buttons; the seek and volume sliders support arrow keys, Home and End. Captions use native text tracks; provide captions for speech and meaningful audio. Dialog traps focus, closes with Escape, and restores focus to its poster. Touch controls stay visible, and reduced motion removes elastic movement.

## Notes

- autoPlay, defaultMuted, and defaultVolume are initial preferences applied when a source mounts or its dialog opens. Updating them does not restart playback or directly update the active video’s muted state or volume. Use the native ref for subsequent programmatic changes.
- Only documented video props are supported; arbitrary native attributes such as crossOrigin are not forwarded. Cross-origin media setup belongs to the host integration. className and style apply to the outer player wrapper.
- The custom toolbar supports finite-duration files. Unknown or infinite durations disable seeking. Use nativeControls for live streams or device-specific playback features.
- Picture-in-picture and fullscreen appear only when supported. Their state follows browser events, and rejected requests show a recoverable message. Support depends on the browser, operating system, and embedding permissions.
- Custom controls remain visible. Below a 640px player width they flow below the video; larger standard players place them over the frame. Enabling captions keeps the controls below so they cannot cover the text. Minimal controls stay below the frame at every width.
- The Skiper 67, 91, and 97 references informed the interactions. This implementation uses Gaudi primitives and native media APIs; it does not load remote examples or copy registry source.

- Playground (Storybook `core-videoplayer--playground`)
- Minimal & elastic timeline (Storybook `core-videoplayer--minimal`)
- Poster to dialog (Storybook `core-videoplayer--poster-dialog`)
- Empty, error & source changes (Storybook `core-videoplayer--recovery`)
- Browser controls (Storybook `core-videoplayer--native`)

## Related

`core-dialog`, `mdx-preview`

## README

Native video playback with three presentations: `standard` adds a complete toolbar, `minimal` pares it back around an elastic seek rail, and `dialog` opens the player from a poster with a Gaudi Pointer label.

```jsx
import { VideoPlayer } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/VideoPlayer';

<VideoPlayer
  src='/media/film.webm'
  poster='/media/film.webp'
  title='A short film'
  tracks={[{ src: '/media/film.en.vtt', srcLang: 'en', label: 'English', default: true }]}
/>
```

`aspectRatio` defaults to `16 / 9`; `fit='cover'` crops the frame. Pass `variant='minimal'` or `variant='dialog'` for the other workflows. Dialog supports `open`, `defaultOpen`, and `onOpenChange`. It stops playback on close and restores focus to its poster.

`autoPlay`, `defaultMuted`, and `defaultVolume` are initial preferences applied when a source mounts or its dialog opens. They are not controlled playback props: changing them does not restart playback or directly update the active video's muted state or volume. Browser policy may reject autoplay; the player keeps Play available and explains the failure. `loop` and `preload` map to the native video. Media events drive the controls; `onPlay`, `onPause`, `onEnded`, `onTimeUpdate`, and `onError` receive native events. A forwarded `ref` points to the active HTMLVideoElement, or null while the dialog is closed; use it for subsequent programmatic playback changes. Changing `src` resets playback and ignores pending work from the old source.

The standard toolbar includes play/pause/replay, buffered seeking, mute, volume, caption selection, speed, and supported fullscreen/picture-in-picture actions. Minimal retains play, seeking, time, mute, captions, and supported fullscreen. The custom timeline supports finite-duration media; unknown or live durations disable seeking. Set `nativeControls` for browser-owned controls or device-specific/live playback. This still requires a browser-playable `src`; it does not add streaming adapters or codec support. Fullscreen and picture-in-picture depend on browser support and embedding permissions; failures leave inline playback available.

Buttons support Enter/Space. Sliders support arrow keys, Home and End, with spoken time/volume values. The dialog uses Gaudi’s focus trap and Escape handling. Reduced motion disables elastic movement. Touch targets enlarge, and controls wrap below videos in containers narrower than 640px. Captioned playback keeps controls below the frame at every width, preserving authored cue placement. Minimal controls always stay below the frame.

Provide accurate WebVTT captions for meaningful audio. Tracks default to `kind='captions'`; only captions and subtitles appear in the caption selector. Selecting a language or turning captions off changes only those track modes, leaving metadata and chapter track modes untouched. The component accepts the documented video props rather than forwarding arbitrary native attributes, including `crossOrigin`. Serve tracks from the same origin; cross-origin media setup belongs to the host integration. `className` and `style` apply to the outer player wrapper.

### Story assets and inspiration

The 12-second WebM, WebP poster, and English VTT in `.storybook/public/static/media/video-demo*` are local demo assets. The clip slowly zooms Gaudi’s existing `static/images/art/0.svg` with a title overlay and a quiet synthesized 220Hz tone fading in/out. It was generated from a browser render of the SVG with ImageMagick (960×540, Arial title) and FFmpeg (`zoompan`, VP9, 24fps, Opus); no external media is loaded. `video-invalid.webm` intentionally contains text to demonstrate media-error recovery.

Interaction references: [Skiper 67](https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper67), [Skiper 91](https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper91), and [Skiper 97](https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper97). Independently implemented with native media APIs and Gaudi components; no registry source is copied.

# WebPreview

> Core/WebPreview · core · `@gaudi/design-system/core/WebPreview`

A framed browser for a live or generated page: back, forward and reload, an editable address bar, open in a new tab, device widths, a sandboxed iframe with a loading state, an optional console, and a link preview card when a site refuses framing.

## Import

```js
import WebPreview from '@gaudi/design-system/core/WebPreview';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/core';
```

Exports: `DEFAULT_WEB_PREVIEW_SANDBOX`, `WebPreviewBody`, `WebPreviewConsole`, `WebPreviewDevices`, `WebPreviewHistoryButtons`, `WebPreviewNavigation`, `WebPreviewNavigationButton`, `WebPreviewOpenButton`, `WebPreviewRoot`, `WebPreviewUrl`, `countWebPreviewLogs`, `createWebPreviewHistory`, `default`, `defaultWebPreviewLabels`, `formatWebPreviewUrl`, `normalizeWebPreviewUrl`, `pushWebPreviewHistory`, `stepWebPreviewHistory`, `useWebPreview`, `webPreviewDevices`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url / defaultUrl` | `string` | `''` | no | Controlled or initial address. |
| `onUrlChange` | `(url) => void` | — | no | Called with each visited address. |
| `srcDoc` | `string \| (url) => string \| null` | — | no | Generated HTML instead of loading the address; a function serves several pages. |
| `title` | `string` | `Preview of <url>` | no | Accessible name of the framed page. |
| `device / defaultDevice` | `desktop \| tablet \| phone` | `desktop` | no | Frame width: full, 768px or 390px. Narrow screens scroll inside the frame. |
| `onDeviceChange` | `(device) => void` | — | no | Called with the chosen width. |
| `devices` | `boolean \| string[]` | `true` | no | Show the width toggle, or limit it. |
| `logs` | `Array<{ level, message, timestamp? }>` | — | no | Console entries; passing an array shows the console. |
| `defaultConsoleOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Open the console initially. |
| `embeddable` | `boolean` | `true` | no | false replaces the frame with a LinkPreview card. |
| `previewData` | `object` | — | no | Metadata or endpoint for that fallback card. |
| `endpoint` | `string` | — | no | Metadata or endpoint for that fallback card. |
| `sandbox` | `string` | `allow-scripts allow-forms allow-popups allow-presentation allow-modals` | no | iframe sandbox; allow-same-origin is left out on purpose. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Extra toolbar controls. |
| `labels` | `object` | `English` | no | Copy overrides. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { WebPreview } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<>
<WebPreview
  defaultUrl='https://preview.example.dev/'
  srcDoc={(url) => generatedPages[url]}
  logs={logs}
  title='Generated landing page'
/>

{/* A site that refuses framing: the app knows from the headers. */}
<WebPreview defaultUrl='https://github.com/vercel/next.js' embeddable={false} />
</>
```

## Accessibility

The toolbar is a labelled toolbar of named buttons, the address bar is a labelled text field that flags unusable input in an alert, the width toggle is a radio group, the iframe has a title, the body is aria-busy while loading, and the console is a disclosure over a role="log" list.

## Notes

- Compose WebPreviewRoot, WebPreviewNavigation, WebPreviewHistoryButtons, WebPreviewUrl, WebPreviewOpenButton, WebPreviewDevices, WebPreviewBody and WebPreviewConsole for a different toolbar.
- Browsers do not report blocked frames, so the app decides embeddable (for example from X-Frame-Options read by its preview endpoint).

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `core-webpreview--playground`)
- AI message with web preview (Storybook `core-webpreview--ai-message-with-web-preview`)
- Blocked embed (Storybook `core-webpreview--blocked-embed`)
- Controlled navigation (Storybook `core-webpreview--controlled-navigation`)

## Related

`core-linkpreview`

## README

A framed browser for showing a live or generated page inside an interface: back, forward and reload, an editable address bar, open in a new tab, device widths, a sandboxed iframe with a loading state, an optional console, and a LinkPreview card when a site refuses to be framed. Use it for assistant replies that built a page, deploy previews and documentation demos.

### Usage

```jsx
import { WebPreview } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<WebPreview
  defaultUrl='https://preview.example.dev/'
  srcDoc={(url) => generatedPages[url]}
  logs={logs}
  title='Generated landing page'
/>

// The app knows a site refuses framing (its preview endpoint can read X-Frame-Options).
<WebPreview defaultUrl='https://github.com/vercel/next.js' embeddable={false} previewData={payload} />
```

- `url` / `defaultUrl` with `onUrlChange`; `device` / `defaultDevice` (`desktop`, `tablet` 768px, `phone` 390px) with `onDeviceChange`. Narrow screens scroll inside the frame, never the page.
- `srcDoc` renders generated HTML; a function `(url) => html | null` serves several pages so the address bar works offline.
- `logs` (`{ level: 'log' | 'info' | 'warn' | 'error', message, timestamp? }`) shows the console; the host collects them (for example over `postMessage`), the preview never reads the framed page.
- `sandbox` defaults to `allow-scripts allow-forms allow-popups allow-presentation allow-modals`. `allow-same-origin` is left out on purpose: with scripts it would let the page reach the host.
- The address bar adds `https://` to bare hosts and refuses `javascript:`, `data:` and `file:` addresses (`normalizeWebPreviewUrl`).

### Parts

Compose `WebPreviewRoot`, `WebPreviewNavigation`, `WebPreviewHistoryButtons`, `WebPreviewNavigationButton`, `WebPreviewUrl`, `WebPreviewOpenButton`, `WebPreviewDevices`, `WebPreviewBody` and `WebPreviewConsole` for a different toolbar; `useWebPreview()` reads the state. The history, address and log rules are pure functions in the same entry.

### Accessibility

The controls sit in a labelled toolbar with named buttons and tooltips, the address bar is a labelled field that reports unusable input in an alert, the width toggle is a radio group, the iframe has a `title`, the body is `aria-busy` while loading, and the console is a disclosure over a `role="log"` list whose toggle names errors and warnings.

## README

### Patterns

The app-shell examples (`Blocks/App Shell`) are Gaudi compositions for knowledge, reading, research and finance workspaces: a library rail, a reading desk, research projects, a digest inbox, a publishing console, notebook tabs, a research assistant, a newsletter reader, study chat, two top-bar layouts (collections and journal), crawler control, a source network and a finance dashboard. Every example follows these conventions so parallel work stays consistent.

**Files and names**

- Fixture `src/components/blocks/AppShell/stories/fixtures/app-shell/app-shell-<slug>.jsx` exports `Pattern`; the slug is a short descriptive kebab-case name (for example `app-shell-library-rail`), never a number. Import Gaudi parts directly from public namespaces such as `@gaudi/design-system/blocks/AppShell`, `@gaudi/design-system/core/Button`, `@gaudi/design-system/icons/RegistryIcon`, and `@gaudi/design-system/hooks/interaction/use-hotkey`. Package self-reference lets the fixture and its copyable source share the same imports.
- Story `export const <Slug> = { name, ...pattern('<slug>', description), play }` lives in an owner-local story file: most patterns use `AppShellPatterns.stories.jsx`, the library rail is the primary story in `AppShell.stories.jsx`, and finance uses `FinanceDashboard.stories.jsx`. Keep the shared `Blocks/App Shell` title and owner ID. `name` is `Topology · key features` (for example `Icon rail · workspace switcher, nested nav and user menu`); the description says what the reader can do and how it behaves in a narrow frame.
- Each story has a play test built from `AppShell.story-steps.js` helpers: `expectFramed`, `openNavigation` (the docked sidebar, or the phone sheet opened from the header) and `desktopSidebar`. Cover the current page (`aria-current`), the example's actions, any menus or nested navigation, and collapse/expand when the sidebar is docked. The vitest browser is phone sized, so tests must pass in both layouts.
- Add the example to `src/docs/catalogue/coverage.json` (`name`, `title`, `description`, `file`, `sha256` of the fixture bytes, `storyId` `blocks-application-appshell--<slug>`), then run `pnpm catalogue:sync`.

**Visual vocabulary** (reuse these parts; do not restyle them per fixture)

- `AppShellFrame` is the root of every example: the bordered app window on the shared card radius, 48rem tall by default (40rem on phones), with internal scrolling. Use `surface='muted'` (default) when the content sits in an inset panel and `surface='default'` for a plain surface with a flush or floating sidebar.
- `SidebarProvider` → `Sidebar` (`collapsible='icon'` for rails, `variant='floating'` for cards) → `AppShellPanel` (the `main` landmark; `inset` by default, `inset={false}` for flush content). `AppShellHeader` holds breadcrumbs, search or actions. Place `SidebarTrigger` first in the header, or at the top inside `SidebarHeader` with a header trigger on phones; `AppShellBody` holds the page.
- `AppShellNav` follows explicit item `href` links; items without `href` invoke `onValueChange` without navigation. Modifier-clicks keep native link behavior. It renders sidebar groups from data: icons or status dots, count `badge`, inline `tag`, live `indicator`, nested `items` (collapsible, a flyout menu on the icon rail, remembered section view), `collapsible` group labels, `hideOnRail`, and `actions` row menus. Use `itemClassName` for topology-specific active rows (for example raised rows on a floating card).
- Collapsed `SidebarMenuButton` rows center their first visual and keep later children screen-reader-only. Portraits are capped at 24px to fit the rail; do not compensate with negative margins. Labels and account menus remain accessible.
- `AppShellNav` also takes `item.leading` (a custom mark such as a `ProgressRing` or a presence avatar; speak its value through `status`) and `action` (a `SidebarGroupAction` at the end of the group label). Rows with a count badge keep their label clear of it.
- Use `SidebarTrigger` at the top of the shell, inside the sidebar header or before the breadcrumbs. Keep the trigger visible and in the same place when collapsed; do not add a floating edge toggle or reserve a gutter for one. Several shells share the docs page, so give at most one of them the ⌘B shortcut (`shortcut={false}` on the others).
- Compose Core `Skeleton` for loading content. Rich placeholder layouts live only in `stories/fixtures/AppShellPlaceholder.jsx` and the Loading layouts story; they are example compositions, not package exports.
- The research-assistant, newsletter-reader and study-chat shells add: `SidebarProvider defaultWidth` with `SidebarResizeHandle` (a focusable separator on the edge: drag, arrow keys, Home/End, double-click resets), Core Skeleton compositions for an unloaded conversation, and `AppShellNav` people rows (`avatar`, `presence`, `suffix`), bare counts (`badge: { label, variant: 'plain' }`), a hover `quickAction` beside the row menu and a `action`. Chat shells compose the Chat parts (`ChatModelSelect` with model `icon`/`details`, `ChatPromptComposer actions`) and Core `EmptyState` with a labelled list of Core `Button` starter prompts in a responsive grid.
- More placeholder presets: `tiles` (3 × 3 block cards), `board` (tiles under a row of blank cards), `quad` (four short cards above a 2 × 2 grid) and `stack` (three metric tiles above a tall list), from the `block`, `blank`, `tile` and `rows` kinds.
- Top bars spanning the window: give `SidebarProvider` `className='flex-col'`, render the header first and put `Sidebar` and `AppShellPanel` in a `relative flex` row below it. `AppShellNotifications` is the bell and notifications sheet (`inset` floats it); `Sidebar` takes `mobileWidth`, `mobileClassName`, `mobileTitle` and `mobileDescription` for a wider or renamed phone sheet; `AppShellNav` takes `labelIcon` and `labelClassName` for route-group headings.
- Overlays: menus and tooltips portal to the page; the phone sidebar sheet opens inside the frame. Command palettes (`CommandDialog`) open over the page.
- Gaudi tokens only: semantic colours (`bg-success`, `text-text-muted`…), `rounded-(--ds-radius-control)` / `--ds-radius-card` for tiles and cards (circles only for dots and avatars), registry icons through `RegistryIcon`, brand marks from `src/icons/brands`, Gaudi's generated illustrations from Storybook's local `/avatars/...` assets for avatars, and the shared hooks (`useHotkey` for ⌘K).
- Check each example at 320, 390, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1600 px in light and dark: the frame border is visible inside the preview, nothing overflows the page, and the rail, nested navigation, menus and phone sheet work.

#### Finance dashboard example

[FinanceDashboard.stories.jsx](stories/FinanceDashboard.stories.jsx) presents the [finance dashboard fixture](stories/fixtures/app-shell/app-shell-finance-dashboard.jsx) as a copyable composition. It combines flat, labelled navigation groups and a compact search header with stacked revenue bars, report totals, visitor distribution, product sales and a customer table. The layout uses App Shell and Dashboard parts, `BarChart`, `DataTable` and Core controls; actions and selection use Gaudi's default accent, while charts inherit the standard chart palette. Success colours are reserved for positive changes and account or payment status.

Navigation switches local views, search finds pages and record details, role and plan filters update the customer table, and report, transaction and invoice tables offer CSV export. All figures and records are illustrative fixture data. Copy the story's public-import source into the consuming application, replace the sample data and `/avatars/` assets, and connect routing, services, permissions and persistence there. The fixture and its private helpers are examples, not package exports.

The frame is 62rem tall with a 40rem compact height and internal panel scrolling. Narrow frames use the sidebar sheet, stack the dashboard panels and filters, and keep horizontal table scrolling inside each table. Preserve the frame-scoped ⌘/Ctrl+K search shortcut so other examples on the page do not respond. Closing record details returns focus to the opening control, with the search button as the fallback when a search result has unmounted.

### Overview

Application frames at three levels:

- **`AppShell`**: a simple responsive workspace with a navigation rail (or a top bar), a mobile navigation sheet, a header, the content landmark, a skip link, an optional detail rail and an optional status bar. It stays in document flow.
- **Sidebar parts** (`SidebarProvider`, `Sidebar`, `SidebarInset`, `SidebarTrigger`, `SidebarRail`, menus, groups and sub-menus): for richer shells, such as a rail that collapses to icons, floating and inset sidebars, nested groups with badges and row menus, secondary panels, and right-hand inspectors. On phones the sidebar becomes a Sheet drawer.
- **Frame parts** (`AppShellFrame`, `AppShellPanel`, `AppShellHeader`, `AppShellBody`, `AppShellNav`): present either kind of shell as an app window inside a page, a marketing section or a documentation preview.

### Usage

```jsx
import AppShell, { AppShellFrame } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/AppShell';
import { SkeletonRoot as Skeleton } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Skeleton';

<AppShell
  brand='Gaudi'
  navigation={navigation}
  header={<h1>Articles</h1>}
  aside={<IssueDetails />}
  statusBar={<span>All changes saved</span>}
>
  <DataTable columns={columns} rows={articles} searchable sortable pagination />
</AppShell>

// Sidebar-free apps put the brand and navigation in the header.
<AppShell layout='topbar' brand='Gaudi' navigation={sections} header={<UserMenu />}>…</AppShell>

// Inside a page, present the shell as an app window.
<AppShellFrame>
  <AppShell brand='Gaudi' navigation={navigation}>…</AppShell>
</AppShellFrame>
```

```jsx
import {
  AppShellBody, AppShellFrame, AppShellHeader, AppShellNav, AppShellPanel,
  Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarProvider, SidebarTrigger
} from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/AppShell';
import { SkeletonRoot as Skeleton } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Skeleton';

<AppShellFrame>
  <SidebarProvider storageKey='gaudi-sidebar'>
    <Sidebar collapsible='icon'>
      <SidebarContent role='navigation' aria-label='Workspace'>
        <AppShellNav label='Library' items={pages} value={page} onValueChange={setPage} />
      </SidebarContent>
    </Sidebar>
    <AppShellPanel>
      <AppShellHeader><SidebarTrigger />{breadcrumb}</AppShellHeader>
      <AppShellBody>
        <Skeleton className='m-4 h-64' />
      </AppShellBody>
    </AppShellPanel>
  </SidebarProvider>
</AppShellFrame>
```

### Frame

`AppShellFrame` draws a bordered window on `--ds-radius-card` with clipped overflow and a fixed height (`height`, 56rem by default and 40rem in compact layouts; the CSS variables `--ds-app-shell-frame-height` and `--ds-app-shell-frame-height-compact` also set it). Content scrolls inside: `AppShellPanel` (and the simple `AppShell` workspace) scroll on their own, and the sidebar is positioned against the frame instead of the viewport. The frame measures itself, and sidebar parts switch to the phone layout when the frame, not the viewport, is narrower than `compactBelow` (768px). The phone sheet portals into the frame, so it opens inside the window. Menus, tooltips and dialogs still portal to the page.

### API

| Prop / export                             | Type                       | Contract                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `brand / navigation / header / footer`    | ReactNode                  | Supplied slot content; the host owns route state and active links.                         |
| `layout`                                  | `sidebar` / `topbar`       | A navigation rail, or brand and navigation in the header.                                  |
| `aside / asideLabel`                      | ReactNode / string         | A named complementary rail beside the content; stacks below it under xl.                   |
| `statusBar`                               | ReactNode                  | A status strip under the content.                                                          |
| `children`                                | ReactNode                  | Page content inside the shell main landmark.                                               |
| `navigationLabel / menuLabel / skipLabel` | string                     | Localized accessible labels.                                                               |
| `className`                               | string                     | Root composition; the desktop rail begins at 1024px.                                       |
| `AppShellFrame.height / compactBelow`     | string or number / number  | Window height (56rem; 40rem when compact) and the frame width for the phone layout (768).     |
| `AppShellFrame.surface / label`           | `muted` / `default`; string | The window surface, and an optional region name.                                          |
| `AppShellPanel.inset`                     | boolean                    | A bordered panel set into the frame (default), or flush beside a floating sidebar.         |
| `AppShellHeader.bordered`                 | boolean                    | A rule under the sticky panel header.                                                      |
| `AppShellNav`                             | items, value, …            | Data-driven sidebar group; see the Patterns section and the component docs.                |
| `SidebarProvider.storageKey`              | string                     | Restores and saves the expanded state in localStorage after mount.                         |
| `SidebarProvider.shortcut`                | string / false             | The ⌘/Ctrl key that toggles the sidebar (`b`); `false` turns it off.                       |
| `SidebarProvider.labels`                  | object                     | `expanded`, `collapsed` announcements and the `toggle` trigger name. |
| `Sidebar.variant / collapsible / side`    | string                     | `sidebar`, `floating` or `inset`; `offcanvas`, `icon` or `none`; edge.                     |
| `SidebarTrigger.label / tooltip`          | string / boolean           | Trigger name, and a tooltip with the shortcut keys.                                        |
| `SidebarMenuButton.tooltip`               | string / object            | Names the item on the collapsed icon rail.                                                 |

### Accessibility

Keep the skip link and the main landmark, and name each navigation and complementary region. Mark the current page with `aria-current` (`AppShellNav` does; a remembered section view is only highlighted). The trigger reports `aria-expanded` and `aria-keyshortcuts`, and expanding or collapsing is announced politely. Keep the trigger at the top of the sidebar or before the breadcrumbs, including when collapsed. On phones the sidebar is a Sheet that traps focus and returns it to the trigger, and choosing a page closes it. Collapsed icon rails name every item with a tooltip, and nested sections open as menus. Status dots carry a spoken `status`; placeholder grids are decorative and hidden from assistive technology, and their skeletons do not animate.

When several shells share a page (as in these docs), turn the shortcut off on all but one, because each provider listens on the window.

### Ownership and verification

The host supplies data, translations, network calls, permissions and persistence. Gaudi owns layout, semantics and local interaction. Examples document working behavior and states, with Storybook interaction/axe checks and a server-rendering contract test alongside the component.

# Auth

> Blocks/Auth · blocks · `@gaudi/design-system/blocks/AuthForm`

Sign-in, sign-up, magic-link, passkey and single sign-on screens: AuthForm handles the fields, feedback and providers, and Screen frames it beside imagery, quotes or logos.

## Import

```js
import Auth from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/AuthForm';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks';
```

Exports: `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `password \| email \| signup` | `password` | no | Authentication form fields; email sends a sign-in link without a password, signup adds a name and a new password. Password fields have a reveal button. |
| `onSubmit` | `(values) => void \| Promise<void>` | — | no | Host-owned authentication request. |
| `title / submitLabel` | `string` | `Sign in` | no | Form heading and submission action. |
| `description / footer` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Instructions and related actions. |
| `nameLabel / emailLabel / passwordLabel` | `string` | `Full name / Email / Password` | no | Input labels. |
| `emailPlaceholder / passwordPlaceholder` | `string` | — | no | Optional example text inside the fields. |
| `passwordMinLength` | `number` | — | no | Optional host-defined native minimum; signup has no built-in password length policy. |
| `passwordHint` | `ReactNode \| false` | `Per mode` | no | Help text under the password field; false hides it. |
| `passwordAction` | `ReactNode` | — | no | A link beside the password label, such as Forgot password. |
| `identifier` | `email \| username` | `email` | no | Ask for an email, or a username that also accepts an email. |
| `providers` | `Array<{ id, label, icon }>` | — | no | Single sign-on buttons above the form, sharing its pending and error state. |
| `onProvider` | `(id) => void \| Promise<void>` | — | no | Single sign-on buttons above the form, sharing its pending and error state. |
| `providerLayout` | `grid \| stack` | `grid` | no | Provider buttons side by side or stacked, and the divider before the email fields. |
| `dividerLabel` | `string` | `or` | no | Provider buttons side by side or stacked, and the divider before the email fields. |
| `showPasswordLabel / hidePasswordLabel` | `string` | `Show password / Hide password` | no | Accessible names of the password reveal button, for translation. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Extra fields before the submit button, such as keep me signed in or terms. |
| `pendingLabel` | `string` | `Per mode` | no | Submit text while the request is pending. |
| `successMessage / errorMessage` | `string` | `Built-in feedback` | no | Submission result messages. |
| `Screen` | `component` | — | no | Full-screen frame: the form beside an optional aside, with header and footer bands. See the Screen frame example for its props. |

## Variants

- `mode`: `password`, `email`, `signup`
- `identifier`: `email`, `username`
- `providerLayout`: `grid`, `stack`

## Usage

```jsx
import AuthForm from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/AuthForm';

<AuthForm mode='password' onSubmit={signIn} />
```

## Accessibility

Native labels and autocomplete support password managers; the password keeps its label and hint when revealed. Pending submissions and provider redirects share one guard so requests never overlap; errors retain the user’s values.

- Choose a sign-in method — registry item `@gaudi/screens-sign-in-methods` (uses `AuthForm`, `Button`, `Dropbox`, `GaudiBrand`, `InputOTP`, `InputOTPGroup`, `InputOTPSeparator`, `InputOTPSlot`, `Label`, `Link`, `Loom`, `RegistryIcon`, `Screen`, `Stripe`, `Supabase`)
- Split with imagery — registry item `@gaudi/screens-split-imagery` (uses `AuthForm`, `Borealis`, `GaudiBrand`, `Link`, `RegistryIcon`, `Screen`, `ToggleGroupItem`, `ToggleGroupRoot`)
- Split with testimonials — registry item `@gaudi/screens-split-testimonials` (uses `AuthForm`, `GaudiBrand`, `Link`, `RegistryIcon`, `Screen`, `ScreenTestimonial`)

## Related

`core-input`

## README

Password and email-link form recipes with native validation, pending state and recoverable errors. onSubmit receives form values. Applications own providers, credentials, sessions and navigation.

### Usage

```jsx
<AuthForm
  title='Sign in'
  description='Continue to your writing workspace.'
  onSubmit={signIn}
/>
```

Reuse the recipe for other account steps by renaming the copy: a reset request is `mode='email'` with its own `submitLabel`
and `pendingLabel`.

```jsx
<AuthForm
  title='Reset your password'
  mode='email'
  submitLabel='Send reset link'
  pendingLabel='Sending…'
  emailPlaceholder='you@example.com'
  successMessage='If that address has an account, a reset link is on its way.'
  onSubmit={requestReset}
/>
```

Add single sign-on above the email fields and a reset link beside the password:

```jsx
<AuthForm
  title='Welcome back'
  passwordAction={<Link href='/reset'>Forgot password?</Link>}
  providers={[{ id: 'google', label: 'Google', icon: <Icon name='Google' decorative /> }]}
  onProvider={startOAuth}
  onSubmit={signIn}
/>
```

### API

| Prop / export                                 | Type                         | Contract                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onSubmit`                                    | function({email, password?}) | Required host-owned authentication callback. Reject to show an error. |
| `mode`                                        | password, email or signup    | Password, email-link or sign-up form (name, email, new password).     |
| `title / description / footer`                | ReactNode                    | Product context and links.                                            |
| `submitLabel / successMessage / errorMessage` | string                       | Action and outcome copy.                                              |
| `nameLabel / emailLabel / passwordLabel`      | string                       | Visible accessible field labels.                                      |
| `emailPlaceholder / passwordPlaceholder`      | string                       | Optional example text inside the fields. No placeholder by default.   |
| `passwordHint`                                | ReactNode or false           | Help text under the password; defaults per mode, `false` hides it.    |
| `passwordMinLength` | number | Optional native minimum supplied by the host; signup imposes no minimum by default. Pair it with a matching `passwordHint`. |
| `passwordAction`                              | ReactNode                    | A link beside the password label, such as Forgot password.            |
| `identifier`                                  | email or username            | `username` asks for a username field that also accepts an email.      |
| `providers / onProvider`                      | {id, label, icon}[] / fn(id) | Sign-on buttons above the form; they share its pending and error state. |
| `providerLayout / dividerLabel`               | grid or stack / string       | Provider buttons side by side or stacked, and the divider copy.       |
| `showPasswordLabel / hidePasswordLabel` | string | Reveal-button names; default `Show password` / `Hide password`. |
| `children`                                    | ReactNode                    | Extra fields before submit, such as keep me signed in or terms.       |
| `pendingLabel`                                | string                       | Submit text while `onSubmit` is pending. Defaults per mode.           |

Email identifiers use `EmailInput`, so they inherit the default smooth caret and single-address pattern validation. Username identifiers remain text inputs; masked passwords retain the native caret. A surrounding `InputConfigProvider caretMode='native'` opts the form out of smooth mode.

### Ownership and verification

The host supplies password policy (`passwordMinLength` and matching help text), data, translations, network calls, permissions and persistence. Gaudi owns layout, semantics and local interaction. Examples document working behavior and states, with Storybook interaction/axe checks and a server-rendering contract test alongside the component.

# Chat

> Blocks/Chat · blocks · `@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Chat`

The chat frame: a shell for a full page or a sidebar assistant that composes the Chat parts: the thread, the composer, sessions, files, the plan and activity.

## Import

```js
import Chat from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Chat';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks';
```

Exports: `ChatShell`, `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ChatShell.variant` | `page \| sidebar` | `page` | no | Page lays navigation, thread and details side by side from md and xl; sidebar is one narrow column. Side content moves into Sheets on narrow screens. |
| `ChatShell.title` | `string` | — | no | Conversation heading and actions. |
| `subtitle` | `string` | — | no | Conversation heading and actions. |
| `headerActions` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Conversation heading and actions. |
| `ChatShell.navigation / details / composer` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Side columns and the composer, filled with Chat parts such as ChatSessionList, ChatPlan and ChatPromptComposer. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Content composed from the exported parts. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { ChatShell } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Chat';
import { ChatPlan, ChatSessionList, ChatMessageParts, ChatMessageScroller, ChatMessageScrollerContent, ChatMessageScrollerItem, ChatMessageScrollerProvider, ChatMessageScrollerViewport, ChatPromptComposer } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<ChatMessageScrollerProvider autoScroll>
  <ChatShell
    title='Local-first drafts post'
    navigation={<ChatSessionList sessions={sessions} activeId={activeId} onSelect={openChat} onRename={rename} onDelete={remove} />}
    details={<ChatPlan steps={plan} />}
    composer={<ChatPromptComposer status={streaming ? 'streaming' : 'ready'} onSubmit={send} onStop={stop} />}
  >
    <ChatMessageScroller>
      <ChatMessageScrollerViewport aria-label='Conversation'>
        <ChatMessageScrollerContent>
          {turns.map((turn) => (
            <ChatMessageScrollerItem key={turn.id} messageId={turn.id} scrollAnchor={turn.role === 'user'}>
              <ChatMessageParts parts={turn.parts} streaming={turn.streaming} />
            </ChatMessageScrollerItem>
          ))}
        </ChatMessageScrollerContent>
      </ChatMessageScrollerViewport>
    </ChatMessageScroller>
  </ChatShell>
</ChatMessageScrollerProvider>
```

## Accessibility

The thread owns its scrolling (ChatMessageScroller) so the page never scrolls, the header names the conversation, Sheets restore focus to the button that opened them, and every icon action has a label.

## Related

`chat-chatsessionlist`

## README

`ChatShell` frames a conversation, either as a full page or as a narrow assistant panel beside other work. Everything inside it comes from the Chat area (`@gaudi/design-system/chat`):

- the turns: `ChatMessage`, `ChatBubble`, `ChatMessageParts` and `ChatMessageScroller`;
- the composer: `ChatPromptComposer`, `ChatPromptQueue` and `ChatModelSelect`;
- the side columns: `ChatSessionList`, `ChatWorkspace`, `ChatFileExplorer`, `ChatPlan` and `ChatActivity`;
- the empty state and navigation: Core `EmptyState` with Core `Button` starter prompts, and `ChatThreadNav`.

The shell adds layout only: columns, Sheets on small screens and focus return. It has no chat behaviour of its own, so every example here is a composition you can copy.

### Usage

```jsx
import { ChatShell } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Chat';
import { ChatPlan, ChatSessionList, ChatMessageParts, ChatMessageScroller, ChatMessageScrollerContent, ChatMessageScrollerItem, ChatMessageScrollerProvider, ChatMessageScrollerViewport, ChatPromptComposer } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<ChatMessageScrollerProvider autoScroll>
  <ChatShell
    title='Local-first drafts post'
    navigation={<ChatSessionList sessions={sessions} activeId={activeId} onSelect={openChat} onRename={rename} onDelete={remove} />}
    details={<ChatPlan steps={plan} />}
    composer={<ChatPromptComposer status={streaming ? 'streaming' : 'ready'} onSubmit={send} onStop={stop} />}
  >
    <ChatMessageScroller>
      <ChatMessageScrollerViewport aria-label='Conversation'>
        <ChatMessageScrollerContent>
          {turns.map((turn) => (
            <ChatMessageScrollerItem key={turn.id} messageId={turn.id} scrollAnchor={turn.role === 'user'}>
              <ChatMessageParts parts={turn.parts} streaming={turn.streaming} />
            </ChatMessageScrollerItem>
          ))}
        </ChatMessageScrollerContent>
      </ChatMessageScrollerViewport>
    </ChatMessageScroller>
  </ChatShell>
</ChatMessageScrollerProvider>
```

### Parts

| Part | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `ChatShell` | `variant` page or sidebar. Page shows `navigation`, the thread and `details` side by side from md and xl; below that they open in Sheets from labelled header buttons, which get focus back when the Sheet closes. Sidebar is one column with navigation in a Sheet. `title`, `subtitle`, `headerActions` and `composer` fill the frame; the thread (`children`) owns its scrolling. |

Each part placed in the shell is documented on its own Chat page.

### Session navigation

[Session panel](?path=/story/blocks-chat--session-panel) shows a compact assistant with **History** and **New chat** in its persistent header. History replaces the transcript with `ChatSessionList` inside the panel and hides the composer. **Back to conversation** resumes the current chat; choosing another session opens that session's transcript and saved draft. Search, rename, and delete stay part of the existing session list.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Button } from '@gaudi/design-system';
import { ChatShell } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Chat';
import { ChatSessionList, ChatPromptComposer } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

const [historyOpen, setHistoryOpen] = useState(false);
const openChat = (id) => { setActiveId(id); setHistoryOpen(false); };

<ChatShell
  variant='sidebar'
  title={activeSession.title}
  headerActions={<>
    <Button size='xs' variant='ghost' aria-expanded={historyOpen} onClick={() => setHistoryOpen((open) => !open)}>
      {historyOpen ? 'Back to conversation' : 'History'}
    </Button>
    <Button size='xs' variant='ghost' onClick={() => { startChat(); setHistoryOpen(false); }}>New chat</Button>
  </>}
  composer={historyOpen ? null : <ChatPromptComposer value={activeSession.draft} onValueChange={saveDraft} onSubmit={send} />}
>
  {historyOpen ? (
    <div className='min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto p-3'>
      <ChatSessionList sessions={sessions} activeId={activeSession.id} onSelect={openChat} onRename={renameChat} onDelete={deleteChat} />
    </div>
  ) : conversation}
</ChatShell>
```

Place the state and composition inside the host component. `conversation` is its transcript view; `activeSession` supplies that session's title and draft. Store transcripts and drafts by session ID, and update the controlled session list after rename or deletion. When deleting the active session, choose a remaining chat or create a new one. The shell and session list do not own persistence or message delivery.

[Session page](?path=/story/blocks-chat--session-page) uses the `navigation` slot shown in Usage above. The list sits beside the transcript on larger screens and opens in the shell's existing navigation Sheet on narrow screens. Both layouts use the same `ChatSessionList` owner and host state. Its [primary playground](?path=/story/chat-chatsessionlist--playground) also shows the complete compact chat context.

### Accessibility

The page never scrolls; the thread does, inside a labelled region. While a reply streams, mark it `aria-busy` (ChatMessageParts does this) and announce the start and the end once in a polite status. Never announce every token. Every icon action has a label, and choosing a chat or file in the phone Sheet closes it and returns focus to the button that opened it.

### Workspace context panel

The **Workspace context: agents, files and preview** example places `ChatWorkspace` in `details`. It combines an agent roster, scoped file exploration and a host-owned Dialog preview. Control `view`, `agentId` and file selection above `ChatShell` so desktop and mobile copies share state. The existing shell supplies the mobile details Sheet.

### Welcome composition

**Welcome: orb, input and starter prompts** combines the existing `ChatPersona`, Core EmptyState parts, `ChatPromptComposer`, `ChatModelSelect` and Core `Button`. Choosing a starter fills and focuses the input; submitting calls the host. A compact example shows prompt chips without the orb. These are compositions on this page, with no separate ChatWelcome or ChatPromptSuggestions owner. For follow-ups within a reply, use `ChatMessageParts` with a `suggestions` part and `onSuggestion`.

# Dashboard

> Blocks/Dashboard · blocks · `@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Dashboard`

Full dashboards composed from Stat Cards, Charts, DataTable and Core parts, on a grid that reflows by its own width, with a period toolbar for presets, a custom range and comparison.

## Import

```js
import Dashboard from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Dashboard';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks';
```

Exports: `DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_LABELS`, `DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_PERIODS`, `DashboardGrid`, `DashboardPanel`, `DashboardToolbar`, `dashboardSpan`, `default`, `resolveDashboardPeriod`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DashboardGrid.label` | `string` | — | no | Names the dashboard region. |
| `DashboardPanel.span / spanMd / rowSpan` | `number` | `12 / derived / —` | no | Columns of twelve on wide containers, of six on medium ones, and rows to span. |
| `DashboardPanel.title / description / action / toolbar / footer` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Panel heading, help, header action, controls row and footer. |
| `DashboardPanel.scroll` | `x \| y \| both` | — | no | A labelled, focusable scroll region for wide tables and long lists. |
| `scrollLabel` | `string` | — | no | A labelled, focusable scroll region for wide tables and long lists. |
| `maxHeight` | `CSS length` | — | no | A labelled, focusable scroll region for wide tables and long lists. |
| `dashboardSpan(span, spanMd, rowSpan)` | `function` | — | no | Grid placement classes for any child, such as a StatCard. |
| `DashboardToolbar.period / defaultPeriod / onPeriodChange` | `string / function` | `30d` | no | Active preset, or custom. |
| `DashboardToolbar.range / defaultRange / onRangeChange` | `{ from, to } / function` | — | no | Custom date range from the calendar. |
| `DashboardToolbar.compare / defaultCompare / onCompareChange` | `boolean / function` | `false` | no | Compare with the previous period. |
| `DashboardToolbar.onChange` | `(period) => void` | — | no | Resolved { period, from, to, days, previous, compare } on every change. |
| `DashboardToolbar.periods` | `Period[]` | `DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_PERIODS` | no | Presets, optional controls, the end date and copy. |
| `allowCustom` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Presets, optional controls, the end date and copy. |
| `showCompare` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Presets, optional controls, the end date and copy. |
| `today` | `Date` | `now` | no | Presets, optional controls, the end date and copy. |
| `labels` | `object` | `English` | no | Presets, optional controls, the end date and copy. |
| `resolveDashboardPeriod(period, options)` | `function` | — | no | The dates a period covers and the equally long period before it. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { DashboardGrid, DashboardPanel } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Dashboard';

<DashboardGrid label='Overview'>
  <DashboardPanel title='Traffic' span={8}>{trafficChart}</DashboardPanel>
  <DashboardPanel title='Sources' span={4}>{sourceList}</DashboardPanel>
</DashboardGrid>
```

## Accessibility

The grid and each panel are named regions; panel titles are headings. Scrolling panel bodies take focus so the keyboard can scroll them. The toolbar presets are a single-choice group, the calendar opens in a popover, and the active range is announced politely.

## Related

`core-datatable`

## README

Full dashboards for blogs and applications, composed from Stat Cards, Charts, DataTable, FilterBar, Tabs, Progress and the other Core parts. Dashboard adds only the two pieces those owners don't cover: a grid that reflows by its own width, and a period toolbar.

### Usage

```jsx
import { DashboardGrid, DashboardPanel, DashboardToolbar, dashboardSpan } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Dashboard';
import { StatCard } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/StatCard';
import { AreaChart } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts';
import DataTable from '@gaudi/design-system/core/DataTable';

<DashboardToolbar defaultPeriod='30d' defaultCompare onChange={(period) => load(period)} />
<DashboardGrid label='Shop revenue'>
  <StatCard label='Revenue' value='$184,950' delta='+11.6%' deltaDirection='up' deltaTone='success' className={dashboardSpan(3)} />
  <DashboardPanel title='Revenue by product line' span={8}>
    <AreaChart framed={false} data={revenue} stacked series={series} />
  </DashboardPanel>
  <DashboardPanel title='Order queue' span={12}>
    <DataTable caption='Order queue' rows={orders} columns={columns} sortable searchable exportable />
  </DashboardPanel>
</DashboardGrid>
```

### API

| Prop / export | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `DashboardGrid` | A container-query grid: one column when narrow, six from 42rem and twelve from 64rem of its own width, so it fits a page, a split view or a sidebar. `label` names the region. |
| `DashboardPanel` | A titled panel on the Core Card. `span` (of twelve), `spanMd` (of six) and `rowSpan` place it; `title`, `description`, `action`, `toolbar` and `footer` fill it. `scroll` (`x`, `y`, `both`) with `scrollLabel` and `maxHeight` makes the body a focusable scroll region. |
| `dashboardSpan(span, spanMd, rowSpan)` | Placement classes for any grid child, such as a StatCard. |
| `DashboardToolbar` | Period presets, a custom range from the Calendar, a compare switch and a slot for actions. `period`, `range` and `compare` are each controlled or uncontrolled; `onChange` receives `{ period, from, to, days, previous, compare }`. |
| `resolveDashboardPeriod(period, { today, range, periods })` | The dates a period covers and the equally long period before it. |
| `DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_PERIODS` / `DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_LABELS` | The 7d, 30d, 90d and 12m presets and the English copy. |

Charts inside a panel usually pass `framed={false}` so the panel supplies the border and title. Tables keep their own scroll region; give a panel `scroll` only for custom content such as a timesheet.

### Accessibility

The grid and panels are named regions, and panel titles are headings. A scrolling panel body is focusable so keyboard users can scroll it. The presets are a single-choice group, the custom range opens in a popover, and the toolbar announces the active range, with its comparison, politely when it changes.

# Forms

> Blocks/Forms · blocks · `@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Forms`

Form behaviour on the Core Field parts: validation with accessible errors, a summary that takes focus after a failed submit, values you edit in place and live character counts.

## Import

```js
import Forms from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Forms';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks';
```

Exports: `CharacterCount`, `EditableField`, `FormErrorSummary`, `default`, `useFormValidation`, `validators`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `useFormValidation({ initialValues, rules, validateOn })` | `hook` | `validateOn 'blur'` | no | Values, errors and handlers. Rules map a field name to one validator or a list, run in order; errors show on blur or submit and re-check as the person types. |
| `form.field(name, { describedBy })` | `props` | — | no | id, name, value, onChange, onBlur, aria-invalid and aria-describedby for a text-like control. |
| `form.setValue / setValues / handleSubmit / reset` | `functions` | — | no | Update values, block invalid submits (onValid receives the values) and restore a state. |
| `validators` | `required \| email \| minLength \| maxLength \| pattern \| min \| max` | — | no | Message-returning validators; custom rules receive (value, values). |
| `FormErrorSummary.form` | `form` | — | no | Lists errors after a submit, takes focus and links each entry to its control. |
| `labels` | `Record<name, string>` | — | no | Lists errors after a submit, takes focus and links each entry to its control. |
| `title` | `string` | — | no | Lists errors after a submit, takes focus and links each entry to its control. |
| `EditableField.label` | `string` | — | no | A label and value with Edit; Save calls onSave and closes, a thrown error keeps it open. |
| `value` | `any` | — | no | A label and value with Edit; Save calls onSave and closes, a thrown error keeps it open. |
| `onSave` | `(value) => void \| Promise` | — | no | A label and value with Edit; Save calls onSave and closes, a thrown error keeps it open. |
| `EditableField.validate / format / renderControl` | `function` | — | no | Message for an invalid draft, how the value reads, and a custom control instead of Input. |
| `CharacterCount.value` | `string` | — | no | Remaining characters, announced politely near the limit; reference the id from aria-describedby. |
| `max` | `number` | — | no | Remaining characters, announced politely near the limit; reference the id from aria-describedby. |
| `id` | `string` | — | no | Remaining characters, announced politely near the limit; reference the id from aria-describedby. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `validators`: `required`, `email`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `min`, `max`

## Usage

```jsx
import { FormErrorSummary, useFormValidation, validators } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Forms';
import Button from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Button';
import { EmailInput } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Input';

function ContactForm() {
  const form = useFormValidation({
    initialValues: { email: '' },
    rules: { email: [validators.required('Enter an email.'), validators.email()] }
  });
  return <form onSubmit={form.handleSubmit(saveContact)}>
    <FormErrorSummary form={form} labels={{ email: 'Email' }} />
    <EmailInput aria-label='Email' {...form.field('email')} />
    <Button type='submit'>Save contact</Button>
  </form>;
}
```

## Accessibility

Errors sit next to their control, are linked with aria-describedby and mark it aria-invalid. The summary is an alert that receives focus and moves focus to a field from each link. EditableField returns focus to Edit after Save, Cancel or Escape.

## Notes

- Lay out rows with FieldGroup and Field orientation=responsive; Forms adds behaviour, not layout.

- Continue working during a field save (Storybook `blocks-forms--async-field-save`)

## Related

`core-field`, `core-input`

## README

Form behaviour for blogs and applications on top of the Core Field parts: validation with accessible errors, a summary
that takes focus after a failed submit, values you edit in place and live character counts. Layout stays with
`FieldGroup` and `Field` (use `orientation='responsive'` for label-control rows); Forms adds behaviour, not wrappers.

```jsx
import { FormErrorSummary, useFormValidation, validators } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Forms';
import { FieldError, FieldGroup, FieldLabel, FieldRoot as Field } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Field';
import { EmailInput } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Input';

const form = useFormValidation({
  initialValues: { email: '' },
  rules: { email: [validators.required('Enter your email address.'), validators.email()] }
});

<form noValidate onSubmit={form.handleSubmit(subscribe)}>
  <FormErrorSummary form={form} labels={{ email: 'Email' }} />
  <Field data-invalid={form.errors.email ? true : undefined}>
    <FieldLabel htmlFor={form.id('email')}>Email</FieldLabel>
    <EmailInput {...form.field('email')} />
    <FieldError id={form.errorId('email')}>{form.errors.email}</FieldError>
  </Field>
</form>
```

### API

| Prop / export                                        | Type                                      | Contract                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `useFormValidation({ initialValues, rules, validateOn })` | hook                                  | Form state. `rules` maps a name to a validator or a list; `validateOn` is `blur` or `submit`. |
| `form.field(name, { describedBy })`                  | props                                     | `id`, `name`, `value`, `onChange`, `onBlur`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`.       |
| `form.id(name)` / `form.errorId(name)`               | string                                    | Control and error ids, also used by the summary links.                                    |
| `form.setValue` / `setValues` / `handleSubmit` / `reset` | functions                             | Update values, block invalid submits (`onValid(values)`), restore a state.                |
| `validators`                                         | required, email, minLength, maxLength, pattern, min, max | Message-returning checks; custom rules receive `(value, values)`.                |
| `FormErrorSummary`                                   | `form`, `labels`, `title`                 | After a failed submit, lists each error, takes focus and links to the control.            |
| `EditableField`                                      | `label`, `value`, `onSave`, `validate`, `format`, `renderControl` | Value with Edit; Enter saves, Escape cancels, a thrown save error keeps it open. |
| `CharacterCount`                                     | `value`, `max`, `id`                      | Remaining characters, announced politely near the limit.                                  |

### Accessibility

- Errors sit beside their control, are referenced by `aria-describedby` and set `aria-invalid`.
- Format validators pass on empty values, so optional fields stay optional; add `validators.required` when needed.
- `FormErrorSummary` is an alert that receives focus; each link moves focus to its field, or to the first control in a
  group such as a rating or a checkbox list.
- `EditableField` returns focus to its Edit button after Save, Cancel or Escape.

# Heroes

> Blocks/Marketing/Heroes · blocks · `@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Hero`

Responsive hero sections for product, editorial, and marketing pages. One shared layout owns the heading, introduction, action group, and media; compose the slots with existing Gaudi components.

## Import

```js
import Heroes from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Hero';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks';
```

Exports: `Hero`, `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Optional label, badge, or mark above the heading. It stays outside the heading so the section name is only the title. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | — | no | The primary heading. Keep it concise and specific. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Supporting paragraph, rendered with Gaudi typography. |
| `layout` | `centered \| split \| editorial \| background` | `centered` | no | Centered stack, side-by-side image, editorial heading and introduction, or background image with an opaque readable content panel. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Primary and secondary actions; use Button and Link. Long labels wrap. |
| `media` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Prepared image, video, or product preview. Background layout is intended for decorative imagery. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Optional supporting content below the actions. |
| `headingAs` | `h1 \| h2 \| h3` | `h1` | no | Choose the heading level for its place in the page. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `layout`: `centered`, `split`, `editorial`, `background`
- `headingAs`: `h1`, `h2`, `h3`

## Usage

```jsx
import { Hero } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Hero';
import Button from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Button';

<Hero title='A good place to start.' description='Your content. Shared foundations.' actions={<Button href='/start'>Get started</Button>} />
```

## Accessibility

The section is labelled by its heading. Reading order is eyebrow, heading, description, actions, supporting content, then media. Images need meaningful alternative text, or empty alt text when decorative. Background imagery must be decorative and non-interactive.

## Notes

- The hero responds to its container, stacking split and editorial layouts below 48rem.
- Supply prepared content and real destinations. Navigation, forms, claims, and product behavior belong to the host.
- Animated examples reuse Gaudi backgrounds (Aurora, Grainient, Dark Veil, Floating Lines, Liquid Ether) and include a pause control; reduced motion stops them.
- The examples are original Gaudi compositions using local artwork; no Tailwind Plus source is included.

## Examples

- Aurora (Storybook `blocks-marketing-heroes--playground`)
- Mesh gradient (Storybook `blocks-marketing-heroes--mesh-gradient`)
- Live surface (Storybook `blocks-marketing-heroes--live-surface`)
- Journal topics (Storybook `blocks-marketing-heroes--journal-topics`)
- Split image (Storybook `blocks-marketing-heroes--split-image`)
- Product preview (Storybook `blocks-marketing-heroes--product-preview`)
- Editorial (Storybook `blocks-marketing-heroes--editorial`)

## Related

`blocks-navigation`, `animations-backgrounds-aurora`, `animations-backgrounds-grainient`, `core-button`, `core-link`

## README

A responsive marketing introduction, showcased in **Blocks → Marketing → Heroes**.

```jsx
import { Hero } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Hero';
import Button from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Button';

<Hero
  layout='split'
  title='A good place to start.'
  description='Your content. Shared foundations.'
  actions={<Button href='/start'>Get started</Button>}
  media={<img src='/cover.jpg' alt='Your image description' />}
/>
```

`layout` supports `centered`, `split`, `editorial`, and `background`. Split and editorial layouts stack below a 48rem container width. With no media, split keeps a single content column. Slots accept existing Gaudi components; the block does not own navigation, forms, destinations, or product data. `eyebrow` places a short label, Badge, or mark above the heading without changing the section name. `children` adds supporting content below the actions.

The section labels itself with its heading. Use `headingAs` to fit the document hierarchy. Supply decorative, non-interactive media for `background`; its opaque content panel keeps text readable in both themes. Images require descriptive alt text unless decorative. Button and Link provide the action semantics, focus, and keyboard behavior.

For an animated hero, place the Hero inside a Gaudi background such as `Borealis` or `Grainient`, give the Hero `className='bg-transparent'`, and offer a pause control. Use the dark theme scope for dark effects so text keeps its contrast.
