## Accessibility

The current chat has aria-current; row menus are named after each chat, and rename and delete use labelled dialogs. In the compact composition, History and New chat remain in the header while history hides the composer; Back to conversation or session selection resumes the transcript. The page navigation Sheet closes after selection and returns focus to its opener.

## Examples

- Session history in a full chat panel (Storybook `chat-chatsessionlist--playground`)

## Related

`core-sheet`

## README

Past conversations grouped by day or week, with title search, current-session selection, a new-chat action, and rename and delete dialogs. Compose the list inside a chat so choosing a session opens its transcript and draft.

### Usage

```jsx
import { ChatShell } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Chat';
import { ChatSessionList, ChatMessageParts, ChatPromptComposer } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<ChatShell
  title={activeSession.title}
  navigation={
    <ChatSessionList
      sessions={sessions}
      activeId={activeSession.id}
      onSelect={openChat}
      onNew={startChat}
      onRename={renameChat}
      onDelete={deleteChat}
    />
  }
  composer={<ChatPromptComposer value={activeSession.draft} onValueChange={saveDraft} onSubmit={send} />}
>
  <div role='region' aria-label='Conversation' tabIndex={0} className='min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto p-4'>
    {activeSession.turns.map((turn) => <ChatMessageParts key={turn.id} parts={turn.parts} />)}
  </div>
</ChatShell>
```

The host owns `sessions`, the active ID, and each session's transcript and draft. Selection changes the active ID; rename updates that session's title; deletion removes it and chooses a remaining session or starts a new one if necessary. Keep drafts keyed by session ID so switching chats does not carry text into another conversation. Search filters the supplied titles locally and does not change the active session.

For a compact assistant panel, keep the shell header visible and use its **History** action to replace the conversation with this list. Hide the composer while browsing history; **Back to conversation** or selecting a session restores it. Keep **New chat** in the header. This is a `ChatShell` composition, with no additional public wrapper. The full-page layout uses the shell's `navigation` slot; on narrow screens the existing navigation Sheet contains the list.

### API

| Prop / part | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `sessions` | `{ id, title, preview?, updated?, group?, live? }`. |
| `activeId` / `onSelect(id)` | Host-controlled current chat (`aria-current`) and selection callback. |
| `onNew()` / `onRename(id, title)` / `onDelete(id)` | Host callbacks for new chat, a confirmed rename, and confirmed deletion. Only supplied actions appear. |
| `searchable=true` / `labels` | Local title search and interface copy overrides. |

### Accessibility

Rows are buttons with the current one marked; each row menu is named after the chat, and rename and delete go through dialogs with clear titles. The full-page shell closes its narrow-screen navigation Sheet after session selection and returns focus to the opener. The compact composition keeps History and New chat available in the header.

### Examples

- [ChatSessionList playground](?path=/story/chat-chatsessionlist--playground): the list inside a compact conversation panel, with search, selection, rename, deletion, and separate session drafts.
- [Blocks/Chat · Session panel](?path=/story/blocks-chat--session-panel): the compact History / Back to conversation flow and header New chat action.
- [Blocks/Chat · Session page](?path=/story/blocks-chat--session-page): full-page navigation beside the conversation, using the existing Sheet on narrow screens.

### Accessibility

Each citation is a button named "Source 1: title" (", and 2 more" when grouped). The card opens on hover for a mouse without taking focus, and on click, tap, Enter or Space with focus inside; Escape closes it. The carousel pages with the arrow keys, its buttons or a swipe, and announces "2 of 3". Links leave the page with clear names.

# ChatTool

> Chat/ChatTool · chat · `@gaudi/design-system/chat/ChatTool`

One tool call with status, input and output as data, nested calls and a retry, plus ChatMessageToolApproval for calls that wait on the person.

## Import

```js
import ChatTool from '@gaudi/design-system/chat/ChatTool';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';
```

Exports: `ChatMessageData`, `ChatMessageTool`, `ChatMessageToolApproval`, `approvalStates`, `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | — | no | Tool name. |
| `status` | `pending \| running \| done \| failed \| cancelled \| awaiting \| denied` | `pending` | no | Status badge; failed opens with the error. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Initial disclosure; a failed call opens on its own. |
| `input` | `unknown` | — | no | Shown with ChatMessageData. |
| `output` | `unknown` | — | no | Shown with ChatMessageData. |
| `error` | `string` | — | no | Shown with ChatMessageData. |
| `onRetry` | `function` | — | no | Retry a failed call. |
| `ChatMessageData.value` | `unknown` | — | no | A list or table with a JSON view. |
| `label` | `string` | — | no | A list or table with a JSON view. |
| `ChatMessageToolApproval.state / defaultState / onStateChange` | `requested \| approved \| denied \| executed` | `requested` | no | Approval lifecycle; control it to move to executed with the result as children. |
| `ChatMessageToolApproval.onApprove` | `({ always }) => void` | — | no | The person’s decision; always is the “always allow” choice. |
| `onDeny` | `() => void` | — | no | The person’s decision; always is the “always allow” choice. |
| `ChatMessageToolApproval.allowAlways` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Offer “always allow”, explain a denial, and replace the copy. |
| `reason` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Offer “always allow”, explain a denial, and replace the copy. |
| `labels` | `object` | `English copy` | no | Offer “always allow”, explain a denial, and replace the copy. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `status`: `pending`, `running`, `done`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `awaiting`, `denied`

## Usage

```jsx
import { ChatMessageTool, ChatMessageToolApproval } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<>
<ChatMessageTool name='schedule_newsletter' status={status} input={input} output={output} error={error} onRetry={retry} />

<ChatMessageToolApproval
  name='publish_post'
  description='Publish the draft to the blog'
  input={{ slug: 'local-first-drafts' }}
  allowAlways
  onApprove={({ always }) => approve(always)}
  onDeny={deny}
/>
</>
```

## Accessibility

The header is a disclosure naming the tool and status; errors are alerts. An approval is a labelled group; after a decision focus moves to its outcome, which is a status message.

## Notes

- See Agent run on Chat/ChatReasoning for an approval inside a full agent run, with approve and deny.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `chat-chattool--playground`)
- Structured data with a JSON view (Storybook `chat-chattool--structured-data`)
- A running call fails (Storybook `chat-chattool--failure-recovery`)
- A delayed approval keeps reader focus (Storybook `chat-chattool--controlled-approval`)

Curated patterns:

- Running tools — registry item `@gaudi/chat-tool-running-tools` (uses `ChatAgentMark`, `ChatMessage`, `ChatMessageAvatar`, `ChatMessageContent`, `ChatMessageHeader`, `ChatMessageParts`)

## Related

`blocks-chat`, `chat-chatreasoning`

## README

One tool call the assistant made: its name and status, the input and output as readable data with a JSON view, nested calls, and an error with a retry. `ChatMessageToolApproval` is the call that waits for the person: what the tool wants to do, Approve or Deny (optionally "always allow"), then approved, denied or executed.

### Usage

```jsx
import { ChatMessageTool, ChatMessageToolApproval } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<ChatMessageTool name='schedule_newsletter' status={status} input={input} output={output} error={error} onRetry={retry}>
  {nestedCalls}
</ChatMessageTool>

<ChatMessageToolApproval
  name='publish_post'
  description='Publish the draft to the blog and email subscribers'
  input={{ slug: 'local-first-drafts', notify: 4180 }}
  allowAlways
  state={state}
  onStateChange={setState}
  onApprove={({ always }) => run({ always })}
  onDeny={cancel}
>
  {state === 'executed' ? <ChatMessageData value={result} /> : null}
</ChatMessageToolApproval>
```

### API

| Prop / part | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | pending, running, done, failed or cancelled; `awaiting` and `denied` for approvals. |
| `input` / `output` / `error` | Shown with ChatMessageData; a failed call opens on its own with the error. |
| `onRetry` | Adds a retry to a failed call. |
| `ChatMessageData` | `value` read as a list or table, with a JSON view; `label` names it. Keys retain their supplied casing and numbers are not localized implicitly. Pass prepared strings when formatting is needed. |
| `ChatMessageToolApproval.state` | `requested`, `approved`, `denied` or `executed`; uncontrolled it follows the person's choice (`defaultState`, `onStateChange`). |
| `ChatMessageToolApproval.onApprove` / `onDeny` | The decision; `onApprove` receives `{ always }`. |
| `ChatMessageToolApproval.allowAlways` / `reason` / `labels` | Offer "always allow", explain a denial, and replace any copy. Children are the result once `executed`. |

### Accessibility

The tool header is a disclosure button naming the tool and its status. Errors are alerts. The JSON view is a labelled toggle. An approval is a group named by its question; Approve and Deny are plain buttons, and after a decision focus moves to the outcome, which is also a status message.

```jsx
<ChatMicSelector value={deviceId} onValueChange={setDeviceId} />
<ChatSpeechInput deviceId={deviceId} onInterim={setPreview} onTranscript={append} onAudio={transcribe} />
<ChatVoiceSelector voices={voices} groupBy='provider' value={voice} onValueChange={setVoice} onPreview={speakSample} />
<ChatAudioPlayer src={reply.audioUrl} title='Reply' peaks={reply.peaks} download='reply.mp3' />
</>
```

## Accessibility

ChatSpeechInput is a pressed-state button stopped by Escape that announces listening and transcribing politely and explains when it is disabled; ChatMicSelector names its select and explains a blocked permission; ChatVoiceSelector is a fieldset of native radios with named sample buttons; the ChatAudioPlayer scrubber is a slider that reads time.

## Examples

- Voice mode (Storybook `chat-voice--voice-mode`)
- Cancel capture and pending transcription (Storybook `chat-voice--capture-cancellation`)

## Related

`chat-chatpersona`

## README

Building blocks for talking to an assistant: dictate a prompt, pick the microphone, pick the voice that answers and play the spoken reply. They pair with ChatPersona for a full voice mode.

- `ChatSpeechInput`: a mic button for the composer’s mic slot, with idle, listening and processing states and a ring that follows the input level.
- `ChatMicSelector`: the input device picker, with permission, refresh and a test level meter.
- `ChatVoiceSelector`: a data-driven list of TTS voices with tags and sample playback.
- `ChatAudioPlayer`: a compact player for voice messages and TTS replies.
- Helpers: `useAudioLevel(stream)`, `useAudioInputs()`, `voiceSupport()`, `getSpeechRecognition()`, `computePeaks()`, `formatAudioTime()`.

### Usage

```jsx
import { ChatAudioPlayer, ChatMicSelector, ChatPromptComposer, ChatSpeechInput, ChatVoiceSelector } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<ChatMicSelector value={deviceId} onValueChange={setDeviceId} />
<ChatSpeechInput
  deviceId={deviceId}
  onInterim={setDraftPreview}
  onTranscript={(text) => setDraft((draft) => `${draft} ${text}`.trim())}
  onAudio={(blob) => transcribe(blob)} // Firefox and Safari: return the transcript
/>
<ChatVoiceSelector voices={voices} groupBy='provider' value={voice} onValueChange={setVoice} onPreview={speakSample} />
<ChatAudioPlayer src={reply.audioUrl} title='Reply' peaks={reply.peaks} download='reply.mp3' />
```

The host supplies its available `voices`. The former `exampleVoices` package export now lives only in `stories/fixtures/exampleVoices.js` for the Voice mode demo.

### API

| Component | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `ChatSpeechInput` | `onTranscript(text, { final })`, `onInterim(text)`, `onAudio(blob) => transcript?`, `onStateChange`, `onError(kind)`, `onLevel(level)`; `mode` auto, speech or recorder; `lang`, `deviceId`, `showLevel`, `labels`, plus Button `size` / `variant`. |
| `ChatMicSelector` | `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange(deviceId, device)`, `meter` (a Test button and level meter), `autoRequest`, `labels`. |
| `ChatVoiceSelector` | `voices` (`{ id, name, provider?, gender?, accent?, age?, style?, description?, previewUrl? }`), `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange(id, voice)`, `onPreview(voice, { signal })`, `groupBy`, `searchable`, `labels`. |
| `ChatAudioPlayer` | `src`, `title`, `peaks` (0..1), `duration`, `speeds`, `download` (true or a file name), `autoPlay`, `onPlay` / `onPause` / `onEnded`, `labels`. |
| `useAudioLevel(stream, { onLevel })` | `{ levelRef, waveformRef }` for ChatPersona, updated every frame without re-rendering. |
| `useAudioInputs({ autoRequest })` | `{ devices, permission, error, refresh, request }`. |

All browser APIs (SpeechRecognition, MediaRecorder, getUserMedia, enumerateDevices, AudioContext, Audio) are read lazily and guarded, so every part renders on the server; ChatSpeechInput stays disabled until the browser reports what it supports. Disabling it or changing `mode`, `deviceId` or `lang` cancels the current capture and ignores pending transcription results. Unmounting releases the microphone.

### Accessibility

ChatSpeechInput is a real button with `aria-pressed` while listening; Escape stops it; a polite status announces listening, transcribing and stopped, and a disabled button explains why through `aria-describedby`. ChatMicSelector names its select, explains a blocked permission with a retry, and only opens the microphone for an explicit test. ChatVoiceSelector is a fieldset of Core RadioGroup controls (arrow keys move the choice) with separate, named sample buttons. ChatAudioPlayer’s scrubber is a slider that reads time (“0:12 of 0:45”) and moves with the arrow keys, Page Up / Page Down, Home and End. Motion (the level ring, the meter, spinners) is not the only signal, and calms down for reduced motion.


## Accessibility

Core Tabs and Tree own keyboard navigation. Agent actions move focus to the Files tab. Control view, agentId and explorer selection when composing desktop and Sheet copies in ChatShell.

## Notes

- The host owns preview rendering, permissions and file IO. ChatShell owns responsive layout and overlays.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `chat-chatworkspace--playground`)
- Agent roster and activity (Storybook `chat-chatworkspace--agent-roster`)
- Empty (Storybook `chat-chatworkspace--empty`)
- Controlled workspace navigation (Storybook `chat-chatworkspace--controlled-navigation`)

## Related

`core-tabs`, `core-tree`, `core-sheet`, `chat-chatactivityindicator`

## README

A context panel for the agents and files around a conversation. An agent's **View files** action opens its folder in `ChatFileExplorer`; **All files** restores the complete hierarchy. `ChatShell` owns responsive placement and mobile sheets.

```jsx
import { ChatWorkspace } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<ChatWorkspace
  agents={[{ id: 'research', name: 'Research', state: 'thinking', description: 'Checking sources', fileRootId: 'research-files' }]}
  fileExplorerProps={{ items, defaultExpanded: ['shared'], selectedId, onSelect, onPreview, onRefresh }}
/>
```

### API

| Prop | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `agents` | `{ id, name, description?, state?, labels?, fileRootId? }[]`. Stable opaque IDs determine each `ChatAgentMark`. `state` and `labels` use `ChatActivityIndicator`. |
| `fileExplorerProps` | The existing `ChatFileExplorer` props, including `items`, selection, search, actions and recovery states. No second file schema. |
| `view / defaultView / onViewChange` | Controlled or local `files` / `agents` tab. Defaults to `files`. |
| `agentId / defaultAgentId / onAgentChange` | Controlled or local agent scope; `null` means all files. The agent must point to an existing folder, including an empty one. |
| `title / description / actions` | Panel heading, optional supporting text and header actions. |
| `labels` | Override `files`, `agents`, `allFiles`, `viewFiles`, `noAgents`, `noAgentsDescription`, `noAgentFiles`. |
| `className` | Layout integration. The panel has no fixed height or overlay behavior. |

Scope changes reset the explorer's local search and expansion. A missing agent or removed folder falls back to the full tree. The host supplies preview content and file IO through the explorer callbacks. Keep agent permissions, task orchestration and fetching in the application.

When using `ChatShell.details`, control `view`, `agentId` and `fileExplorerProps.selectedId` from the host so the desktop panel and mobile sheet share the current selection. See **Blocks / Chat / Workspace context: agents, files and preview** for a complete example.

### Accessibility

Core Tabs provides tab keyboard navigation. Agent identity and activity have text equivalents. Choosing an agent's files or returning to all files focuses the Files tab; Core Tree owns the explorer's keyboard interaction. Empty agent/file states are explicit.

- Response time by route — registry item `@gaudi/box-plot-chart-response-times` (uses `BoxPlotChart`, `ToggleGroupItem`, `ToggleGroupRoot`)

## Related

`core-field`

## README

Distributions side by side: median, quartiles, whiskers at 1.5 × IQR and outliers, from raw samples or precomputed summaries.

[Open the docs](http://localhost:6007/?path=/docs/charts-boxplotchart--docs) for the Playground and detailed examples, each with its complete JSX.

### Usage

```jsx
import { BoxPlotChart } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts';

<BoxPlotChart ariaLabel='Load time by template' data={[{ label: 'Home', values: [410, 460, 480, 520, 1420] }]} unit='ms' />
```

Import from `@gaudi/design-system/charts` or `@gaudi/design-system/charts/BoxPlotChart`. Charts are not exported from the root entry, so pages without a chart never load Recharts. In an article, render the same chart through MDX/Chart.

### API

| Prop | Type | Default | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | Array<{ label, values } \| { label, min, q1, median, q3, max, outliers? }> | [] | Groups. |
| `labelKey / valuesKey` | string | label / values | Field names. |
| `unit` | string | — | Suffix on axis ticks. |
| `color` | string | chart-1 | Box colour. |
| `title / description` | ReactNode | — | Figure caption above the plot. |
| `ariaLabel` | string | title or Chart | Accessible name of the plot, the single keyboard stop. |
| `height` | number | type-specific | Plot height in pixels. |
| `state` | loading \| error \| empty \| invalid | from data | Force a state; empty and invalid are otherwise detected from the data. |
| `labels` | Partial<DEFAULT_CHART_LABELS> | English copy | Copy for states, the keyboard hint, the data table and its toggle. |
| `locale / formatValue` | string / Intl.NumberFormatOptions \| (value) => string | runtime / number | Number format for axes, tooltips, the readout and the table. |
| `showData` | hidden \| toggle \| visible | hidden | Data table visibility; hidden keeps it available to assistive technology. |
| `onActivate / onActiveChange` | (point, index) => void / (index \| null) => void | — | Click, Enter or Space on a point; the active point changed. |
| `toolbar / framed` | ReactNode / boolean | — / true | Controls beside the caption; the figure border and padding. |
| `className` | string | — | Additional classes on the outer element. |

### Accessibility

The plot is one tab stop named by ariaLabel. The arrow keys walk the points, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter or Space activates and Escape clears; the active point is drawn and read out politely. Every value is mirrored in a data table, and the SVG is hidden from assistive technology.

Colours come from the chart palette tokens (`--ds-color-chart-1` … `-8`, the sequential, diverging and heatmap ramps and the chart neutrals), with light and dark values checked by the token tests.

See [source notices](../../../../README.md#third-party-notices).

# ChartFrame

> Charts/ChartFrame · charts · `@gaudi/design-system/charts/ChartFrame`

The frame every chart renders in: a captioned figure with one keyboard stop and a readout, loading, empty, invalid and error states, locale-aware numbers and a data table built from points. Use it around a custom visual, with the Recharts composition parts and Gaudi primitives.

## Import

```js
import ChartFrame from '@gaudi/design-system/charts/ChartFrame';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts';
```

Exports: `ChartActiveMarker`, `ChartAnnotations`, `ChartAreaGradient`, `ChartContainer`, `ChartDataTable`, `ChartFrame`, `ChartGrid`, `ChartLegend`, `ChartLegendContent`, `ChartReferenceLabel`, `ChartReferenceLine`, `ChartStatePanel`, `ChartStyle`, `ChartTooltip`, `ChartTooltipContent`, `ChartTooltipRows`, `ChartXAxis`, `ChartYAxis`, `DEFAULT_CHART_LABELS`, `binValues`, `boxStats`, `chartAxisTick`, `chartColors`, `chartScales`, `chartTones`, `createChartFormatter`, `createRowsTooltip`, `dataStatus`, `default`, `extent`, `getChartColor`, `groupSmallSlices`, `isChartNumber`, `niceTicks`, `scaleLinear`, `useChartFrame`, `useRechartsActive`

## Props

| `status` | `ready \| loading \| empty \| invalid \| error` | `ready` | no | The frame state; charts derive it from their data. |
| `columns` | `number` | — | no | Row length for Up and Down on grid-shaped visuals. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Content composed from the exported parts. |

| `ChartContainer / ChartGrid / ChartXAxis / ChartYAxis / ChartReferenceLine / ChartAnnotations / createRowsTooltip` | `parts` | — | no | Style bespoke Recharts charts with chart tokens. |
| `title / description` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Figure caption above the plot. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `title or Chart` | no | Accessible name of the plot, the single keyboard stop. |

| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `status`: `ready`, `loading`, `empty`, `invalid`, `error`
- `state`: `loading`, `error`, `empty`, `invalid`
- `showData`: `hidden`, `toggle`, `visible`

## Usage

```jsx
import { ChartFrame, useChartFrame } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts';

<ChartFrame title='Writing goals' ariaLabel='Progress towards writing goals' points={points} showData='toggle'>
  <GoalBars />
</ChartFrame>
```

# DonutChart

> Charts/DonutChart · charts · `@gaudi/design-system/charts/DonutChart`

Parts of a whole as a donut with a centre summary, or a pie (PieChart); slices are selectable and small ones fold into Other.

## Import

```js
import DonutChart from '@gaudi/design-system/charts/DonutChart';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts';
```

```jsx
import { FunnelChart } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts';

<FunnelChart ariaLabel='Trial to paid funnel' data={steps} align='center' />
```

## Accessibility

The plot is one tab stop named by ariaLabel. The arrow keys walk the points, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter or Space activates and Escape clears; the active point is drawn and read out politely. Every value is mirrored in a data table, and the SVG is hidden from assistive technology.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `charts-funnelchart--playground`)
- Centred funnel with a colour per step (Storybook `charts-funnelchart--centred`)
- Custom copy and locale (Storybook `charts-funnelchart--localised`)

Curated patterns:

- Newsletter signups — registry item `@gaudi/funnel-chart-newsletter-signups` (uses `FunnelChart`, `ToggleGroupItem`, `ToggleGroupRoot`)

| `series` | Array<{ key, label?, dashed? }> | from yKey | Value fields drawn as series, in order; a dashed series reads as a projection or target. |
| `curve` | monotone \| linear \| step | monotone | Line interpolation. |
| `showDots` | boolean | true | Point markers. |
| `references / annotations` | Array<{ x?, y?, label, tone? }> | — | Labelled guide lines and point notes. |
| `showGrid / showLegend / showTooltip` | boolean | true / false / true | Presentation. |
| `colors` | string[] | categorical palette | Override the series colours with chart tokens. |
| `title / description` | ReactNode | — | Figure caption above the plot. |
| `ariaLabel` | string | title or Chart | Accessible name of the plot, the single keyboard stop. |
| `height` | number | type-specific | Plot height in pixels. |
| `state` | loading \| error \| empty \| invalid | from data | Force a state; empty and invalid are otherwise detected from the data. |
| `labels` | Partial<DEFAULT_CHART_LABELS> | English copy | Copy for states, the keyboard hint, the data table and its toggle. |
| `locale / formatValue` | string / Intl.NumberFormatOptions \| (value) => string | runtime / number | Number format for axes, tooltips, the readout and the table. |
| `showData` | hidden \| toggle \| visible | hidden | Data table visibility; hidden keeps it available to assistive technology. |
| `onActivate / onActiveChange` | (point, index) => void / (index \| null) => void | — | Click, Enter or Space on a point; the active point changed. |
| `toolbar / framed` | ReactNode / boolean | — / true | Controls beside the caption; the figure border and padding. |
| `className` | string | — | Additional classes on the outer element. |

### Accessibility

The plot is one tab stop named by ariaLabel. The arrow keys walk the points, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter or Space activates and Escape clears; the active point is drawn and read out politely. Every value is mirrored in a data table, and the SVG is hidden from assistive technology.

Colours come from the chart palette tokens (`--ds-color-chart-1` … `-8`, the sequential, diverging and heatmap ramps and the chart neutrals), with light and dark values checked by the token tests.

See [source notices](../../../../README.md#third-party-notices).

# OrgChart

> Charts/OrgChart · charts · `@gaudi/design-system/charts/OrgChart`

A connected organization hierarchy with person cards, expandable reporting lines, and contained scrolling.

## Import

```js
import { OrgChart } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts/OrgChart';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts';
```

Exports: `OrgChart`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `OrgNode \| null` | — | no | Root { id, name, role?, department?, avatar?, children? }. IDs must be unique; children form an acyclic tree. |
| `label` | `string` | `Organization chart` | no | Accessible name of the scrolling region. |
| `collapsedIds / defaultCollapsedIds / onCollapsedIdsChange` | `string[] / function` | `[]` | no | Controlled or initial collapsed branches; callback receives the next IDs. |
| `onNodeClick` | `(node) => void` | — | no | Makes person cards keyboard-accessible buttons. The host owns details or selection. |
| `renderNode` | `(node) => ReactNode` | `Person avatar and text` | no | Custom card content. Keep it non-interactive when onNodeClick wraps it in a button. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Disables person and branch actions; scrolling remains available. |
| `labels` | `object` | `English labels` | no | Override empty and expand(node), collapse(node), reports(count) text. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { OrgChart } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts/OrgChart';

const team = { id: 'lead', name: 'Bram Ellery', role: 'Engineering Lead', children: [{ id: 'dev', name: 'Sam Rivera', role: 'Engineer' }] };
<OrgChart label='Engineering organization' data={team} />
```

## Accessibility

Nested lists convey reporting relationships. Branch buttons expose expanded state, retain focus when toggled, and work with Enter or Space. The labelled scroll region is keyboard focusable. Avatars are decorative because names are visible.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `charts-orgchart--playground`)
- Collapsed departments (Storybook `charts-orgchart--department-overview`)
- Empty (Storybook `charts-orgchart--empty`)

## README

A connected reporting hierarchy with collapsible branches. Import from `@gaudi/design-system/charts/OrgChart` or `@gaudi/design-system/charts` and load Gaudi's global stylesheet.

```jsx
import { OrgChart } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts/OrgChart';

const team = {
  id: 'lead', name: 'Bram Ellery', role: 'Engineering Lead',
  children: [{ id: 'dev', name: 'Sam Rivera', role: 'Engineer' }]
};

<OrgChart label='Engineering organization' data={team} />
```

Nodes accept `id`, `name`, `role`, `department`, `avatar`, and `children`. Supply a finite, acyclic tree with unique stable IDs. A null root displays the empty state. Use `defaultCollapsedIds` for the initial overview or `collapsedIds` with `onCollapsedIdsChange` for host-owned expansion. `onNodeClick(node)` makes person cards buttons; the application supplies the detail view. `renderNode(node)` customizes their contents; avoid interactive children when the card is itself a button. `disabled` disables both card and branch actions.

Nested lists preserve reporting relationships for assistive technology. Expand/collapse buttons retain focus and expose `aria-expanded`. The named region contains horizontal scrolling on small screens and is keyboard focusable. Person names remain visible beside decorative avatars. Override `labels.empty`, `labels.expand(node)`, `labels.collapse(node)` and `labels.reports(count)` to localize it.

Use Tree for a compact navigable outline; use Flow for an editable graph with pan, zoom, and arbitrary connections. OrgChart deliberately presents a reporting tree without a canvas dependency.

| `toolbar` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Controls beside the caption; the figure border and padding. |
| `framed` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Controls beside the caption; the figure border and padding. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `showData`: `hidden`, `toggle`, `visible`

## Usage

```jsx
import { SankeyChart } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts';

<SankeyChart ariaLabel='Support tickets from channel to outcome' links={[{ source: 'Email', target: 'Billing', value: 420 }, { source: 'Billing', target: 'Solved', value: 390 }]} />
```

## Accessibility

The plot is one tab stop named by ariaLabel. The arrow keys walk the points, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter or Space activates and Escape clears; the active point is drawn and read out politely. Every value is mirrored in a data table, and the SVG is hidden from assistive technology.

# TournamentBracket

> Charts/TournamentBracket · charts · `@gaudi/design-system/charts/TournamentBracket`

A knockout bracket with connected match cards, round paging, scores, penalties, and explicit winners.

## Import

```js
import { TournamentBracket } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts/TournamentBracket';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts';
```

Exports: `TournamentBracket`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rounds` | `Round[]` | `[]` | no | Ordered { id, name, matches } rounds, each with half the matches of the previous one, ending in a single final. IDs are unique. |
| `label` | `string` | `Tournament bracket` | no | Accessible name of the bracket region. |
| `round / defaultRound / onRoundChange` | `number / function` | `0` | no | Controlled or initial leftmost round index. Clamped for the current container width. |
| `onMatchClick` | `(match) => void` | — | no | Makes match cards buttons for host-owned details. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Disables round navigation and match actions. |
| `labels` | `object` | `English labels` | no | Localize navigation, match statuses, TBD, winner, penalties, versus, empty and invalid-state text. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { TournamentBracket } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts/TournamentBracket';

const rounds = [{ id: 'final', name: 'Final', matches: [{ id: 'f1', status: 'completed', home: { name: 'North', score: 2 }, away: { name: 'South', score: 1 }, winner: 'home' }] }];
<TournamentBracket rounds={rounds} />
```

## Accessibility

Labelled match groups expose round and participant names. Native buttons support keyboard navigation; current rounds are announced politely. Winners have a text alternative as well as an icon and weight. Motion respects reduced-motion preferences. One, two or three rounds fit the container without page overflow.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `charts-tournamentbracket--playground`)
- Final with a winner (Storybook `charts-tournamentbracket--final-result`)
- Empty (Storybook `charts-tournamentbracket--empty`)

## README

A knockout bracket with connected match cards and responsive round paging. Import from `@gaudi/design-system/charts/TournamentBracket` or `@gaudi/design-system/charts`, with Gaudi's global stylesheet.

```jsx
import { TournamentBracket } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts/TournamentBracket';

const rounds = [{
  id: 'final', name: 'Final', matches: [{
    id: 'f1', label: 'Oct 25 · 19:00', status: 'completed',
    home: { name: 'North', score: 2 }, away: { name: 'South', score: 1 }, winner: 'home'
  }]
}];
<TournamentBracket rounds={rounds} />
```

Supply ordered rounds `{ id, name, matches }`. Each round must have half as many matches as the previous one, ending with a single final. Round IDs are unique, and match IDs are unique across rounds. Empty data has an empty state; structurally invalid data displays a readable error. Represent byes and undecided participants with null sides while preserving the bracket structure.

Matches accept `id`, optional `label`, `status` (`upcoming`, `live`, `completed`), `home`, `away`, and `winner` (`home` or `away`). Each side accepts `name`, `seed`, `score`, and `penalties`. Zero scores are preserved. Winners and advancement are explicitly supplied by the application: scores never infer a result, and the component does not propagate winners.

The measured container shows one round below 560px, two below 880px, and up to three above it. Navigation shifts one round at a time and keeps the final two rounds together when space permits. `defaultRound` selects the initial leftmost round; `round` and `onRoundChange` provide controlled navigation. Out-of-range values are clamped for rendering without changing host state. `onMatchClick(match)` turns cards into keyboard-accessible buttons. `disabled` disables navigation and match actions.

Match groups name their round and participants; winners have visible icons and accessible text. Navigation announces the visible rounds. Layout motion respects reduced motion. Override `labels` to localize `previous`, `next`, `empty`, `invalid`, `invalidDescription`, `tbd`, `winner`, `completed`, `live`, `upcoming`, `penalties`, and `versus`.

The round-window interaction was inspired by [Skiper UI's knockout bracket](https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper107). This is an independent Gaudi implementation using its own primitives, hooks, tokens and CSS grid geometry; no Skiper source or remote assets are bundled.

# TreemapChart

> Charts/TreemapChart · charts · `@gaudi/design-system/charts/TreemapChart`

Nested rectangles sized by value, tinted by group or shaded on the heat ramp.

## Import

```js
import TreemapChart from '@gaudi/design-system/charts/TreemapChart';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts';
```

Exports: `TreemapChart`, `default`, `treemapLeaves`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `Array<{ name, value } \| { name, children }>` | `[]` | no | One or two levels. |
| `nameKey / valueKey` | `string` | `name / value` | no | Field names. |
| `colorBy` | `group \| value` | `group` | no | Tint by top-level group or shade by value. |
| `colors` | `string[]` | `categorical palette` | no | Override the series colours with chart tokens. |
| `title / description` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Figure caption above the plot. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `title or Chart` | no | Accessible name of the plot, the single keyboard stop. |
| `height` | `number` | `type-specific` | no | Plot height in pixels. |
| `state` | `loading \| error \| empty \| invalid` | `from data` | no | Force a state; empty and invalid are otherwise detected from the data. |
| `labels` | `Partial<DEFAULT_CHART_LABELS>` | `English copy` | no | Copy for states, the keyboard hint, the data table and its toggle. |
| `locale` | `string` | `runtime` | no | Number format for axes, tooltips, the readout and the table. |
| `formatValue` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions \| (value) => string` | `number` | no | Number format for axes, tooltips, the readout and the table. |
| `showData` | `hidden \| toggle \| visible` | `hidden` | no | Data table visibility; hidden keeps it available to assistive technology. |
| `onActivate` | `(point, index) => void` | — | no | Click, Enter or Space on a point; the active point changed. |
| `onActiveChange` | `(index \| null) => void` | — | no | Click, Enter or Space on a point; the active point changed. |
| `toolbar` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Controls beside the caption; the figure border and padding. |
| `framed` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Controls beside the caption; the figure border and padding. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `colorBy`: `group`, `value`
- `state`: `loading`, `error`, `empty`, `invalid`
- `showData`: `hidden`, `toggle`, `visible`

## Usage

```jsx
import { TreemapChart } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts';

<TreemapChart ariaLabel='Hours read by section' data={[{ name: 'Essays', children: [{ name: 'Engineering', value: 1240 }] }]} />
```

## Accessibility

The plot is one tab stop named by ariaLabel. The arrow keys walk the points, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter or Space activates and Escape clears; the active point is drawn and read out politely. Every value is mirrored in a data table, and the SVG is hidden from assistive technology.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `charts-treemapchart--playground`)
- One level shaded by value (Storybook `charts-treemapchart--flat`)
- Spend by team (Storybook `charts-treemapchart--spend`)

Curated patterns:

- Storage by folder — registry item `@gaudi/treemap-chart-storage-folders` (uses `ToggleGroupItem`, `ToggleGroupRoot`, `TreemapChart`)

## Related

`core-field`

## README

Nested rectangles sized by value, tinted by group or shaded on the heat ramp.

[Open the docs](http://localhost:6007/?path=/docs/charts-treemapchart--docs) for the Playground and detailed examples, each with its complete JSX.

### Usage

```jsx
import { TreemapChart } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts';

<TreemapChart ariaLabel='Hours read by section' data={[{ name: 'Essays', children: [{ name: 'Engineering', value: 1240 }] }]} />
```

Import from `@gaudi/design-system/charts` or `@gaudi/design-system/charts/TreemapChart`. Charts are not exported from the root entry, so pages without a chart never load Recharts. In an article, render the same chart through MDX/Chart.

### API

| Prop | Type | Default | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | Array<{ name, value } \| { name, children }> | [] | One or two levels. |
| `nameKey / valueKey` | string | name / value | Field names. |
| `colorBy` | group \| value | group | Tint by top-level group or shade by value. |
| `colors` | string[] | categorical palette | Override the series colours with chart tokens. |
| `title / description` | ReactNode | — | Figure caption above the plot. |
| `ariaLabel` | string | title or Chart | Accessible name of the plot, the single keyboard stop. |
| `height` | number | type-specific | Plot height in pixels. |
| `state` | loading \| error \| empty \| invalid | from data | Force a state; empty and invalid are otherwise detected from the data. |
| `labels` | Partial<DEFAULT_CHART_LABELS> | English copy | Copy for states, the keyboard hint, the data table and its toggle. |
| `locale / formatValue` | string / Intl.NumberFormatOptions \| (value) => string | runtime / number | Number format for axes, tooltips, the readout and the table. |
| `showData` | hidden \| toggle \| visible | hidden | Data table visibility; hidden keeps it available to assistive technology. |
| `onActivate / onActiveChange` | (point, index) => void / (index \| null) => void | — | Click, Enter or Space on a point; the active point changed. |
| `toolbar / framed` | ReactNode / boolean | — / true | Controls beside the caption; the figure border and padding. |
| `className` | string | — | Additional classes on the outer element. |

### Accessibility

The plot is one tab stop named by ariaLabel. The arrow keys walk the points, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter or Space activates and Escape clears; the active point is drawn and read out politely. Every value is mirrored in a data table, and the SVG is hidden from assistive technology.

Colours come from the chart palette tokens (`--ds-color-chart-1` … `-8`, the sequential, diverging and heatmap ramps and the chart neutrals), with light and dark values checked by the token tests.

See [source notices](../../../../README.md#third-party-notices).

# WaterfallChart

> Charts/WaterfallChart · charts · `@gaudi/design-system/charts/WaterfallChart`

How a starting value becomes an ending one through increases and decreases, with running totals and subtotals.

## Import

```js
import WaterfallChart from '@gaudi/design-system/charts/WaterfallChart';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts';
```

Exports: `WaterfallChart`, `default`, `waterfallSteps`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `Array<{ label, value? , total? }>` | `[]` | no | Steps; total: true draws the running total or its own value. |
| `labelKey / valueKey / totalKey` | `string` | `label / value / total` | no | Field names. |
| `changeLabel / totalLabel` | `string` | `Change / Total` | no | Names in tooltips and the table. |
| `title / description` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Figure caption above the plot. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `title or Chart` | no | Accessible name of the plot, the single keyboard stop. |
| `height` | `number` | `type-specific` | no | Plot height in pixels. |
| `state` | `loading \| error \| empty \| invalid` | `from data` | no | Force a state; empty and invalid are otherwise detected from the data. |
| `labels` | `Partial<DEFAULT_CHART_LABELS>` | `English copy` | no | Copy for states, the keyboard hint, the data table and its toggle. |
| `locale` | `string` | `runtime` | no | Number format for axes, tooltips, the readout and the table. |
| `formatValue` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions \| (value) => string` | `number` | no | Number format for axes, tooltips, the readout and the table. |
| `showData` | `hidden \| toggle \| visible` | `hidden` | no | Data table visibility; hidden keeps it available to assistive technology. |
| `onActivate` | `(point, index) => void` | — | no | Click, Enter or Space on a point; the active point changed. |
| `onActiveChange` | `(index \| null) => void` | — | no | Click, Enter or Space on a point; the active point changed. |
| `toolbar` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Controls beside the caption; the figure border and padding. |
| `framed` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Controls beside the caption; the figure border and padding. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Variants

- `state`: `loading`, `error`, `empty`, `invalid`
- `showData`: `hidden`, `toggle`, `visible`

## Usage

```jsx
import { WaterfallChart } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts';

<WaterfallChart ariaLabel='Change in subscribers' data={[{ label: 'September', value: 4180, total: true }, { label: 'New', value: 620 }, { label: 'Lost', value: -310 }, { label: 'October', total: true }]} />
```

## Accessibility

## Examples

- Performance budget bridge (Storybook `charts-waterfallchart--budget`)
- Subtotals inside the bridge (Storybook `charts-waterfallchart--subtotals`)

Curated patterns:

- Recurring revenue bridge — registry item `@gaudi/waterfall-chart-revenue-bridge` (uses `ToggleGroupItem`, `ToggleGroupRoot`, `WaterfallChart`)

## Related

`core-field`

# useArrowKeyNav

> Hooks/A11y/useArrowKeyNav · hooks · `@gaudi/design-system/hooks`

Moves focus between items with the arrow keys, Home and End while the group stays one Tab stop. The active item has tabIndex 0 and the rest -1. Keys typed in text fields and keys with Command, Control or Alt are left alone.

## Import

```js
import { useArrowKeyNav } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';
```

Exports: `getNextIndex`, `useArrowKeyNav`

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `itemCount` | `number` | — | no | Number of navigable items; the active index is clamped when items are removed. |
| `options.orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal' \| 'both'` | `'vertical'` | no | Which arrow keys move: Up and Down, Left and Right, or all four. |
| `options.wrap` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Loop from the last item to the first and back. |
| `options.dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl'` | `'ltr'` | no | In right-to-left layouts ArrowLeft moves forward. |
| `options.role` | `string` | `'group'` | no | Container role; aria-orientation is added for roles that support it (toolbar, listbox, menu, tablist…). |
| `options.defaultIndex` | `number` | `0` | no | Initial active item, and a callback when it changes. |
| `onActiveChange` | `(index) => void` | — | no | Initial active item, and a callback when it changes. |

## Returns

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `activeIndex` | `number` | The item that holds tabIndex 0. |
| `getItemProps(index)` | `{ tabIndex, onKeyDown, onFocus, ref }` | Spread on each item. |
| `containerProps` | `{ role, aria-orientation? }` | Spread on the container, then give it an accessible name. |
| `setActiveIndex(index, { focus })` | `function` | Move the active item from code; focuses it unless focus is false. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { useArrowKeyNav } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const { getItemProps, containerProps } = useArrowKeyNav(tools.length, { orientation: 'horizontal', role: 'toolbar', wrap: true });

<div {...containerProps} aria-label='Formatting'>
  {tools.map((tool, index) => <Button key={tool} {...getItemProps(index)}>{tool}</Button>)}
</div>
```

## Accessibility

Implements the WAI-ARIA roving tabindex pattern: one Tab stop for the group, arrows inside it. Name the container (aria-label or aria-labelledby) and give it the role the widget really is, such as toolbar.

## Notes

- Gaudi Tabs, ToggleGroup, RadioGroup and menus already handle their own arrow keys.
- `getNextIndex(current, key, options)` is exported for custom key handling.

## Examples

- Toolbar (Storybook `hooks-a11y-usearrowkeynav--toolbar`)
- Vertical section list (Storybook `hooks-a11y-usearrowkeynav--vertical-list`)

## Related

`core-tabs`, `core-togglegroup`, `core-radiogroup`

# useFocusTrap

> Hooks/A11y/useFocusTrap · hooks · `@gaudi/design-system/hooks`

While active, Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside the container. On activation it focuses the first tabbable element (or the container), and on release it returns focus to where it was. Traps nest, and portaled menus inside the trap keep their own focus.

## Import

```js
import { useFocusTrap } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';
```

Exports: `getTrapTarget`, `useFocusTrap`

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options.active` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Whether the trap is on. |
| `options.autoFocus` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Move focus into the container when it activates. |
| `options.initialFocus` | `'first' \| 'container'` | `'first'` | no | Focus the first tabbable element or the container itself (give it tabIndex={-1}). |
| `options.returnFocus` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Return focus to the previously focused element on release. |
| `options.containerRef` | `RefObject<HTMLElement>` | — | no | Use an existing ref instead of the returned one. |

## Returns

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ref` | `RefObject<HTMLElement>` | Attach to the container. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { useFocusTrap } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const trapRef = useFocusTrap({ active: open });

<div ref={trapRef} role='dialog' aria-modal='true' aria-labelledby='menu-title'>…</div>
```

## Accessibility

A trap must always have a visible, keyboard-reachable way out (a Close button and Escape). Pair it with role="dialog", aria-modal and a label, and with useScrollLock so the page behind does not scroll.

## Notes

- Gaudi Dialog, Dialog confirmation, Sheet and Drawer already trap focus; use this hook only for custom overlays.

## Examples

- Custom reply panel (Storybook `hooks-a11y-usefocustrap--inline-panel`)
- Focus the container first (Storybook `hooks-a11y-usefocustrap--container-focus`)

## Related

`core-dialog`, `core-sheet`, `hooks-usescrolllock`

---

# useLiveAnnouncer

> Hooks/A11y/useLiveAnnouncer · hooks · `@gaudi/design-system/hooks`

Announces short messages ("Saved", "3 results", "Copied") through shared visually hidden live regions. The regions exist before the first message so it is not lost, and repeating a message announces it again.

## Import

```js
import { useLiveAnnouncer } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';
```

Exports: `announce`, `useLiveAnnouncer`

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options.clearAfter` | `number` | `5000` | no | Milliseconds before an announced message is cleared from the region. |

## Returns

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `announce(message, politeness)` | `(string, 'polite' \| 'assertive') => void` | Read a message; 'polite' waits, 'assertive' interrupts. |
| `clear()` | `function` | Empty both regions. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { useLiveAnnouncer } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const { announce } = useLiveAnnouncer();

const save = async () => {
  await saveDraft();
  announce('Draft saved');
};
```

## Accessibility

Use 'polite' for almost everything. Reserve 'assertive' for errors and time-critical changes, keep messages short, and never announce every keystroke or streamed token.

## Notes

- `announce(message, politeness)` is also exported for non-React code.

## Examples

- Polite and assertive messages (Storybook `hooks-a11y-useliveannouncer--save-feedback`)
- Result count after typing settles (Storybook `hooks-a11y-useliveannouncer--result-count`)

# usePrefersReducedMotion

> Hooks/A11y/usePrefersReducedMotion · hooks · `@gaudi/design-system/hooks`

True when the operating system reduce-motion setting is on, updated live. Built on useMediaQuery.

## Import

```js
import { usePrefersReducedMotion } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';
```

Exports: `REDUCED_MOTION_QUERY`, `usePrefersReducedMotion`

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fallback` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Value during server rendering and hydration. |

## Returns

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reduced` | `boolean` | True when motion should be reduced. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { usePrefersReducedMotion } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const reduced = usePrefersReducedMotion();

window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: reduced ? 'auto' : 'smooth' });
```

## Accessibility

When set, skip autoplay, parallax, typing effects and smooth scrolling, or replace them with an instant change. global.css already shortens CSS transitions; use this hook for motion driven from JavaScript.

## Notes

- `REDUCED_MOTION_QUERY` is exported for CSS-in-JS or imperative checks.

## Examples

- Read the preference (Storybook `hooks-a11y-useprefersreducedmotion--reading`)
- Turn autoplay off (Storybook `hooks-a11y-useprefersreducedmotion--autoplay-off`)

## Related

`hooks-usemediaquery`

# useLocalStorage

> Hooks/Data/useLocalStorage · hooks · `@gaudi/design-system/hooks`

Stores a JSON value under a key. The server render and hydration use the initial value, and the stored value is read right after. Every caller with the same key stays in sync in this tab and in other tabs; blocked storage falls back to memory.

## Import

```js
import { useLocalStorage } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';
```

Exports: `localStorageStore`, `useLocalStorage`

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | — | no | Storage key; namespace it, for example reader:font-size. |
| `initialValue` | `any` | — | no | Value on the server, during hydration and when nothing is stored. |
| `options.serialize` | `(value) => string` | — | no | Custom encoding. |
| `deserialize` | `(raw) => any` | — | no | Custom encoding. |
| `options.syncTabs` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Follow writes from other tabs. |

## Returns

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[0] value` | `any` | Current value. |
| `[1] setValue` | `(value \| (current) => value) => void` | Store a new value. |
| `[2] removeValue` | `() => void` | Delete the key and fall back to initialValue. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { useLocalStorage } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const [fontSize, setFontSize, resetFontSize] = useLocalStorage('reader:font-size', 'md');
```

## Accessibility

Persisted preferences (text size, reduced motion, dismissed notices) must still have a visible control to change them back.

## Notes

- Never store secrets, tokens or personal data in localStorage.

## Examples

- Reading preference (Storybook `hooks-data-uselocalstorage--preference`)
- Callers stay in sync (Storybook `hooks-data-uselocalstorage--synced`)
- Preferences follow the active key (Storybook `hooks-data-uselocalstorage--per-project`)

# useMap

> Hooks/Data/useMap · hooks · `@gaudi/design-system/hooks`

Accepts a Map or iterable of key-value pairs. Each mutation creates a new Map, preserving caller-owned input. The initial entries are snapshotted once, including single-use iterators; reset copies that snapshot.

## Import

```js
import { useMap } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';
```

Exports: `useMap`

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `initialEntries` | `Map \| Iterable<[key, value]>` | `[]` | no | Initial contents, snapshotted at mount for reset. Later changes to this argument are ignored; use setAll to replace state. |

## Returns

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[map, actions]` | `[Map, object]` | Read-only-by-convention Map and stable actions. |
| `actions.set / remove / setAll / clear / reset` | `function` | Set one key, remove a key, replace all entries, empty the Map or restore the initial entries. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { useMap } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const [drafts, { set, remove, reset }] = useMap([['intro', 'Draft']]);
```

## Accessibility

Render stable keys and keep focus meaningful when entries are removed.

## Notes

- Do not call map.set/delete/clear directly; those mutations cannot notify React.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `hooks-data-usemap--playground`)

## Related

`core-map`

# useReadLocalStorage

> Hooks/Data/useReadLocalStorage · hooks · `@gaudi/design-system/hooks`

Reads through the same store as useLocalStorage, including same-tab notifications, native cross-tab storage events and blocked-storage fallback. It never exposes write actions.

## Import

```js
import { useReadLocalStorage } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';
```

Exports: `useReadLocalStorage`

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | — | no | Storage key to subscribe to. |
| `initialValue` | `any` | `null` | no | Server, hydration, absent-key and invalid-JSON fallback. |
| `options.deserialize` | `function` | `JSON.parse` | no | Custom reader and whether to subscribe to cross-tab changes. |
| `syncTabs` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Custom reader and whether to subscribe to cross-tab changes. |

## Returns

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `any` | Current parsed value or initialValue. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { useReadLocalStorage } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const density = useReadLocalStorage('reading-density', 'comfortable');
```

## Accessibility

Announce meaningful changes in context. Do not put sensitive data in browser storage.

## Notes

- Same-tab changes made with useLocalStorage notify readers. Direct localStorage.setItem calls in the same tab do not dispatch a storage event.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `hooks-data-usereadlocalstorage--playground`)

## Related

`hooks-uselocalstorage`

# useSelection

> Hooks/Data/useSelection · hooks · `@gaudi/design-system/hooks`

Tracks selected ids for lists, tables and bulk actions. Uncontrolled from initialSelectedIds, or controlled with selectedIds and onSelectionChange; every change produces a new Set.

## Import

```js
import { useSelection } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';
```

Exports: `selectionState`, `toggleInSet`, `useSelection`

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options.selectedIds` | `Set<id>` | — | no | Controlled selection. |
| `options.initialSelectedIds` | `Set<id>` | `new Set()` | no | Initial selection when uncontrolled. |
| `options.onSelectionChange` | `(ids: Set<id>) => void` | — | no | Called with the next selection. |

## Returns

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `selectedIds / count` | `Set<id> / number` | The selection and its size. |
| `isSelected(id)` | `boolean` | Whether an id is selected. |
| `getSelectAllState(ids)` | `true \| false \| 'indeterminate'` | State for a select-all checkbox. |
| `toggleSelection / select / deselect` | `(id) => void` | Change one id. |
| `selectAll / toggleAll / clearSelection / setSelection` | `function` | Change many ids at once. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { useSelection } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const { isSelected, toggleSelection, getSelectAllState, toggleAll, count } = useSelection();
```

## Accessibility

Give every checkbox a label naming its row, give the select-all checkbox an indeterminate state, and announce bulk results (for example with useLiveAnnouncer).

## Notes

- DataTable has its own selection; use this hook for custom lists, galleries and cards.

# useScript

> Hooks/Environment/useScript · hooks · `@gaudi/design-system/hooks`

Callers using the same resolved URL share one script. A null source or disabled hook stays idle. No URL is built in, and Storybook uses a local inert fixture. The copied example includes the public file location and contents to create in your app.

## Import

```js
import { useScript } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';
```

Exports: `useScript`

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string \| null` | — | no | Host-supplied script URL. |
| `options.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Whether this caller requests the script. |
| `options.removeOnUnmount` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Remove a hook-owned script after its final caller leaves, only if no caller requested retention. |

## Returns

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `'idle' \| 'loading' \| 'ready' \| 'error' \| 'unknown'` | Loading on server for enabled sources; idle for disabled/absent sources. Unknown means a pre-existing script has no observable load status. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { useScript } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const status = useScript('/scripts/local-preview.js', { enabled: previewOpen });
```

## Accessibility

Provide text for loading/error states and an alternative when an integration is unavailable.

## Notes

- Removing a script tag cannot undo code it already ran. Prefer retaining shared libraries.
- Pre-existing scripts are never removed. Mark known external script state with data-gaudi-script-status="ready" or wait for its load/error event.
- Failed retained scripts stay error; use a new URL or removeOnUnmount to release the failed entry before retrying.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `hooks-environment-usescript--playground`)

# useCopyToClipboard

> Hooks/Interaction/useCopyToClipboard · hooks · `@gaudi/design-system/hooks`

Writes text with the Clipboard API and falls back to a hidden textarea (restoring focus and selection) where the API is blocked. isCopied resets after the timeout. Merges two earlier implementations: copyToClipboard and copy are the same function.

## Import

```js

```

| `options.onCopy / onError` | `(text) => void` | — | no | Called after a successful or failed copy. |

## Returns

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copy(text) / copyToClipboard(text)` | `(text) => Promise<boolean>` | Copy; resolves to whether it worked. |
| `isCopied / copiedText` | `boolean / string \| null` | Feedback state. |
| `reset()` | `function` | Clear the copied state now. |

## Usage

## Accessibility

## Notes

- CodeBlock already has a copy button; use this hook for custom copy actions.

# useEventListener

> Hooks/Interaction/useEventListener · hooks · `@gaudi/design-system/hooks`

Attaches a listener to window (default), document, an element or a ref, and removes it on unmount. The latest handler always runs without re-subscribing, and refs are re-read after every commit so the listener follows conditional elements.

## Import

```js
import { useEventListener } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';
```

Exports: `useEventListener`

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eventName` | `string` | — | no | DOM event such as 'keydown', 'scroll' or 'resize'. |
| `handler` | `(event) => void` | — | no | Called for each event; may change on every render. |
| `target` | `'window' \| 'document' \| Element \| RefObject \| null` | `'window'` | no | Where to listen; null detaches. |
| `options` | `boolean \| AddEventListenerOptions` | — | no | capture, passive, once and signal. |

## Returns

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `(nothing)` | `void` | The listener lives as long as the component. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { useEventListener } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

useEventListener('resize', () => setWidth(window.innerWidth));
useEventListener('scroll', onScroll, panelRef, { passive: true });
```

## Accessibility

Keyboard listeners on window or document must not swallow keys that belong to focused controls; check event.target and event.defaultPrevented.

## Notes

- Mark scroll and touch listeners passive so they never delay scrolling.

## Examples

- Window events (Storybook `hooks-interaction-useeventlistener--window-events`)
- Document events (Storybook `hooks-interaction-useeventlistener--document-events`)
- An element through a ref (Storybook `hooks-interaction-useeventlistener--element-ref`)

# useHotkey

> Hooks/Interaction/useHotkey · hooks · `@gaudi/design-system/hooks`

Runs a callback for a combination such as 'mod+k' (Command+K on macOS, Control+K elsewhere), 'shift+?' or 'escape'. Skips plain keys while the reader types in a field, and returns aria-keyshortcuts and Kbd keys for the hint.

## Import

```js
import { useHotkey } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';
```

Exports: `isApplePlatform`, `matchHotkey`, `parseHotkey`, `toAriaKeyShortcuts`, `toKbdKeys`, `useHotkey`

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keys` | `string \| string[]` | — | no | One or more combinations: 'mod+k', 'ctrl+shift+p', '/', 'escape'. |
| `callback` | `(event, combo) => void` | — | no | Called when a combination matches. |
| `options.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | no | When and where to listen. |
| `target` | `target` | `'document'` | no | When and where to listen. |
| `event` | `'keydown' \| 'keyup'` | `'keydown'` | no | When and where to listen. |
| `options.preventDefault` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Stop the browser default for a matched shortcut. |
| `options.enableInInputs / allowRepeat` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Also fire in text fields, and on held-key repeats. |

## Returns

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaKeyShortcuts` | `string` | Value for aria-keyshortcuts, e.g. 'Meta+K Control+K'. |
| `kbdKeys` | `string` | Keys for Kbd, e.g. 'command,k' on macOS and 'ctrl,k' elsewhere. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { useHotkey } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const { ariaKeyShortcuts, kbdKeys } = useHotkey('mod+k', () => setOpen(true));

<Button aria-keyshortcuts={ariaKeyShortcuts} onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Search <Kbd keys={kbdKeys} /></Button>
```

## Accessibility

Every shortcut needs a visible control that does the same thing. Put aria-keyshortcuts on that control and show the keys with Kbd. Avoid single-key shortcuts unless they can be turned off (WCAG 2.1.4).

## Notes

- `parseHotkey`, `matchHotkey`, `toAriaKeyShortcuts` and `toKbdKeys` are exported for custom handling.

## Examples

- Platform-aware mod key (Storybook `hooks-interaction-usehotkey--command-palette`)
- Single-key shortcuts that can be turned off (Storybook `hooks-interaction-usehotkey--single-keys`)

## Related

`core-kbd`

# useMousePosition

# useScrollLock

## Returns

| Name | Type | Description |

# useInView

# useControllableState

> Hooks/State/useControllableState · hooks · `@gaudi/design-system/hooks`

The component owns the state until its host passes value; then the host accepts, refuses or replaces each change offered through onChange. The setter takes a value or an updater and skips unchanged values. DataTable uses it.

## Import

```js
import { useControllableState } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';
```

Exports: `useControllableState`

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options.value` | `any` | — | no | Controlled value; undefined means uncontrolled. |
| `options.defaultValue` | `any` | — | no | Initial value when uncontrolled. |
| `options.onChange` | `(value) => void` | — | no | Called with each change. |

## Returns

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[0] value` | `any` | The current value. |
| `[1] setValue` | `(value \| (current) => value) => void` | Offer a change. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { useControllableState } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

function Rating({ value, defaultValue = 0, onChange }) {
  const [rating, setRating] = useControllableState({ value, defaultValue, onChange });
}
```

## Accessibility

Controlled components must still reflect every change visibly and to assistive technology (checked, expanded, selected), even when the host refuses it.

## Notes

- Decide once: switching between controlled and uncontrolled during a component life is not supported.

## Examples

- Uncontrolled (Storybook `hooks-state-usecontrollablestate--uncontrolled`)
- Controlled, with the host refusing changes (Storybook `hooks-state-usecontrollablestate--controlled`)

## Related

`core-datatable`

# useCountdown

> Hooks/State/useCountdown · hooks · `@gaudi/design-system/hooks`

Composes useInterval with count state. Changing the interval restarts the timer interval; reset stops it and restores the current countStart. Counts represent ticks, not elapsed wall-clock time.

## Import

```js
import { useCountdown } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';
```

Exports: `useCountdown`

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options.countStart` | `number` | `60` | no | Starting value and terminal value. |
| `countStop` | `number` | `0` | no | Starting value and terminal value. |
| `options.intervalMs` | `number` | `1000` | no | Positive milliseconds per tick; invalid values stop the timer. |
| `options.isIncrement` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Count up toward the target instead of down. |

## Returns

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `count / isRunning` | `number / boolean` | Current count and whether the timer is advancing. |
| `start / stop / reset` | `function` | Start or resume, pause, or stop and reset. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { useCountdown } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const { count, isRunning, start, stop, reset } = useCountdown({ countStart: 30 });
```

## Accessibility

Keep pause and reset controls available. Avoid announcing every tick; announce completion separately.

## Notes

- Timers can be throttled in background tabs. Use an application deadline for time-critical expiry.
- Starting at or beyond the target does not run.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `hooks-state-usecountdown--playground`)

## Related

`hooks-useinterval`

# useDebounceCallback

> Hooks/State/useDebounceCallback · hooks · `@gaudi/design-system/hooks`

Runs the latest callback once, delay ms after the last call, with the latest arguments: autosave, search requests and resize work. Pending work is cancelled on unmount.

## Import

```js
import { useDebounceCallback } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';
```

Exports: `createDebouncer`, `useDebounceCallback`

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |

| `callback` | `(...args) => void` | — | no | The work to run. |
| `delay` | `number` | `300` | no | Milliseconds after the last call. |

## Returns

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `debounced(...args)` | `function` | Schedule the work. |
| `debounced.cancel / flush / isPending` | `function` | Drop pending work, run it now, or check for it. |

## Usage


# useThrottleCallback

> Hooks/State/useThrottleCallback · hooks · `@gaudi/design-system/hooks`

Keeps scroll, pointer and resize handlers responsive without running on every event: the first call runs at once and later calls fold into one trailing call with the latest arguments.

## Import

```js
import { useThrottleCallback } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';
```

Exports: `createThrottler`, `useThrottleCallback`

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `callback` | `(...args) => void` | — | no | The work to run. |
| `wait` | `number` | `200` | no | Minimum milliseconds between runs. |
| `options.leading / trailing` | `boolean` | `true / true` | no | Run on the first call, and once more after the window. |

## Returns

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `throttled(...args)` | `function` | Call as often as you like. |
| `throttled.cancel / flush` | `function` | Drop or run the pending trailing call. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { useThrottleCallback } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const onScroll = useThrottleCallback(() => setProgress(readProgress()), 100);
```

## Accessibility

Keep the final state accurate (trailing: true) so progress indicators and announcements end on the real value.

## Notes

- `createThrottler(callback, wait, options)` is exported for non-React code.

## Examples

- Throttle pointer moves (Storybook `hooks-state-usethrottlecallback--pointer-moves`)

# useTimeout

## Returns

## Usage

`core-input`

## README

Asymmetric, folded shards tumble through a broad stream with perspective depth and pearl reflections. RGB edge separation follows the camera position. Hold the pointer to gather the stream, then release to unfurl it.

```jsx
import { AeroShards } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/AeroShards';

<AeroShards height={500} paused={paused} />
```

- `paused` (boolean, default false): Freeze the current frame. Reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers also stop animation.
- `speed` (number, default 1): Playback multiplier from 0 to 5. Zero freezes time.
- `intensity` (number, default 1): Visibility of the shards, clamped to 0–2. Zero shows only the background color.
- `scale` (number, default 1): Spatial scale from 0.25 to 4. Larger values produce larger details.
- `colors` (string[], default Gaudi theme colors): Up to three CSS colors. Omit to follow the current Gaudi theme.
- `background` (string, default var(--ds-color-surface)): CSS color behind the effect, also used by the static fallback.
- `interactive` (boolean, default true): The pointer repels nearby shards. Press and hold to gather a rotating cloud; release to unfurl. Input stops while paused.
- `height` (number | string, default 360): Container height in pixels or a CSS length. Numeric values are clamped to 1–4096; width fills the available container.
- `children` (ReactNode, default —): Accessible foreground content layered above the decorative canvas.
- `className / style / ref` (DOM props, default —): Applied to the outer div. Standard DOM attributes and handlers are forwarded.

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Foreground children remain readable and interactive. Provide a pause control for continuous motion, and place text on a contrasting surface. Reduced motion displays a still frame; unavailable WebGL uses a static color fallback.

A bounded mesh of 1,280 independently positioned shards uses four non-coplanar triangular faces per shard. Size, depth, shape and roll vary independently. Holding gathers the same particles into individual circulating orbits; release restores their stream trajectories without resetting time. Narrow containers crop the same world span instead of concentrating the entire particle count into a phone-sized field.

The private renderer shares Gaudi’s canvas lifecycle, uses depth testing for overlapping facets, and releases its mesh, shaders, texture and depth framebuffer on unmount or context replacement. This is an original approximation of the rendered reference; alternate upstream materials, formations and presets are not included.

Visual idea inspired by [AeroShards](https://reactbits.dev/backgrounds/aero-shards) from [React Bits](https://reactbits.dev). Independently implemented for Gaudi from the rendered visual reference; no React Bits source code, shaders or assets are included.

# CRTWarp

Coarse phosphor cells form evolving plasma shapes beneath fine scanlines, analog grain, and local pointer distortion.

| `intensity` | `number` | `1` | no | Effect strength, clamped to 0–2. Zero reveals the background color. |
| `scale` | `number` | `1` | no | Spatial scale of the effect, clamped to 0.25–4. |
| `colors` | `string[]` | `Gaudi theme tokens` | no | Up to three CSS colors. Omitted colors inherit the current Gaudi palette. |

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Keep important content in children and provide a pause control for continuous animation. Reduced motion renders a static frame; unsupported WebGL retains the styled container and content.

## Notes

- The playground layers a Gaudi header, hero and working documentation links above the effect. The Demo content switch hides only this foreground; canvas size, animation phase and pause state are retained.
- The plasma signal has stepped contours and separated phosphor channels. Coarse signal cells keep their size in CSS pixels while fine scanlines and grain retain the analog texture.
- Visual idea inspired by CRT Warp from React Bits (MIT + Commons Clause). Independently implemented for Gaudi; no React Bits source, shaders or assets are included.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `animations-backgrounds-crt-warp--playground`)

## README

Cellular plasma islands split and reconnect through broad stepped phosphor contours, curved scanlines, and analog grain.

```jsx
import { CRTWarp } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/CRTWarp';

<CRTWarp height={360} speed={1} intensity={1} interactive />
```

Two displaced fields drift independently to form irregular islands that merge and separate. Several nested brightness bands preserve dark space between saturated cores; separated phosphor channels and a continuous halo soften the coarse contours. Signal cells use CSS pixels, and barrel curvature bends both the field and its fine scanlines. Grain covers the whole signal, including dark areas. Pointer motion locally bends the field when `interactive` is enabled. The supplied palette remains visible without washing every core toward white.

### Contract

- `paused=false` freezes the current frame when enabled. `speed=1` accepts 0–5; zero stops time.
- `intensity=1` accepts 0–2. `scale=1` accepts 0.25–4. Invalid numbers use safe defaults.
- `colors` optionally supplies up to three CSS colors; defaults come from the current Gaudi theme. `background` defaults to `var(--ds-color-surface)`.
- `interactive=false` enables pointer response when set. Content and controls retain their normal pointer behavior.
- `height=360` accepts pixels or a CSS length; numeric values are clamped to 1–4096. The canvas fills its container with a device pixel ratio capped at 1.5 and a drawing buffer of approximately two million pixels at most.
- `children`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and DOM attributes belong to the outer container. Children render above the canvas.

The shared renderer pauses for reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers, and releases its observers, animation frame and WebGL resources on unmount. Server output is deterministic. A static styled background remains available when WebGL fails.

### Accessibility

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Keep meaningful text and controls in semantic children. Provide a pause control for continuous motion and maintain text contrast when layering content over the effect.

### Visual reference

Inspired by the visual idea of [React Bits CRT Warp](https://reactbits.dev/backgrounds/crt-warp) (MIT + Commons Clause). This is an independent Gaudi implementation; no upstream component source, shader or asset is redistributed.
