- `speed` (number, default `1`): Animation speed multiplier, clamped to 0–5. Zero holds a static frame.
- `intensity` (number, default `1`): Effect strength, clamped to 0–2. Zero reveals the background color.
- `scale` (number, default `1`): Spatial scale of the effect, clamped to 0.25–4.
- `colors` (string[], default `Gaudi theme tokens`): The first CSS color supplies the tint; omitted colors inherit Gaudi theme tokens.
- `background` (string, default `var(--ds-color-surface)`): CSS color behind the effect and its static fallback.
- `interactive` (boolean, default `true`): Let pointer position influence the effect without capturing clicks or scrolling.
- `height` (number | string, default `360`): Container height in pixels or a CSS length. Numeric values are clamped to 1–4096; width fills the available container.
- `children` (ReactNode, default `—`): Optional semantic content layered above the decorative canvas.
- `className / style / ref / DOM props` (DOM props, default `—`): Forwarded to the outer container.

The shared renderer caps drawing at 30fps, device pixel ratio at 1.5, and its buffer at approximately two million pixels. It stops for reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers, and cleans up its GPU resources on unmount. A static fallback preserves the content if WebGL is unavailable.

### Accessibility

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Keep important content in children and provide a pause control for continuous animation. Reduced motion renders a static frame; unsupported WebGL retains the styled container and content.

# FloatingLines

> Animations/Backgrounds/FloatingLines · animations · `@gaudi/design-system/animations/FloatingLines`

Three layered families of glowing lines cross the surface and bend around the pointer.

## Import

```js
import FloatingLines from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/FloatingLines';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations';
```

Exports: `FloatingLines`, `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `paused` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Freeze the current frame. Reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen surfaces also stop motion. |
| `speed` | `number` | `1` | no | Motion multiplier, clamped to 0–5. Zero keeps the current frame still. |
| `intensity` | `number` | `1` | no | Strength of the effect, clamped to 0–2. Zero shows only the background color. |
| `scale` | `number` | `1` | no | Scale changes the sweep of the curves and the pointer lens. Clamped to 0.25–4. |
| `colors` | `string[]` | `Gaudi chart colors 1–3` | no | Up to three CSS colors, including CSS variables. Omitted colors use the current Gaudi palette. |
| `background` | `string` | `var(--ds-color-surface)` | no | Base CSS color beneath the effect. Follows the current theme by default. |
| `interactive` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Bend nearby line families around the pointer, with a smooth return on leave. No interaction is needed to use the content. |
| `height` | `number \| string` | `360` | no | Surface height in pixels or a CSS length. Numeric values are clamped to 1–4096. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Optional content rendered above the decorative canvas. Keep text and controls on a contrasting surface. |
| `className / style / ref` | `DOM props` | — | no | Applied to the outer div along with other DOM props and pointer handlers. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { FloatingLines } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/FloatingLines';

<FloatingLines height={360} paused />
```

## Accessibility

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; children remain accessible. Reduced motion shows a still frame, and unavailable graphics use a static color fallback. Provide a visible pause control when motion continues beside meaningful content. Keep text contrast independent of the moving artwork.

## Notes

- The playground layers a Gaudi header, hero and working documentation links above the effect. The Demo content switch hides only this foreground; canvas size, animation phase and pause state are retained.
- Eight curves in each family converge and separate at different angles and brightnesses. The local pointer lens relaxes smoothly after the pointer leaves.
- Visual idea inspired by Floating Lines from React Bits (MIT + Commons Clause). Independently implemented for Gaudi; no React Bits code or assets are included.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `animations-backgrounds-floating-lines--playground`)

## README

Broad, softly lit swells roll toward a hazy horizon, with atmospheric depth and subtle pointer parallax.

```jsx
import { GradientWaves } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/GradientWaves';

<GradientWaves height={360} speed={1} intensity={1} interactive />
```

The shader traces a continuous height field with broad foreground swells. Surface lighting and distance haze soften receding crests; pointer movement subtly shifts the viewpoint.

### Contract

- `paused=false` freezes the current frame when enabled. `speed=1` accepts 0–5; zero stops time.
- `intensity=1` accepts 0–2. `scale=1` accepts 0.25–4. Invalid numbers use safe defaults.
- `colors` optionally supplies up to three CSS colors; defaults come from the current Gaudi theme. `background` defaults to `var(--ds-color-surface)`.
- `interactive=false` enables pointer response when set. Content and controls retain their normal pointer behavior.
- `height=360` accepts pixels or a CSS length; numeric values are clamped to 1–4096. The canvas fills its container with a device pixel ratio capped at 1.5 and a drawing buffer of approximately two million pixels at most.
- `children`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and DOM attributes belong to the outer container. Children render above the canvas.

The shared renderer pauses for reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers, and releases its observers, animation frame and WebGL resources on unmount. Server output is deterministic. A static styled background remains available when WebGL fails.

### Accessibility

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Keep meaningful text and controls in semantic children. Provide a pause control for continuous motion and maintain text contrast when layering content over the effect.

# LiquidEther

| `intensity` | `number` | `1` | no | Effect strength, clamped to 0–2. Zero reveals the background color. |
| `scale` | `number` | `1` | no | Spatial scale of the effect, clamped to 0.25–4. |
| `colors` | `string[]` | `Gaudi theme tokens` | no | Up to three CSS colors. Omitted colors inherit the current Gaudi palette. |
| `background` | `string` | `var(--ds-color-surface)` | no | CSS color behind the effect and its static fallback. |


## Accessibility

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Keep important content in children and provide a pause control for continuous animation. Reduced motion renders a static frame; unsupported WebGL retains the styled container and content.

## Notes

- The playground layers a Gaudi header, hero and working documentation links above the effect. The Demo content switch hides only this foreground; canvas size, animation phase and pause state are retained.
- A bounded velocity and dye simulation retains, transports, and dissipates each plume. Pointer movement adds dye and momentum; an autonomous drifting source runs when the pointer is absent. Pausing and zero-delta redraws preserve the field, and a seeded plume provides a deterministic reduced-motion still.
- Visual idea inspired by Liquid Ether from React Bits (MIT + Commons Clause). Independently implemented for Gaudi; no React Bits source, shaders or assets are included.

- Playground (Storybook `animations-backgrounds-liquid-ether--playground`)

`core-pointer`

## README

Colored dye follows pointer movement, curls through a retained velocity field, and gradually dissipates.

```jsx
import { LiquidEther } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/LiquidEther';

<LiquidEther height={360} speed={1} intensity={1} interactive />
```

A bounded velocity and dye simulation retains, transports, and dissipates each plume. Pointer movement adds dye and momentum; an autonomous drifting source runs when the pointer is absent. Pausing and zero-delta redraws preserve the field, and a seeded plume provides a deterministic reduced-motion still.

### Contract

- `paused=false` freezes the current frame when enabled. `speed=1` accepts 0–5; zero stops time.
- `intensity=1` accepts 0–2. `scale=1` accepts 0.25–4. Invalid numbers use safe defaults.
- `colors` optionally supplies up to three CSS colors; defaults come from the current Gaudi theme. `background` defaults to `var(--ds-color-surface)`.
- `interactive=true` injects dye along pointer movement; set it to false for autonomous motion only. Content and controls retain their normal pointer behavior.
- `height=360` accepts pixels or a CSS length; numeric values are clamped to 1–4096. The canvas fills its container with a device pixel ratio capped at 1.5 and a drawing buffer of approximately two million pixels at most.
- `children`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and DOM attributes belong to the outer container. Children render above the canvas.

The shared renderer pauses for reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers, and releases its observers, animation frame and WebGL resources on unmount. Server output is deterministic. A static styled background remains available when WebGL fails.

### Accessibility

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Keep meaningful text and controls in semantic children. Provide a pause control for continuous motion and maintain text contrast when layering content over the effect.

- `scale` (number, default `1`): Spatial scale of the sea, clamped to 0.25–4.
- `colors` (string[], default `Gaudi theme tokens`): Up to three CSS colors for the points. Omitted colors inherit the current Gaudi palette.

- `interactive` (boolean, default `false`): Lift the sea under the pointer without capturing clicks or scrolling.
- `height` (number | string, default `360`): Container height in pixels or a CSS length. Numeric values are clamped to 1–4096; width fills the available container.

The shared renderer caps drawing at 30fps, device pixel ratio at 1.5, and its buffer at approximately two million pixels. It stops for reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers, and cleans up its GPU resources on unmount. A static fallback preserves the content if WebGL is unavailable.

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Keep important content in children and provide a pause control for continuous animation. Reduced motion renders a static frame; unsupported WebGL retains the styled container and content.

# PixelBlast

> Animations/Backgrounds/PixelBlast · animations · `@gaudi/design-system/animations/PixelBlast`

Separate square pixels form drifting dithered patterns; clicks send circular waves through the field.

## Import

```js
import PixelBlast from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/PixelBlast';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations';
```

Exports: `PixelBlast`, `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `paused` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Freeze the current frame. Reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen surfaces also stop motion. |
| `speed` | `number` | `1` | no | Motion multiplier, clamped to 0–5. Zero keeps the current frame still. |
| `intensity` | `number` | `1` | no | Strength of the effect, clamped to 0–2. Zero shows only the background color. |
| `scale` | `number` | `1` | no | Scale changes the square size and spacing in CSS pixels, independent of device pixel ratio. Clamped to 0.25–4. |
| `colors` | `string[]` | `Gaudi chart colors 1–3` | no | Up to three CSS colors, including CSS variables. Omitted colors use the current Gaudi palette. |
| `background` | `string` | `var(--ds-color-surface)` | no | Base CSS color beneath the effect. Follows the current theme by default. |
| `interactive` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Create an outward-decaying ripple at each click or tap. No interaction is needed to use the content. |
| `height` | `number \| string` | `360` | no | Surface height in pixels or a CSS length. Numeric values are clamped to 1–4096. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Optional content rendered above the decorative canvas. Keep text and controls on a contrasting surface. |
| `className / style / ref` | `DOM props` | — | no | Applied to the outer div along with other DOM props and pointer handlers. |

## Usage

```jsx

<PixelBlast height={360} paused />
```

## Accessibility

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; children remain accessible. Reduced motion shows a still frame, and unavailable graphics use a static color fallback. Provide a visible pause control when motion continues beside meaningful content. Keep text contrast independent of the moving artwork.

## Notes

- The playground layers a Gaudi header, hero and working documentation links above the effect. The Demo content switch hides only this foreground; canvas size, animation phase and pause state are retained.
- Squares keep the same size as density changes. A click creates an outward-moving wave that fades; paused and reduced-motion surfaces do not respond.
- Visual idea inspired by Pixel Blast from React Bits (MIT + Commons Clause). Independently implemented for Gaudi; no React Bits code or assets are included.

### Contract

- `paused=false` freezes the current frame when enabled. `speed=1` accepts 0–5; zero stops time.
- `intensity=1` accepts 0–2. `scale=1` accepts 0.25–4. Invalid numbers use safe defaults.
- `colors` optionally supplies up to three CSS colors; defaults come from the current Gaudi theme. `background` defaults to `var(--ds-color-surface)`.
- `interactive=false` enables pointer response when set. Content and controls retain their normal pointer behavior.
- `height=360` accepts pixels or a CSS length; numeric values are clamped to 1–4096. The canvas fills its container with a device pixel ratio capped at 1.5 and a drawing buffer of approximately two million pixels at most.
- `children`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and DOM attributes belong to the outer container. Children render above the canvas.

The shared renderer pauses for reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers, and releases its observers, animation frame and WebGL resources on unmount. Server output is deterministic. A static styled background remains available when WebGL fails.

### Accessibility

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Keep meaningful text and controls in semantic children. Provide a pause control for continuous motion and maintain text contrast when layering content over the effect.

### Visual reference

Inspired by the visual idea of [React Bits Web Threads](https://reactbits.dev/backgrounds/web-threads) (MIT + Commons Clause). This is an independent Gaudi implementation; no upstream component source, shader or asset is redistributed.

# GlyphInspector

> Animations/Text/GlyphInspector · animations · `@gaudi/design-system/animations/GlyphInspector`

Inspect animated letter outlines with a gliding frame, floating square particles, measurement guides and a live readout. Hover to take control; drag and release a letter to return it to its slot.

## Import

```js
import GlyphInspector from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/GlyphInspector';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations';
```

Exports: `GlyphInspector`, `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string` | `"Gaudi"` | no | Text to display. Keep it short enough for the chosen font size. |
| `autoplay` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Step the inspector through the letters while no letter is hovered or held. |
| `draggable` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Allow decorative letters to be lifted a short distance; release returns them to their slot. Does not change the text. |
| `readout` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Show the inspected character, its code point and its measured size (or drag offset) below the frame. |
| `guides` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Draw faint horizontal guides along the top and bottom of the inspected letter across the line. |
| `interval` | `number` | `900` | no | Milliseconds between automatic steps, clamped to 200–10000 before applying tempo. |
| `outline` | `dashed \| dotted \| solid` | `"dashed"` | no | Stroke style of the inspected letter outline. |
| `accent` | `string` | `"currentColor"` | no | Color of the frame, guides and readout. |
| `particles` | `number` | `12` | no | Number of drifting square particles around the frame, rounded and clamped to 0–40. Set 0 to hide them. |
| `tempo` | `number` | `1` | no | Speed multiplier for automatic inspection, outline tracing and particles, clamped to 0.25–3. |
| `reveal` | `letter \| area \| none` | `"letter"` | no | Outline the inspected letter, softly reveal nearby letter outlines around the pointer, or keep all letters filled. |
| `radius` | `number` | `120` | no | Area reveal radius in CSS pixels, clamped to 20–400. Only used with reveal="area". |
| `paused` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Stop motion and dragging while keeping the inspector visible at activeIndex, even with autoplay disabled. System reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers also stop motion. |
| `activeIndex` | `number` | `0` | no | Zero-based character index to inspect when paused. Counts Unicode code points, including spaces. Out-of-range, non-integer or non-finite values fall back to 0. Empty text shows no inspector. Ignored while running. |
| `className / style / ref` | `DOM props` | — | no | Applied to the outer span. Typography is inherited. |

## Variants

- `outline`: `dashed`, `dotted`, `solid`
- `reveal`: `letter`, `area`, `none`

## Usage

```jsx
import { GlyphInspector } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/GlyphInspector';

<GlyphInspector text="Gaudi" paused activeIndex={2} />
```

## Accessibility

The complete text is exposed once; decorative letters are hidden from assistive technology. Hover and drag do not change the text. Reduced motion removes animated inspection and dragging; an explicitly paused inspector remains visible without motion. Provide a pause control for continuous autoplay.

## Notes

- Visual idea inspired by Tech Text from React Bits (MIT + Commons Clause). Independently implemented for Gaudi; no React Bits code or assets are included.
- Typography is inherited and shrinks to fit the available width. The component reserves space for its particles, readout and bounded drag movement.

- Pointer exploration (Storybook `animations-text-glyphinspector--variant`)
- Area reveal (Storybook `animations-text-glyphinspector--area-reveal`)
- Paused at an index (Storybook `animations-text-glyphinspector--paused`)

# ReelText

> Animations/Text/ReelText · animations · `@gaudi/design-system/animations/ReelText`

A formatted value whose digits spin into place on slot-machine reels, landing left to right.

## Import

```js
import ReelText from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/ReelText';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations';
```

Exports: `ReelText`, `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string \| number` | `""` | no | The value to show, already formatted. Digits become reels; every other character stays fixed. |
| `duration` | `number` | `900` | no | Milliseconds the first reel takes to land, clamped to 0–4000. |
| `stagger` | `number` | `70` | no | Milliseconds between consecutive reels landing, left to right, clamped to 0–400. |
| `paused` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Swap values without motion. System reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers do the same. |
| `className / style / ref` | `DOM props` | — | no | Applied to the outer span. Typography is inherited. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { ReelText } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/ReelText';

<ReelText value="$31,904" />
```

## Accessibility

The root is one image named with the whole value; the reels are hidden, so the value is read once and never digit by digit. Reduced motion swaps values instantly.

## Notes

- Motion inspired by [Slot text](https://uiarc.dev/components/slot-text) from Arc. Independently implemented for Gaudi; no Arc code or assets are included.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `animations-text-reeltext--playground`)
- Changing value (Storybook `animations-text-reeltext--changing-value`)

## README

A formatted value whose digits spin into place on slot-machine reels. Use it for figures that change in place, such as a metric switching period; it is how `StatCard` animates its value with `valueMotion='reel'`.

```jsx
import { ReelText } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/ReelText';

<ReelText value='$31,904' />
```

Pass the value already formatted. Each digit is a 0–9 reel that rolls to its digit with a fast start and a soft landing (`--ds-motion-ease-out`); reels land left to right, `stagger` milliseconds apart, the first after `duration`. Separators, currency signs and letters stay fixed, and characters are matched from the end, so `999` → `1,000` spins only digits. The first paint rolls up from zero.

The root is one image with the whole value as its accessible name; the reels are hidden from assistive technology. Reduced motion, `paused`, hidden tabs and offscreen containers swap the value without motion.

Motion inspired by Arc's Slot text.

# WarpText

> Animations/Text/WarpText · animations · `@gaudi/design-system/animations/WarpText`

Text gently undulates at rest and bends beneath a moving pointer lens. Hover magnifies a local area, adds a soft ripple and optional RGB refraction, then eases back on exit.

## Import

```js
import WarpText from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/WarpText';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations';
```

Exports: `WarpText`, `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string` | `"Bend the moment"` | no | Text to render; newline characters create multiple centered lines. |
| `warpStrength` | `number` | `0.08` | no | Ambient distortion, clamped to 0–0.25. Set 0 for hover-only warping. |
| `warpScale` | `number` | `1.7` | no | Size of the ambient distortion field, clamped to 0.5–5. |
| `speed` | `number` | `0.55` | no | Ambient and ripple speed, clamped to 0–3. Zero holds the field still; pointer interaction remains available. |
| `pointerRadius` | `number` | `0.42` | no | Lens radius as a fraction of the container height, clamped to 0.1–1. |
| `pointerStrength` | `number` | `0.38` | no | Pointer-driven bending and magnification, clamped to 0–1. Zero disables the lens. |
| `refraction` | `number` | `0.018` | no | RGB edge separation, clamped to 0–0.06. Set 0 for a clean lens. Most visible on light text against a dark surface. |
| `ripple` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Add a soft radial ripple inside the pointer lens. |
| `paused` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Render undistorted text and stop pointer effects and frame updates. Also respects reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers. |
| `className / style / ref` | `DOM props` | — | no | Applied to the root. Typography and color are inherited; text shrinks to fit. Set height through style or className. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { WarpText } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/WarpText';

<div style={{ fontSize: 96, fontWeight: 700 }}>
  <WarpText text="Bend the moment" />
</div>
```

## Accessibility

The full text is exposed once. The canvas is decorative and does not change the accessible text. Paused and reduced-motion states are undistorted. Touch does not latch hover, and no extra keyboard stop is added for a decorative effect. Provide a pause control for continuous motion.

## Notes

- Typography and color come from the host. The text texture fits its container and refreshes when fonts or themes change.
- WebGL unavailable or lost: the readable HTML text remains visible. Forced colors uses the HTML fallback.
- Visual behavior inspired by Warp Text from React Bits. Independently implemented for Gaudi; no upstream source or assets are included.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `animations-text-warptext--playground`)
- Hover lens (Storybook `animations-text-warptext--hover-only`)
- Multiline refraction (Storybook `animations-text-warptext--multiline`)

The complete text is exposed once; decorative words are hidden from assistive technology. Reduced motion removes blur and corner marks. Pausing stops automatic changes while retaining the current visual focus. Provide a pause control for continuous cycling.

## Notes

- Visual idea inspired by [True Focus](https://reactbits.dev/text-animations/true-focus) from [React Bits](https://reactbits.dev) (MIT + Commons Clause). Independently implemented for Gaudi; no React Bits code or assets are included.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `animations-text-wordspotlight--playground`)
- Gentle focus (Storybook `animations-text-wordspotlight--variant`)

## README

A moving set of corner marks brings one word into focus while the surrounding words soften.

```jsx
import { WordSpotlight } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/WordSpotlight';

<WordSpotlight text="Gaudi" />
```

- `text` (string, default "Focus on what matters"): Words to display. Whitespace separates words, which wrap within the container.
- `interval` (number, default 1800): Milliseconds between automatic word changes, clamped to 400–30000. Hover holds the selected word.
- `blur` (number, default 4): Blur radius of unfocused words in pixels, 0–10. Reduced motion renders all words clearly.
- `paused` (boolean, default false): Stop automatic word changes; hover can still select a word. Reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers also stop automatic changes.
- `className / style / ref` (DOM props, default —): Applied to the outer span. Typography is inherited.

The complete text is exposed once; decorative words are hidden from assistive technology. Reduced motion removes blur and corner marks. Pausing stops automatic changes while retaining the current visual focus. Provide a pause control for continuous cycling.

Visual idea inspired by [True Focus](https://reactbits.dev/text-animations/true-focus) from [React Bits](https://reactbits.dev) (MIT + Commons Clause). Independently implemented for Gaudi; no React Bits code or assets are included.

# Chart

> MDX/Chart · mdx · `@gaudi/design-system/mdx/Chart`

Chart is the MDX adapter for the Charts collection: authors write <Chart type=…> (or a chart by name) in an article and get the same framed, accessible chart an application renders from @gaudi/design-system/charts.

In MDX, use Chart with type, or any chart by name from the MDX component map; the blog loads it with dynamic(() => import('@gaudi/design-system/mdx/Chart')). In application code import the charts from @gaudi/design-system/charts. Each chart type has its own page under Charts with detailed examples; this page shows how a chart reads inside an article.

## Import

```js
import Chart from '@gaudi/design-system/mdx/Chart';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/mdx';
```

Exports: `CHART_TYPES`, `Chart`, `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `bar \| line \| area \| composed \| pie \| donut \| scatter \| bubble \| radar \| radial \| sparkline \| range \| waterfall \| bar-list \| funnel \| sankey \| treemap \| box-plot \| histogram \| gauge \| heatmap` | `bar` | no | Picks the chart from the Charts collection; every other prop goes to that chart. |
| `data` | `Array<Record<string, unknown>> \| number[]` | `[]` | no | Records for the chart; the data shape follows the type (series, slices, steps, cells, groups). |
| `xKey` | `string` | `label` | no | Category field and value fields for series charts; composed series take type and axis. |
| `yKey` | `string` | `value` | no | Category field and value fields for series charts; composed series take type and axis. |
| `series` | `Array<{ key, label, type?, axis?, dashed? }>` | — | no | Category field and value fields for series charts; composed series take type and axis. |
| `title / description` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Figure caption. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `title or Chart` | no | Accessible name of the plot. |
| `height` | `number \| auto` | `320 (type-specific)` | no | Plot height; list-shaped charts default to auto. |
| `state` | `loading \| error \| empty \| invalid` | `from data` | no | Force a state; otherwise empty and invalid are detected from the data. |
| `labels` | `Partial<typeof DEFAULT_CHART_LABELS>` | `English copy` | no | Copy for states, the keyboard hint, the data table and its toggle. |
| `locale` | `string` | `runtime` | no | Number formatting for axes, tooltips, the readout and the table. |
| `formatValue` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions \| (value) => string` | `default number` | no | Number formatting for axes, tooltips, the readout and the table. |
| `showData` | `hidden \| toggle \| visible` | `hidden` | no | Data table visibility; hidden keeps it available to assistive technology. |
| `onActivate` | `(point, index) => void` | — | no | Click, Enter or Space on a point; the active point changed. |
| `onActiveChange` | `(index \| null) => void` | — | no | Click, Enter or Space on a point; the active point changed. |
| `references` | `Array<{ x?, y?, label, tone? }>` | — | no | Labelled guide lines and point notes on category and scatter charts. |
| `annotations` | `Array<{ x, y, label, tone? }>` | — | no | Labelled guide lines and point notes on category and scatter charts. |
| `stacked / showGrid / showLegend / showTooltip` | `boolean` | `false / true / false / true` | no | Series chart presentation. |
| `selectedIndex` | `number \| null` | — | no | Donut selection; the centre summary shows the selected slice. |
| `defaultSelectedIndex` | `number \| null` | `null` | no | Donut selection; the centre summary shows the selected slice. |
| `onSelect` | `(slice, index) => void` | — | no | Donut selection; the centre summary shows the selected slice. |
| `otherThreshold` | `number` | — | no | Fold small slices into Other; the donut centre caption. |
| `maxSlices` | `number` | — | no | Fold small slices into Other; the donut centre caption. |
| `centerLabel` | `string` | `Total` | no | Fold small slices into Other; the donut centre caption. |
| `toolbar` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Controls beside the caption; the figure border and padding. |
| `framed` | `boolean` | `true (false for Sparkline)` | no | Controls beside the caption; the figure border and padding. |
| `colors` | `string[]` | `Gaudi categorical palette` | no | Override the series or slice colours. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Root figure class override. |

## Variants

- `type`: `bar`, `line`, `area`, `composed`, `pie`, `donut`, `scatter`, `bubble`, `radar`, `radial`, `sparkline`, `range`, `waterfall`, `bar-list`, `funnel`, `sankey`, `treemap`, `box-plot`, `histogram`, `gauge`, `heatmap`
- `state`: `loading`, `error`, `empty`, `invalid`
- `showData`: `hidden`, `toggle`, `visible`

## Usage

```jsx
<Chart
  type='line'
  title='Readers by channel'
  ariaLabel='Monthly readers by channel'
  data={[
    { label: 'Jan', search: 1840 },
    { label: 'Feb', search: 2110 }
  ]}
  yKey='search'
/>

<DonutChart title='Essays by topic' data={[{ label: 'Data', value: 42 }, { label: 'Engineering', value: 28 }]} />
```

## Accessibility

Every chart is a captioned figure whose plot is one tab stop with a name and the role description "chart". The arrow keys walk the points (Up and Down move between rows on a heatmap), Home and End jump to the ends, Enter or Space activates the point, and Escape clears it; the active point is drawn on the chart and read out in a polite live region. Every value is also in a data table, hidden by default and shown with showData. Loading sets aria-busy, invalid and error states are alerts, and the SVG itself is hidden from assistive technology because the table carries the same data.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `mdx-chart--playground`)
- Writing a chart in MDX (Storybook `mdx-chart--in-mdx`)

## README

The MDX adapter for the Charts collection. Authors write `<Chart type=… />` in an article, or any chart by name from the MDX component map, and get the same framed, accessible chart an application renders from `@gaudi/design-system/charts`.

[Open the docs](http://localhost:6007/?path=/docs/mdx-chart--docs) for the Playground and an article that renders a chart inside its prose.

### In an article

```mdx
Search still brings in most readers, and the newsletter has grown every month.

<Chart
  type='line'
  title='Readers by channel'
  ariaLabel='Monthly readers by channel'
  data={[{ label: 'Jan', search: 1840 }, { label: 'Feb', search: 2110 }]}
  yKey='search'
/>

<DonutChart title='Essays by topic' data={[{ label: 'Data', value: 42 }, { label: 'Engineering', value: 28 }]} />
```

The blog loads the adapter on demand with `dynamic(() => import('@gaudi/design-system/mdx/Chart'))`; `MDXComponents` from `@gaudi/design-system/mdx` also maps every chart by name.

### Types

`type` picks the chart; every other prop goes to it. Each type has its own page under **Charts** with detailed examples.

| `type` | Chart |
| --- | --- |
| `bar`, `line`, `area`, `composed`, `range`, `sparkline` | BarChart, LineChart, AreaChart, ComposedChart, RangeChart, Sparkline |
| `waterfall`, `funnel`, `sankey` | WaterfallChart, FunnelChart, SankeyChart |
| `pie`, `donut`, `bar-list`, `treemap` | PieChart, DonutChart, StackedBarList, TreemapChart |
| `histogram`, `box-plot`, `scatter`, `bubble` | HistogramChart, BoxPlotChart, ScatterChart, BubbleChart |
| `gauge`, `radial`, `radar`, `heatmap` | GaugeChart, RadialBarChart, RadarChart, HeatmapChart |

Keyboard reading, the data table, the loading, empty, invalid and error states, and locale formatting come from the chart's frame; see `Charts/ChartFrame`.

# Citation

> MDX/Citation · mdx · `@gaudi/design-system/mdx/CitationPopover`

Citation documents the blog citation authoring flow and the Gaudi runtime components that hydrate generated citation links.

Use citations in three places. Authors put BibTeX files in the blog, list those files in post frontmatter, and cite keys directly in prose with Pandoc-style brackets. The blog MDX pipeline runs rehypeSimpleCitations, which converts those text markers into numbered anchors plus a generated References section. Gaudi does not parse BibTeX or rewrite MDX; it only provides the runtime CitationPopover and CitationTracker behavior for the generated markup.

## Import

```js
import Citation from '@gaudi/design-system/mdx/CitationPopover';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/mdx';
```

Exports: `default`

## Authoring Example

```jsx
---
title: 'An Introduction to Knowledge Graphs'
bibliography: ['meta/bibliography/references.bib', 'meta/bibliography/kg.bib']
---

A heterogeneous graph [@HusseinYC18; @WangJSWYCY19; @YangXJWHW20] assigns types to nodes and edges.

The same source can be cited again later [@HusseinYC18].

<!-- Do not hand-write citation anchors, popover data attributes, or references markup. -->
```

## Accessibility

Generated citation links are real anchors with readable labels. Popovers open on hover or focus, grouped references remain individually reachable, and CitationTracker keeps bibliography back-links pointed at the most recent citation instance.

## Notes

- The authoring API is markdown citation syntax, not a React component API.
- `rehypeSimpleCitations` is the blog rehype plugin. It loads BibTeX through `citation-js`, assigns first-use numbers, supports grouped citations, emits citation anchors, and appends the References list.
- `CitationPopover` binds to generated anchors marked with `data-citation-popover` and reads the generated citation keys, numbers, and reference text from data attributes.
- `CitationTracker` updates bibliography back-links so a reference points back to the most recent citation instance the reader used.

## Do

- Add BibTeX files to `data/meta/bibliography` in the blog repo.
- List the BibTeX files in post frontmatter with `bibliography: ['meta/bibliography/references.bib', 'meta/bibliography/kg.bib']`.
- Cite one source with `[@HusseinYC18]` and grouped sources with `[@HusseinYC18; @WangJSWYCY19; @YangXJWHW20]`.
- Let `rehypeSimpleCitations` generate numbered anchors, popover data attributes, and the References section.
- Use `CitationPopover` and `CitationTracker` only as runtime hydration for the generated citation markup.

## Don’t

- Do not hand-write `<sup>`, `citation-link` classes, `data-citation-*` attributes, or References markup in MDX.
- Do not import `CitationPopover` or `CitationTracker` inside individual MDX posts.
- Do not use `CitationPopover` as a manual popover for arbitrary text; it expects generated citation anchors.

## Consumer responsibilities

- Keep BibTeX source files in the blog, usually under `data/meta/bibliography`. They do not belong in the design-system package.
- Register `rehypeSimpleCitations` in the blog MDX/content pipeline so citation text is transformed before React renders the article.
- Mount `CitationTracker` once in the app layout and mount `CitationPopover` near the rendered article content.
- Keep citation keys in MDX prose exactly matched to the BibTeX ids in the bibliography files.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `mdx-citation--playground`)

## Related

`mdx-citationtracker`

# Footnote

> MDX/Footnote · mdx · `@gaudi/design-system/mdx/Footnote`

Footnote hydrates generated markdown footnote references with hover and focus popover previews.

Authors do not write a React component for each footnote. They write standard markdown footnote syntax in the post. The blog MDX pipeline extracts the definitions, enhances the generated footnote reference anchors with `data-footnote-*` attributes, and may visually collapse the bottom notes section. Gaudi only owns the small client runtime that reads those generated attributes and shows the preview popover on hover or keyboard focus.

## Import

```js
import Footnote from '@gaudi/design-system/mdx/Footnote';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/mdx';
```

Exports: `default`

## Authoring Example

```jsx
Inline prose can use a normal markdown footnote reference.[^model-note]

[^model-note]: This explanatory note can include links, emphasis, and short supporting context.

<!-- Runtime wiring lives outside the post:
app layout/page shell: <MDXLayoutRenderer ... />
article runtime: <Footnote />
-->

<!-- The blog pipeline generates anchors with data-footnote-popover, data-footnote-number, and data-footnote-content. -->
```

## Accessibility

Generated footnote references are real anchors, so readers can still jump to the notes list. `Footnote` adds hover and focus previews without replacing the underlying link or removing the accessible footnote relationship.

## Notes

- `Footnote` listens for `mouseenter`, `mouseleave`, `focusin`, and `focusout` on generated links marked with `data-footnote-popover="true"`.
- The popover body is read from generated `data-footnote-content`, so the plugin must sanitize and serialize the note content before runtime.
- The component positions the popover next to the reference and flips left when it would overflow the viewport.
- The visible footnotes list remains the source of truth; the popover is a reading convenience.

## Do

- Write standard markdown footnotes with `[^id]` references and `[^id]: note text` definitions.
- Let `remarkFootnoteData` extract note content and let `rehypeFootnotePopoverV2` attach popover data to generated reference links.
- Use `Footnote` as a page-level runtime binder after the article has rendered.
- Keep footnote copy short enough for a compact popover; long supporting material belongs in the visible footnotes section.

## Don’t

- Do not hand-write `data-footnote-*` attributes in article MDX.
- Do not use `<Footnote />` as an inline MDX component or wrapper around footnote text.
- Do not hide the underlying footnote references without preserving anchor navigation and focus behavior.

## Consumer responsibilities

- Enable markdown footnotes in the blog MDX pipeline with `remarkGfm`.
- Run `remarkFootnoteData` before rehype so footnote definitions are available on `file.data.footnotes`.
- Run `rehypeFootnotePopoverV2` after footnotes are converted to HTML so reference anchors receive `data-footnote-popover`, `data-footnote-number`, and `data-footnote-content`.
- Mount `Footnote` once near the rendered MDX article, not inside the MDX document itself.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `mdx-footnote--playground`)

# Preview

> MDX/Preview · mdx · `@gaudi/design-system/mdx/Preview`

Preview renders inline link previews for markdown links transformed by the blog MDX pipeline. It is the MDX adapter over the Core LinkPreview, which owns the rich, type-aware rendering.

Authors should usually write normal markdown links. During compilation, the blog turns eligible external markdown links into `Preview` components with `remarkLinks`, then turns eligible internal blog anchors into `Preview internal` components with `rehypeInternalLinks`. Gaudi owns the rendered inline link, fallback state, loading skeleton, and hover card UI; the blog owns the markdown transforms and preview API.

## Import

```js
import Preview from '@gaudi/design-system/mdx/Preview';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/mdx';
```

Exports: `PreviewLoadingSkeleton`, `default`, `usePreviewData`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | `string` | — | no | Target URL to link to and preview. |
| `title` | `string` | — | no | Optional custom title that overrides fetched preview metadata. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Root class override. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Starts the hover card open for deterministic demos and visual tests. |
| `internal` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Renders a local app link and skips remote preview fetching. |
| `previewData` | `object` | `null` | no | Preloaded metadata for deterministic docs, tests, or server-provided previews. |
| `showImage` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Controls whether the hover card can show image preview metadata. |
| `timeout` | `number` | `10000` | no | Preview metadata request timeout in milliseconds. |
| `onLoad` | `(data) => void` | — | no | Called when preview metadata loads successfully. |
| `onError` | `(error) => void` | — | no | Called when preview metadata fails to load. |
| `fallback` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Custom fallback UI for unavailable preview metadata. |
| `variant` | `inline \| card \| compact` | `inline` | no | LinkPreview presentation, for React pages that want a card or a row. |
| `endpoint` | `string \| (url) => string \| null` | `SiteConfig preview.endpoint` | no | App-owned preview endpoint; with none configured nothing is fetched. |
| `resolveImage` | `(link) => string \| null \| template map` | `SiteConfig preview.resolveImage` | no | Image for links whose metadata has none (thumbnails, screenshots); Gaudi ships no image services. |

## Variants

- `variant`: `inline`, `card`, `compact`

## Authoring Example

```jsx
[assaf.website](https://assaf.website)

[Unavailable link](https://this-link-will-not-work.invalid)

[Internal blog link](/blog/engineering/gaudi-my-bash-framework)

<!-- Generated by the blog pipeline:
<Preview url='https://assaf.website' title='assaf.website' />
<Preview url='https://this-link-will-not-work.invalid' title='Unavailable link' />
<Preview internal url='/blog/engineering/gaudi-my-bash-framework' title='Internal blog link' />
-->

<!-- Direct component usage is reserved for React pages and deterministic Storybook examples. -->
```

## Accessibility

Preview renders a real link with a readable label. The hover card is supplemental; the target URL remains reachable without JavaScript, images, or preview metadata.

## Notes

- `remarkLinks` converts external `http` and `https` markdown links into `Preview` MDX text elements with `url` and optional `title` attributes.
- `rehypeInternalLinks` converts matching internal blog anchors like `/blog/category/slug` into `Preview internal` elements after markdown has become HAST.
- External previews call the configured endpoint; without one nothing is fetched. Unavailable URLs render a red fallback link instead of breaking article content.
- Internal previews skip remote fetching and can use local metadata supplied by the app or generated pipeline.
- What each link shows (repository stars and language, video channel and duration, article author and date, post author and counts, Wikipedia excerpts) is decided by `normalizeLinkPreview` in Core/LinkPreview; the adapter only keeps the pipeline props. Images the payload lacks come from the app's `resolveImage`.
- The endpoint resolves from the `endpoint` prop, then `SiteConfigProvider preview={{ endpoint }}`; with neither, links render from `previewData` or as plain links without fetching.

## Do

- Write normal markdown links such as `[assaf.website](https://assaf.website)` in MDX posts.
- Use direct `<Preview />` only in React pages, custom layouts, or deterministic docs examples with `previewData`.
- Use `internal` for local blog links that should render internal metadata without remote preview fetching.
- Provide `title` when the source text is not enough or when deterministic rendering matters.

## Don’t

- Do not rewrite ordinary article links by hand when markdown syntax can express the link.
- Do not rely on the hover card as the only place a title or destination appears.
- Do not fetch external preview metadata inside the design-system package; the consuming app owns the API route.

## Consumer responsibilities

- Register `remarkLinks` in the blog remark pipeline so external markdown links become `Preview` MDX elements.
- Register `rehypeInternalLinks` in the blog rehype pipeline so internal blog anchors become `Preview internal` elements after markdown has become HTML.
- Expose a preview route (the blog uses `/api/preview`) for external metadata fetching, caching, and failure handling, and configure it with `SiteConfigProvider preview={{ endpoint }}` (or `LayoutContainer preview`). There is no default endpoint.
- Configure `preview.resolveImage` (a function or a template map) for derived images such as video thumbnails, repository cards or page screenshots; Gaudi ships no image services.
- Keep `Preview` in the `MDXComponents` map so generated MDX JSX can resolve at render time.

## States and recovery

- Preserve the original destination link while preview metadata loads or fails, so navigation never depends on the enrichment API.
- Name the unavailable preview and keep the supplied title visible; a failed hover card must not become an empty interaction.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `mdx-preview--playground`)
- States (Storybook `mdx-preview--states`)

## Related

`core-linkpreview`, `mdx-image`

## README

The `<Preview>` element the blog's markdown pipeline generates for links (`remarkLinks` for external links, `rehypeInternalLinks` for internal ones). It is a thin adapter over the Core [LinkPreview](../../core/LinkPreview/README.md): rendering, kinds and the normaliser live there.

```jsx
import { Preview } from '@gaudi/design-system/mdx';

<Preview url='https://assaf.website' title='assaf.website' previewData={payload} />
```

Props: `url`, `title`, `internal`, `previewData`, `showImage`, `defaultOpen`, `timeout`, `variant`, `orientation`, `endpoint`, `resolveImage`, `onLoad`, `onError`, `fallback`, `className`.

### No built-in network access

Gaudi loads nothing on its own. The adapter fetches metadata only from an endpoint the app configures, and shows images only from the payload or the app's `resolveImage`. Without either, links render from `previewData` or as plain links. Stories pass static `previewData`.

### What the blog must add (2026-10-02)

The blog relied on two defaults that were removed: the implicit `/api/preview` endpoint and the Microlink screenshot fallback for pages without an Open Graph image (plus the YouTube thumbnail and GitHub Open Graph card derived from the URL). Pass them once through the layout (or `SiteConfigProvider`):

```jsx
// Plain data, so it can be passed from the server LayoutContainer.
const preview = {
  endpoint: '/api/preview',
  resolveImage: {
    video: 'https://img.youtube.com/vi/{videoId}/maxresdefault.jpg',
    repository: 'https://opengraph.githubassets.com/1/{owner}/{repo}',
    wikipedia: null, // Wikipedia shows its excerpt instead
    default: 'https://api.microlink.io/?url={url}&screenshot=true&meta=false&embed=screenshot.url'
  }
};

<LayoutContainer preview={preview} …>   // or <SiteConfigProvider preview={preview}>
```

`resolveImage` may also be a function `({ kind, url, host, data, videoId, repository }) => string | null`, but a function cannot cross from a server component to the client provider, so the template map is the simplest fit for the blog's server `LayoutContainer`. See the [LinkPreview images notes](../../core/LinkPreview/README.md#images).

- Leaderboard — registry item `@gaudi/table-leaderboard` (uses `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarRoot`, `Badge`, `RegistryIcon`, `TableBodyPrimitive`, `TableCellPrimitive`, `TableHeadPrimitive`, `TableHeader`, `TableRoot`, `TableRowPrimitive`)
- Records with avatars, status and actions — registry item `@gaudi/table-records` (uses `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarRoot`, `Badge`, `Button`, `DropdownMenuContent`, `DropdownMenuItemPrimitive`, `DropdownMenuRoot`, `DropdownMenuSeparatorPrimitive`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`, `RegistryIcon`, `TableBodyPrimitive`, `TableCellPrimitive`, `TableHeadPrimitive`, `TableHeader`, `TableRoot`, `TableRowPrimitive`)
- Projects with team avatars — registry item `@gaudi/table-team-projects` (uses `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarGroup`, `AvatarGroupCount`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarRoot`, `Badge`, `RegistryIcon`, `TableBodyPrimitive`, `TableCellPrimitive`, `TableHeadPrimitive`, `TableHeader`, `TableRoot`, `TableRowPrimitive`)
- Vertical details — registry item `@gaudi/table-vertical-details` (uses `Badge`, `Frame`, `FrameDescription`, `FrameHeader`, `FramePanel`, `FrameTitle`, `Pill`, `ProgressRoot`, `TableBodyPrimitive`, `TableCellPrimitive`, `TableRoot`, `TableRowPrimitive`)

## README

This Gaudi owner includes **table**, with shared primitives and article framing.

Import the documented composition from `@gaudi/design-system/mdx/Table`. Existing convenience names are preserved; compound roots use explicit aliases where needed.

[Open the first example](http://localhost:6007/?path=/story/mdx-table--basic) for the complete JSX and public imports. The Storybook catalogue lists every variant and use case under this owner.

Provide visible labels for controls, preserve heading order, and connect controlled values to application state. The examples exercise keyboard and accessibility behavior; application networking and persistence remain consumer responsibilities.

See [reconciliation and compatibility details](../../../../README.md#component-catalogue) and [source notices](../../../../README.md#third-party-notices).

### Shared headers and density

`TableRoot` is the unframed primitive; the default `Table` adds article scrolling, sticky columns and framing. Both accept `density='compact' | 'normal' | 'comfortable'` (default `normal`). Density changes spacing only. `TableHeadPrimitive` (or article `TableHeaderCell`) preserves label casing and uses the same 14px, medium-weight style as DataTable and DataGrid. Its `variant='muted'` default uses the muted surface; `'plain'` uses the surface colour.

Use the supplied row and cell parts, including in MDX mappings. `TableRoot` accepts `containerProps` for the scrolling wrapper, such as `role`, `tabIndex`, and `aria-label`. `TableCellPrimitive as='th' scope='row'` creates a body row header without applying column-header styling. The Header consistency story compares all four implementations and checks their computed styles and sorting.

# Post lists

> Blocks/Blog/Post lists · post · `@gaudi/design-system/post/Post`

Blog-post sections using the same Post summaries and article data as the blog pages. Image cards, featured articles, horizontal rows, and compact archives reuse one component.

## Import

```js
import Postlists from '@gaudi/design-system/post/Post';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/post';
```

Exports: `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `frontMatter` | `Article metadata` | `{}` | no | Title, prepared href, date, subtitle and category { id, label, href }. String categories remain unlinked labels; absent hrefs never create a route. |
| `layout` | `list \| stacked \| horizontal` | `list` | no | Post presentation. Horizontal media stacks in narrow containers. |
| `media` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Optional image or media before the summary. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Optional byline and reading-time composition. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Classes on the list item. |
| `locale` | `string` | — | no | Date formatting locale. |
| `titleVariant` | `string` | `index-list-title` | no | Shared Typography variant; use heading-md for a featured article. |
| `titleAs` | `ElementType` | `h3` | no | Heading element appropriate to the surrounding list. |

## Variants

- `layout`: `list`, `stacked`, `horizontal`

## Usage

```jsx
import { Post } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<ul>
  <Post frontMatter={frontMatter} />
</ul>
```

## Accessibility

Use a meaningful linked title and an appropriate heading level. Content and routing remain application-owned.

## Examples

- Post metadata (Storybook `post-post--playground`)
- Image cards (Storybook `post-post--image-cards`)
- Featured and recent (Storybook `post-post--featured`)
- Horizontal rows (Storybook `post-post--horizontal`)
- Compact list (Storybook `post-post--compact`)

## Related

`mdx-image`

## README

A semantic list entry for the blog. Storybook's **Blocks → Blog → Post lists** shows image cards, featured and recent articles, horizontal rows, and a compact archive using the same component and article data as the blog pages.

```jsx
import Post from '@gaudi/design-system/post/Post';
import { PostReadingTime } from '@gaudi/design-system/post/PostHeader';

<ul>
  <Post
    frontMatter={article}
    layout='stacked'
    media={<img src='/cover.jpg' alt='' />}
    footer={<PostReadingTime readingTime='8 min read' />}
  />
</ul>
```

`frontMatter` contains the supplied `title`, `href`, `date`, `subtitle`, `draft`, and `category` (`{ label, href }` or an unlinked string). `locale` controls date formatting; `titleAs` defaults to `h3`; `titleVariant` defaults to `index-list-title` and accepts a shared Typography variant. Applications prepare routes and content. `Post` does not infer a destination or estimate reading time.

`layout` defaults to `list`, preserving the existing text index. `stacked` puts optional media above the summary. `horizontal` puts media beside the text when the list item is at least 36rem wide and stacks it below that width. `media` and `footer` accept composed content; `className` and standard list-item props pass to the outer `li`.

Place entries inside a list. Use a heading level appropriate to the surrounding section and keep the title link descriptive. Cover artwork that repeats the title's purpose can use empty alt text; meaningful illustrations need a useful description. Keep unrelated buttons and category links outside the title link. Layouts in the examples use shared styles and do not duplicate post metadata rendering.

| `classNames` | `Record<string, string>` | `{}` | no | Slot classes. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Usage

```jsx
import { PostSeriesBox } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<PostSeriesBox series={seriesPosts} currentId='components' />
```

## Accessibility

Identify the current article and use descriptive links for other entries.

## Examples

# TableOfContents

> Blocks/Blog/TableOfContents · post · `@gaudi/design-system/post/TableOfContents`

Responsive article navigation with active sections, expandable heading branches, and an optional diagram and table index. Reuses Scrollspy, Collapsible, Link and the shared expansion hook.

## Import

```js
import TableOfContents from '@gaudi/design-system/post/TableOfContents';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/post';
```

Exports: `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `toc` | `Array<{ id, url?, value, depth?, children? }>` | `[]` | no | Prepared heading IDs and labels. Nest children to describe the hierarchy; top-level count controls initial expansion regardless of heading depth. |
| `contentRef` | `RefObject<HTMLElement>` | — | no | Article to index. Defaults to the first article on the page. |
| `targetRef` | `RefObject<HTMLElement>` | — | no | Document or nested scroll viewport used by shared Scrollspy. Omit for document scrolling. |
| `offset` | `number` | `24` | no | Space above the selected heading for sticky navigation or decorative edges. |
| `smooth` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Smooth section navigation; respects reduced motion. |
| `indexVisuals` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Index captioned diagrams and tables in the article. Image and video figures are excluded. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Root layout classes. Sticky placement and mobile disclosure belong to the surrounding layout. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | `Table of contents` | no | Accessible navigation name when several contents lists share a page. |

## Usage

```jsx
import TableOfContents from '@gaudi/design-system/post/TableOfContents';

<TableOfContents toc={toc} contentRef={articleRef} targetRef={readingViewportRef} offset={24} />
```

## Accessibility

Uses real links and marks the active heading with aria-current. Branch toggles have descriptive names and aria-expanded. Modified link clicks remain native; section navigation respects reduced motion and does not steal focus. Hidden branches keep their targets indexed and expand when a descendant becomes active.

## Examples

- Playground (Storybook `post-tableofcontents--playground`)
- Four or fewer sections (Storybook `post-tableofcontents--compact-toc`)

## Related

`core-scrollspy`, `core-link`, `blocks-blog-article`, `mdx-image`

## README

Use this block for article headings, nested sections, and optional captioned diagrams and tables. It shares Scrollspy tracking and navigation, Link behavior, Collapsible controls, ScrollArea containment, and the expansion hook with the rest of Gaudi.

```jsx
import TableOfContents from '@gaudi/design-system/post/TableOfContents';

<TableOfContents
  toc={toc}
  contentRef={articleRef}
  targetRef={readingViewportRef}
  offset={24}
/>
```

Prepare entries as `{ id, value, url?, depth?, children? }`. Nest `children` to describe expandable branches; flat lists still use `depth` for indentation. Four or fewer top-level entries expand initially, regardless of their heading depth. Larger lists follow the active branch; readers can toggle every branch independently. Closed branches retain their tracking targets and reveal an active descendant.

Omit `targetRef` for document scrolling. Pass the article's actual viewport ref for bounded reading layouts; use the same ref for ReadingIndicator and other Scrollspy navigation. `offset` accounts for sticky headers or decorative edges. `smooth` defaults to true and respects reduced motion. Scrollspy owns scroll listeners and active-section tracking; this block does not create separate heading observers.

`contentRef` scopes visual indexing to one article. Captioned diagrams and tables receive stable anchors; photo, video, and code figures are excluded. Set `indexVisuals={false}` to show only headings. Long labels wrap, and a shared ScrollArea contains longer lists.

The block is visible at every screen width. The surrounding ArticleContentLayout owns sticky placement and the mobile contents disclosure. Use `aria-label` to name navigation when several lists share a page. Real links preserve modified clicks; active links use `aria-current="location"`, and branch toggles expose `aria-expanded` without moving focus.

# Footers

> Blocks/Marketing/Footers · layout · `@gaudi/design-system/layout/Footer`

Site footer with host-supplied navigation, social links, copyright, and optional newsletter form.

## Import

```js
import Footers from '@gaudi/design-system/layout/Footer';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/layout';
```

Exports: `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `standard \| editorial \| centered \| compact` | `standard` | no | Link columns with a newsletter, blog branding, centered navigation, or compact inline navigation. |
| `sections` | `Array<{ title, links: Array<{ href, label }> }>` | `[]` | no | Navigation groups from the host. |
| `socialLinks` | `Array<{ kind, href }>` | `[]` | no | Social destinations; missing URLs are omitted. |
| `copyrightName` | `string \| { name?, author? }` | — | no | Host-owned attribution. |
| `brandTitle` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Host-supplied name or brand component. |
| `brandDescription` | `string` | — | no | Short description beneath the brand. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional classes on the footer landmark. |
| `newsletterProps` | `NewsletterForm props` | — | no | Explicit endpoint and subscription copy. |

## Variants

- `variant`: `standard`, `editorial`, `centered`, `compact`

## Usage

```jsx
import Footer from '@gaudi/design-system/layout/Footer';

<Footer sections={footerLinks} copyrightName='Example Studio' newsletterProps={{ endpoint: '/api/subscribe' }} />
```

## Accessibility

Retains the footer landmark and uniquely named navigation regions. Supply descriptive link labels and a configured newsletter endpoint before allowing subscription.

## Examples

- Blog with link columns (Storybook `layout-footer--blog`)
- With newsletter (Storybook `layout-footer--newsletter`)
- Centered (Storybook `layout-footer--centered`)
- Compact inline (Storybook `layout-footer--compact`)
- Newsletter unavailable (Storybook `layout-components--footer-layout`)
- Newsletter error (Storybook `layout-footer--submission-error`)

## Related

`core-link`, `blocks-navigation`

## README

One footer owner for blog and marketing pages. Import from `@gaudi/design-system/layout/Footer`.

- `standard` places navigation beside the shared `NewsletterForm`.
- `editorial` places a brand and social links beside grouped navigation.
- `centered` centers the brand, a flat list of links, social links, and copyright.
- `compact` puts the brand, flat navigation, and social links in a row when the container permits.

Supply `sections` as `{ title, links: [{ href, label }] }[]`, `socialLinks` as `{ kind, href }[]`, and `copyrightName` as a name or author object. Content and destinations belong to the host. Empty navigation and social groups are omitted. The simple variants flatten the supplied navigation groups.

`brandTitle` accepts a React node, including `GaudiBrand`; `brandDescription` supplies the supporting text. `className` and native footer attributes pass through to the landmark. Each instance generates a unique accessible heading.

`newsletterProps` goes to `NewsletterForm`. An endpoint is required to enable subscriptions; the examples use local sample responses and never subscribe an address. Custom form classes merge with the footer defaults.

The footer responds to its container, so it can be used in page layouts and inset regions. The host owns the outer width and horizontal gutters. Keep each page's footer outside its main landmark.

# Newsletter

> Blocks/Marketing/Newsletter · layout · `@gaudi/design-system/layout/NewsletterForm`

Newsletter sections built from one email subscription form, with an explicit host endpoint and local pending, success, and error feedback.

## Import

```js
import Newsletter from '@gaudi/design-system/layout/NewsletterForm';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/layout';
```

Exports: `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `endpoint` | `string` | — | no | Host endpoint that receives a POST; absent endpoints disable signup. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | `Subscribe to the newsletter` | no | Visible form heading. Pass null to omit it. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | `Get new articles and resources in your inbox.` | no | Supporting copy. Pass null to omit it. |
| `headingAs` | `string` | `h3` | no | Heading level in the host page. |
| `titleVariant` | `string` | — | no | Shared Typography variant; omitted preserves the compact form heading. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Supporting content below the form and feedback, such as a privacy note. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Root layout classes. |
| `classNames` | `{ root?, header?, body?, title?, description?, form?, input?, action?, button?, message? }` | `{}` | no | Part-specific classes. |

## Usage

```jsx
import NewsletterForm from '@gaudi/design-system/layout/NewsletterForm';

<NewsletterForm title='Monthly field notes' endpoint='/api/newsletter' />
```

## Accessibility

Uses EmailInput with single-address pattern validation and the default smooth caret. Names the email input, preserves the submitted address on failure, disables duplicate submissions, and announces feedback beside the field.

## Examples

- Form and availability (Storybook `layout-components--newsletter`)
- Centered (Storybook `layout-newsletter-form--playground`)
- Split (Storybook `layout-newsletter-form--split`)
- Image panel (Storybook `layout-newsletter-form--image-panel`)
- Compact (Storybook `layout-newsletter-form--compact`)
- Submission error (Storybook `layout-newsletter-form--submission-error`)

## README

One subscription form for footer embeds and **Blocks → Marketing → Newsletter** sections. The public import remains `@gaudi/design-system/layout/NewsletterForm`.

```jsx
import NewsletterForm from '@gaudi/design-system/layout/NewsletterForm';

<NewsletterForm
  endpoint='/api/newsletter'
  title='Notes worth sharing.'
  description='New writing and useful resources from our journal.'
  headingAs='h2'
  titleVariant='heading-xl'
>
  <p>Unsubscribe whenever you like.</p>
</NewsletterForm>
```

The host endpoint receives a POST with `{ email }`. A successful HTTP response without an `error` value confirms the subscription. Failed requests preserve the address for retry; pending and successful forms prevent duplicate submission. Endpoint changes and unmounts abort pending work. Without an endpoint, signup is disabled and an unavailable message is shown.

`title` and `description` accept content or `null`. `headingAs` defaults to `h3`; `titleVariant` optionally selects a shared Typography variant. Omit it to retain the compact heading used by existing embeds. `children` follows submission feedback. `classNames` accepts `root`, `header`, `body`, `title`, `description`, `form`, `input`, `action`, `button`, and `message`.

The EmailInput owns single-address validation and caret behavior. Feedback uses an alert for errors and a status for success. All examples share this implementation; section layout styles and local sample endpoints stay in the story fixtures. The response control switches between success, error, and unavailable and resets the example. Demo addresses are never sent to a subscription service.

# LayoutContainer

> Layout/LayoutContainer · layout · `@gaudi/design-system/layout/LayoutContainer`

Async server layout that composes theme context, navigation, a skip link, article content, footer, and host-provided structured data.

## Import

```js
import LayoutContainer from '@gaudi/design-system/layout/LayoutContainer';
// also: import { … } from '@gaudi/design-system/layout';
```

Exports: `default`

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | Page content inside the main landmark. |
| `background` | `ReactNode` | `Borealis` | no | Decorative full-width layer at the top of the page that scrolls with it and sets its own height (for example 100dvh for the whole window), such as an animated band; replaces the default Borealis. |
| `metadata / navigation / preview` | `SiteConfigProvider values` | `{} / — / —` | no | Host site, theme, navigation, and link-preview configuration. |
| `menuProps / footerProps` | `object` | — | no | Navigation and footer presentation props. |
| `jsonLd` | `object \| (() => object \| Promise<object>)` | — | no | Prepared JSON-LD or an async resolver; invalid values are omitted. |
| `analytics` | `ReactNode` | `null` | no | Explicit app-owned analytics element. |

## Usage

```jsx
import LayoutContainer from '@gaudi/design-system/layout/LayoutContainer';

export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
  return <LayoutContainer metadata={metadata} navigation={navigation} jsonLd={loadJsonLd}>
    {children}
  </LayoutContainer>;
}
```

## Accessibility

Keep the skip target and the single main landmark. Supply accessible navigation and footer content; analytics and JSON-LD must come from the host.

## Notes

- Import the async component directly from @gaudi/design-system/layout/LayoutContainer in a server component. Resolve request cookies in the host and pass metadata.theme; Gaudi does not read request cookies.

## Related

`blocks-navigation`
